Send → first token 13 findings · 4 high · 5 medium · 4 low

A cold Claude session needs 3.4–3.8 s to the first token (2.3 s of it is CLI boot with your setting sources). Title and branch generation spawn full-config CLIs (~1.3 GiB each) at the same moment, and the checkpoint baseline is 7× slower than necessary and races the agent.

How it works today (investigator's summary)

Pressing Send renders the user message optimistically and switches on a local 'working' state right away (apps/web/src/hooks/executeChatSendTurn.ts:376-429). Before the provider gets the prompt, a series of serial steps runs. On the client, a non-first Claude send first makes a getThreadWindow review RPC, and worktree mode first makes getConfig, getProjectPreferences and getSettings RPCs. Then the thread.turn.start dispatch goes out; in worktree mode the server first runs git fetch for every origin head, git worktree add, 4 more dispatches and a setup-terminal open inside that same RPC. Next the ProviderCommandReactor lane runs ensureSessionForThread, reconcileThreadGoal and buildSendTurnRequestForThread. These call ProviderService.listSessions twice, and listSessions is an N+1 scan over every persisted binding: 702 SQL statements, 36-41 ms each in the user's real trace. Then come startSession, forks of the title and branch-name CLIs, and the sendTurn fork. For Claude, sendTurn waits on a setPermissionMode control round trip, so the prompt is effectively released only when the CLI finishes booting. Boot takes 2.30-2.38 s with the user's setting sources (0.30 s without them), and first-token latency adds 1.1-1.5 s, for 3.4-3.8 s total on a cold session. A live session takes 1.0-1.45 s. Codex costs about 140 ms for spawn+initialize plus 110-825 ms for thread/start. Its first turn on a new thread then takes 3.0-3.8 s to the first delta, versus 1.5-1.75 s if thread/start ran at least 6 s earlier. Provider sessions are reaped after 5 minutes idle, so the 'existing live thread' case (a) often falls back to a cold resume.

In parallel, on the same Node event loop, the single global CheckpointReactor worker reloads the whole thread detail and runs listSessions 3 times per turn start: for the user message-sent event, for turn-start-requested, and for runtime turn.started. It also captures the first-turn baseline from a fresh temp index, so git add -A has to rehash every tracked file: 820 ms on a 6k-file/121 MiB scratch clone, and 1,360 ms of a 1,487 ms capture in the user's real trace. Seeding the temp index from the real index produces the same tree in 118 ms. sendTurn never waits for the baseline. That is a correctness race: the agent can change files before the baseline exists, and pre-warming sessions would make the race more likely. The first-turn title and branch generations each spawn a provider CLI with the full user config (MCP servers, plugins, tools, project docs). Each costs about 5 CPU-s and about 1.3 GiB of peak process-tree RSS (Claude titles also send about 86k input tokens), and they run at the same moment as the main session boot. That adds about 300 ms to first token on an 18-core M5 Max. The side-question flag set Ryco already has cuts this to about 0.8 CPU-s and 117-250 MiB.

The biggest user-visible wins are speculative session pre-warming with an idle TTL (saves 2.0-2.3 s for Claude, 1.5-2.2 s for Codex), light-mode or deferred title/branch generation, a seeded checkpoint index joined before sendTurn (fixes the race), and removing the listSessions N+1 and the redundant full-detail loads (about 230 ms plus 200-500 ms of main-thread work per turn for this user).

Part of Priority 8: New thread and the first turn

Expected gain

Per first turn: -4 CPU-s and -1.1 to -1.2 GiB transient RSS per generation (×2 in worktree mode); about -300 ms first-token contention measured on an 18-core machine (estimated larger on 8-core laptops); about -85k input tokens per Claude title; title appears 2-5 s sooner.

What happens today

On a first turn, prepareAndSubmitTurnStart forks maybeGenerateThreadTitleForFirstTurn and, in worktree mode, also maybeGenerateAndRenameWorktreeBranchForFirstTurn. Both are forked after ensureSessionForThread returns and before sendTurn. For Claude without Agent Control, that is while the main CLI is still booting. The default text-generation selection is Codex gpt-5.6-luna (settings.ts:660-668). Each call runs codex exec with the user's full config: MCP servers, plugins, hooks, AGENTS.md project docs, read-only shell. The ClaudeTextGeneration path runs claude -p --dangerously-skip-permissions with tools, all setting sources and no --no-session-persistence. The lightweight flag set is used only for answerSideQuestion (CodexTextGeneration.ts:177-205, ClaudeTextGeneration.ts:142-153). Measured per title (Ryco mode vs light flags): Codex 4.8-5.1 vs 0.8 CPU-s, 1,358 vs 117 MiB peak tree RSS, 11-16 vs 4-8 processes. Claude 5.1-5.4 vs 0.8 CPU-s, 1,331 vs 250 MiB, about 86k vs about 1k input tokens, 5.3-7.2 s (one 78-81 s outlier) vs 1.4-2.4 s. With 2 such CLIs running, Claude first token moved +313 ms (+9%) on an 18-core M5 Max. Titles retry 2x with exponential 2 s backoff, and CODEX_TIMEOUT_MS is 180 s, so the worst case holds about 1.3 GiB for up to about 9 minutes. Each Claude title also writes a persisted Claude Code session under ~/.claude/projects/<cwd>.

Proposal

1. (S) Treat generateThreadTitle and generateBranchName like answerSideQuestion. Codex: --ignore-user-config --ignore-rules, mcp_servers={}, project_doc_max_bytes=0, tool features off. Claude: --setting-sources '' --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}' --system-prompt <short> --tools '' --no-session-persistence. Extract a shared lightweightTextGenerationArgs(operation) helper instead of the answerSideQuestion special case. Do the same for OpenCode/Cursor/Grok/Copilot text generation. 2. (S) In worktree mode, merge title and branch into one call with schema {title, branch}: half the spawns. 3. (S) Start generation when the turn's first assistant delta is ingested, or after turn.started plus about 1 s, instead of before sendTurn. 4. (S) Lower the timeout to about 30 s and retries to 1 for titles; the user's own first message is already the fallback title (titleSeed).

Verifier (Confirmed)

Verified that title and branch generation are forked before markDispatched/sendTurn (PCR.ts:1823-1864, fork at 1845/1852) while the Claude CLI is still booting. Default text-gen selection is Codex (settings.ts:660-668). The light flag set is gated to operation === 'answerSideQuestion' only (CodexTextGeneration.ts:177-205; ClaudeTextGeneration.ts:124-153). The Claude title/branch path also runs with tools enabled and --dangerously-skip-permissions in the user's repo (toolsEnabled defaults true, ClaudeTextGeneration.ts:91,162), which is excessive capability for a title. Retry is 2x with exponential 2 s (PCR.ts:1366-1369); timeouts are 180 s (CodexTextGeneration.ts:39, ClaudeTextGeneration.ts:49). Not re-measured: the CPU/RSS/+313 ms contention numbers are a single-machine measurement. The 86k-token Claude figure applies only to users who switched text-gen to Claude. Caveats for the proposal: --ignore-user-config drops custom model_providers/base_url in config.toml, and --setting-sources '' drops settings.json env/apiKeyHelper. Users who rely on these would see title generation fail, so keep a fallback to full mode on auth/provider errors.

none. The side-question isolation code (textGeneration/SideQuestionIsolation.ts) already proves the flag set works.

Part of Priority 8: New thread and the first turn

Expected gain

-700 ms per capture on a 121 MiB repo (measured); about -1.2 s per capture on the user's real repo (1,360 ms add -A); scales with tracked bytes (est. -5 s or more on 1 GiB repos). Applies to every turn completion and the first-turn baseline; also -45 ms detect per op.

What happens today

captureCheckpoint creates a temp dir, runs rev-parse --verify HEAD and read-tree HEAD into an empty GIT_INDEX_FILE, then add -A -- ., write-tree, commit-tree and update-ref: 6 git spawns. The fresh index has no stat data, so add -A rehashes every tracked file on every capture. That means every turn completion, plus the first-turn baseline. Measured on the scratch clone (6,041 files, 121 MiB): 820 ms total, 727 ms in add -A. Copying .git/index into the temp file first: 118 ms total, 45 ms in add -A, same tree. In the user's real trace a completion capture took 1,487 ms, 1,360 ms of it in add -A. GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, core.untrackedCache and fsmonitor gave no further gain (128-134 ms). Entries marked assume-unchanged keep their stale OID in a copied index. Clearing that bit on the temp copy restores the identical tree (verified). The VCS detection cache TTL is only 2 s (VcsDriverRegistry.ts:10), so each checkpoint operation after a pause re-runs detection: 43.8-52.6 ms in the real trace.

Proposal

In captureCheckpoint: resolve the real index path with git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index (correct for linked worktrees), copy it to tempIndexPath, and fall back to read-tree HEAD if missing, if the copy fails, or if a split index is present (sharedindex.*). Run git ls-files -v -z and, if any entry has a lowercase tag, pipe those paths to update-index --no-assume-unchanged --no-skip-worktree --stdin on the temp copy. Alternative: only fall back when such entries exist. Keep add -A / write-tree / commit-tree / update-ref as they are. Raise DETECTION_CACHE_TTL to about 60 s, invalidated by worktree removal/relocation.

I re-ran checkpoint-bench.mjs on the scratch clone (6,041 files, 5 runs). Current: 848 ms total, add -A 756 ms. Seeded: 109 ms total, add -A 41 ms. Trees are identical. untrackedCache/fsmonitor gave no gain. This is not on the first-token critical path (sendTurn never waits), but it runs for every completion capture and the first-turn baseline, and it shortens the race window. DETECTION_CACHE_TTL is 2 s (VcsDriverRegistry.ts:10, 113-119). The current real trace window shows VcsDriverRegistry.detect n=85, p50 39.9 ms over 16 min, which supports a longer TTL. Keep null/negative detections short so a fresh git init is not hidden. Besides assume-unchanged, handle skip-worktree/sparse entries: add -A does not touch them, so a copied index keeps the index version where read-tree HEAD gives the HEAD version. Keep the split-index fallback.

Part of Priority 8: New thread and the first turn

Expected gain

Restores native compaction (avoids one full uncached-context Claude turn per 'compact' choice, often 100k+ input tokens) and user slash commands; also removes ~230 tokens per turn

What happens today

The Claude cache-review 'compact' choice dispatches thread.turn.start with text '/compact' (claudeCacheReview.ts:124). ProviderCommandReactor maps it to input '/compact' (PCR.ts:1254-1260). ProviderService.sendTurn then always rewrites input to ${ASSISTANT_ATTACHMENT_INSTRUCTIONS}\n\n${input} (ProviderService.ts:1703-1706). In ClaudeAdapter, isClaudeNativeCompaction requires input.trim() === '/compact' (claudeNativeCompaction.ts:6), so it is false. buildPromptText therefore does not return the bare '/compact' (ClaudeAdapter.ts:1372), and the host-context prefix may also be added (5979-5984). The CLI receives '<instructions>\n\n/compact' as an ordinary user prompt, and Claude Code only treats input that starts with '/' as a command. The result: instead of a cheap compaction, the user pays a full model turn on the uncached long context, which is exactly what the review tried to avoid. The client then fails with 'Native compaction did not complete successfully' because no context-compaction activity appears (claudeCacheReview.ts:165-175). Every user-typed Claude slash command (/init, /review, custom .claude/commands) is delivered as plain text the same way. No test covers the ProviderService -> adapter path (no test references ASSISTANT_ATTACHMENT_INSTRUCTIONS). Introduced in commit 6f299406f (2026-09-07).

Proposal

Move the attachment instructions to session-level instructions (Claude appendSystemPrompt at ClaudeAdapter.ts:5557-5562, Codex developer instructions) and delete the per-turn prefix. As an immediate S fix, skip the prefix in ProviderService.sendTurn when input.trimStart().startsWith('/'). Add an integration test through ProviderService.sendTurn with a Claude adapter double asserting that the prompt for '/compact' is exactly '/compact'.

This finding was added by the adversarial verifier while checking the investigator's report. It has not been verified a second time.

Part of Priority 8: New thread and the first turn

Expected gain

Claude: -2.0 to -2.3 s to first token on new threads and on threads reaped after 5 min (measured init 2.30-2.38 s). Codex: -1.5 to -2.2 s on the first turn of a thread plus ~0.25 s spawn/initialize (measured).

What happens today

Sessions only start inside the turn-start lane: ensureSessionForThread calls providerService.startSession at ProviderCommandReactor.ts:825. Nothing starts one earlier; a search for prewarm/speculative finds only sidebar thread-detail and WS-subscription prefetch. Measured Claude cold path: spawn->system/init 2.30-2.38 s with the user's setting sources (11 plugins, notion/token-counter/ryco MCP); 0.30 s with none. sendTurn's setPermissionMode await releases the prompt only after that. Warm-process turns reach the first stream event in 0.98-1.45 s; cold totals are 3.4-3.8 s. Codex: spawn+initialize 136-146 ms and thread/start 97-825 ms are awaited in startSession. On top of that, the first turn on a new thread takes 3.0-3.8 s to the first delta, but 1.5-1.75 s when thread/start ran ≥6 s earlier (measured), so the per-thread warm-up overlaps with idle time. Sessions are reaped after 5 minutes idle (ProviderSessionReaper.ts:13), so returning to an 'existing' thread usually pays the cold path again (scenario a degrades to b).

Proposal

1. Add a provider.session.prewarm RPC that the client fires (debounced, max 1 per thread per 30 s) on composer focus or first keystroke in a draft or existing thread, and when a thread is opened whose session status is stopped/reaped. 2. Server: a per-instance warm pool keyed by (instanceId, cwd, runtimeMode, tokenMode, model family), capacity 1-2 per instance, idle TTL 90-120 s, dropped under memory pressure or when settings change. Claude: run openSessionContext with a generated sessionId (or the resume cursor for an existing thread) and no prompt, so the CLI boots and connects MCP. Codex: run makeCodexSessionRuntime + start(), which already does initialize + thread/start (resume for existing threads). 3. On Send, ensureSessionForThread adopts a matching warm runtime by rebinding its runtimeSessionId to the thread (bindSessionToThread) instead of starting a new one; on mismatch, stop it. 4. Reuse the existing reaper and startup admission for limits. 5. Fix the checkpoint baseline ordering first (see checkpoint-baseline-race), because warm sessions shorten the window in which the race is won. Worktree mode: the Claude cwd is unknown until the worktree exists, so pre-warm Codex there via the shared app-server (see codex-shared-app-server), or speculatively create the worktree at draft time (separate decision).

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

Confirmed: no provider-process prewarm exists. A grep for prewarm/warm finds only the sidebar thread-detail prewarm (Sidebar.tsx:1085-1100, useSidebarThreadPrewarm). The only session start is ensureSessionForThread -> providerService.startSession (ProviderCommandReactor.ts:819-836, called at 1033/1013). Claude startSession returns right after createQuery (ClaudeAdapter.ts:5649-5666) because Agent Control is off by default (settings.ts:494-495). The CLI boot is therefore paid inside sendTurn (setPermissionMode / prompt consumption). Reaper threshold is 5 min (ProviderSessionReaper.ts:13). The ~2.0-2.3 s Claude saving is an estimate, not a measurement: claude-coldstart.mjs queues the prompt at t0 and never measured a promptless boot, so it is unknown how much MCP/plugin init completes before the first user message. Cost is under-weighted. The same investigator measured a full-config Claude CLI tree at ~1.3 GiB RSS, and prewarming on composer focus or first keystroke would routinely spawn processes that are never used. Many mismatches waste a warm process: a Claude model change forces a restart (PCR.ts:915-918); effort, thinking and fastMode are baked into spawn settings (ClaudeAdapter.ts:5551-5555); token mode and custom system prompt go into appendSystemPrompt; Agent Control and device bindings are keyed by threadId; provider_session_runtime bindings are keyed by threadId, which does not exist server-side for client drafts. Cheaper first step: keep the session of the currently open thread alive past the 5-min reaper, and prewarm only on opening an existing reaped thread. Risk should be medium-high, not medium.

Part of Priority 8: New thread and the first turn

Expected gain

About -200 to -230 ms main-thread work per turn start and -70 ms per completion for this user (measured 36-41 ms x 6-8 calls); about -1,400 SQL statements per turn start; removes linear growth with history.

What happens today

listSessions asks every adapter for live sessions, then runs directory.listThreadIds() (SELECT * of provider_session_runtime with JSON columns, decoded) and getBinding(threadId) for EVERY row with unbounded concurrency. Each lookup is another SELECT plus Schema decode on synchronous node:sqlite, on the main thread. Rows are never pruned: the user has 701 (698 stopped). Real trace: 35.6-40.8 ms per call, 702 sql.execute spans each; lower bound replayed at 11-13 ms. Callers that only need one thread: ProviderCommandReactor x2 per turn, ProviderRuntimeIngestion on turn.started (on the path to the first projected delta), CheckpointReactor resolveSessionRuntimeForThread x3 per turn start and x2 per completion (also when preferSessionRuntime=false). That is about 6 x 38 ms = about 230 ms of event-loop blocking per turn start, growing linearly with history.

Proposal

Add ProviderService.getSessionForThread(threadId): read the binding via one getBinding, then adapter.listSessions() on that binding's instance only, filtered by sessionMatchesBinding. Use it at all the call sites above. Rewrite listSessions to look up bindings only for threadIds that adapters report as live (k queries, typically 1-5), or to call listBindings() once (it already exists, ProviderSessionDirectory.ts:181-191) instead of N getBinding calls. Optionally prune or archive stopped bindings older than N days, or add WHERE status != 'stopped' where only live ones matter. In resolveCheckpointCwd, skip the session lookup when preferSessionRuntime is false and the thread workspace resolves.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Code matches: ProviderService.ts:2160-2228 runs listThreadIds, then getBinding per row with concurrency 'unbounded', on synchronous node:sqlite. listBindings already exists (ProviderSessionDirectory.ts:181-191). Callers verified: PCR.ts:723-728 and 1226-1230 (serial before sendTurn, so on the critical path); ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:2091-2097 via 2530 on every turn.started before it is projected; CheckpointReactor.ts:302-310 via resolveCheckpointCwd, called even when preferSessionRuntime=false (CR.ts:339); CR.ts:712 on completion. Re-ran list-sessions-bench: 11.05 ms/call lower bound (701 rows), 11.9 ms Effect-shaped. The current trace window shows listSessions at 40.8 and 74.4 ms with span overhead. The fix is easy because resolveRoutableSessionUnlocked (ProviderService.ts:1133-1162) already does a targeted getBinding plus a single-adapter listSessions. Downgraded: the ~230 ms is total event-loop work. The critical-path saving to first token is the 2 PCR calls plus 1 ingestion call, about 35-120 ms, growing linearly with history.

Part of Priority 8: New thread and the first turn

Expected gain

Removes a silent wrong-diff/wrong-revert bug for first turns. Latency cost about +0-120 ms with a seeded index: hidden behind session start for cold sessions, about +100 ms for warm ones.

What happens today

The baseline ref is captured by CheckpointReactor reacting to the thread.message-sent / turn-start-requested domain events. That is a separate subscriber with a single makeDrainableWorker shared by all threads (1531-1537). ProviderCommandReactor forks sendTurn independently. The checkpoint.baseline.captured receipt is published (CheckpointReactor.ts:699-705, 781-787) but nothing in production awaits it. A capture only happens when the baseline ref is missing, i.e. the first turn of a thread, which is the new-thread and worktree case. It takes 820 ms on the 121 MiB clone and 1.5 s on the real repo (fresh index). It queues behind other threads' completion work: a real completion took 1,756 ms. If the agent edits a file before git add -A reads it, the baseline contains the agent's own change, and the turn diff and revert-to-checkpoint silently miss it. Setup scripts launched at ws/context.ts:775 also write files while the baseline runs. Pre-warmed sessions (finding 1) would shrink the window further.

Proposal

Move first-turn baseline creation into the turn-start path: in prepareAndSubmitTurnStart, start ensureBaseline(thread, cwd) (hasCheckpointRef, then the fast seeded capture) concurrently with ensureSessionForThread via Effect.all/fork, and join it before markDispatched/sendTurn with a bounded timeout (e.g. 5 s). On timeout, record checkpoint status 'missing' with an activity instead of silently racing. Keep the CheckpointReactor handler only as a fallback no-op when the ref exists. Make the CheckpointReactor worker keyed per thread (makeKeyedSerialWorker like ProviderCommandReactor's lanes) so one thread's capture/diff never delays another thread's work.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

Confirmed: nothing consumes checkpoint.baseline.captured. It has only publishers (CheckpointReactor.ts:699-705, 781-787) and the schema (RuntimeReceiptBus.ts:22). The reactor uses one global makeDrainableWorker (1531-1537), and sendTurn is forked independently (PCR.ts:1886-1917). The first-turn race is usually won today. A first turn always gets a cold session (Claude ≥2.3 s boot plus ≥1 s to first token before any tool call), and the capture takes 0.1-1.5 s. Losing it needs a backed-up global queue or a large repo, where fresh-index add -A scales with tracked bytes. The investigator missed a broader variant. Turn N's completion capture IS turn N+1's baseline, and it runs after turn.completed in the same global queue. currentTurnCount is derived from projected checkpoints (CR.ts:764-775), so turn N+1's handler can find an older ref and return while N's capture is still pending. A quick follow-up send on a warm session (~1 s to first token) can then put N+1 edits into ref N, and N+1's diff misses them. The fix must also join the previous turn's pending completion capture, not only first-turn baselines. Setup-script output landing in the baseline or the diff is a separate nondeterminism. A per-thread worker is feasible: packages/shared/src/KeyedSerialWorker.ts:65 already exists.

Part of Priority 8: New thread and the first turn

Expected gain

-270 ms (real trace) per turn start from dropping the redundant path, plus -2 x (70-170) ms detail decodes per turn for long threads; frees the event loop during the first-delta window; removes a backpressure stall risk.

What happens today

Each of three triggers runs resolveThreadDetail = getThreadDetailById: user message-sent, turn-start-requested, and runtime turn.started (1486-1492). That query loads ALL messages, activities (with payload JSON), plans and checkpoints of the thread, only to read projectId, worktreePath and the max checkpointTurnCount. Each trigger also runs listSessions, VCS detect and rev-parse. Real trace: the runtime turn.started path took 271.9 ms although the baseline already existed (detail 170 ms, listSessions 41 ms, detect 44 ms, rev-parse 17 ms). Completion adds another detail load (70 ms). A scratch replay of the user's largest thread (27,759 activities, 17.8 MB JSON) costs ≥118 ms per load, 354 ms per turn start, all synchronous decode on the event loop that also projects the first deltas. The subscription also enqueues every thread.message-sent, including streaming assistant deltas, into the single lossless worker (capacity 1,024) behind multi-second git work. Once that worker is full, the bounded domain PubSub (4,096, backpressure) can stall live delivery for all subscribers.

Proposal

1. Replace resolveThreadDetail in the baseline and completion paths with a targeted query: thread shell (projectId, worktreePath, session) + SELECT MAX(checkpoint_turn_count) + SELECT ... WHERE turn_id = ? for the placeholder check. 2. Delete the runtime turn.started baseline handler (the domain path covers it), or reduce it to an in-memory 'baseline known for thread X turnCount N' set. 3. In start(), filter thread.message-sent events with role !== 'user' or streaming === true before worker.enqueue. 4. Key the worker per thread (see checkpoint-baseline-race).

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

Confirmed: 3 full getThreadDetailById loads per turn start. The sources are the user thread.message-sent (decider.ts:1528-1546, turnId null so it passes the CR.ts:737-745 filter), turn-start-requested, and runtime turn.started (CR.ts:1489-1490, 659-707). Each also runs listSessions, detect and rev-parse. getThreadDetailById loads all activities with payload JSON (ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:3025-3113, 1274-1296). The real trace confirms one runtime turn.started path at 271.9 ms. Typical cost is much smaller than claimed: in the real trace window resolveThreadDetail had n=139, p50 2.8 ms, p90 10.6, p99 111, max 170. My rerun of thread-detail-bench gave 109 ms for the 27.8k-activity thread and 55 ms for 6.5k. So ~350 ms per turn start applies only to the largest threads. Streaming deltas are enqueued (trace: processDomainEvent n=18 at ~0 ms), but they are coalesced in ingestion. Filling 1,024 slots needs a multi-second backlog of many threads; that is unmeasured and low-likelihood, though filtering at enqueue is still a free fix. Prior work: performance-efficiency-size-improvements.md item 'Make thread detail snapshots selective or paged' is the generic residual; these call sites are new specifics.

Part of Priority 8: New thread and the first turn

Expected gain

-0.5 s or more (network-dependent fetch) and -2-3 client RTTs (estimate 30-600 ms depending on local vs hosted) per worktree first send; removes the branch-rename-during-turn race.

What happens today

Client: before dispatching it awaits getConfig, then getProjectPreferences, then (if no prefix) getSettings, all serial. The server repeats preference resolution anyway in resolveBootstrapPreferences (ws/context.ts:655-662). Server, inside the dispatch RPC: fetchOrigin defaults to true (draftStore.ts:757/785) and runs git fetch --prune --no-tags origin +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*, all 520 heads here (measured 0.49-0.54 s steady state; more when other branches moved). Then git worktree add (0.84-1.15 s for 6k files), createBootstrapThread + drainThrough, thread.meta.update, worktree.create, thread.attach-to-worktree (4 serial dispatches), and the setup-script PTY open, which takes the node-wide storageLifecycleLock (Semaphore(1), lifecycle.ts:10) that every leaseThreadPath also needs. Only then is turn.start dispatched and session start can begin. After the session starts, the LLM branch rename (git branch -m) runs concurrently with the live agent in the same worktree: a ref-lock race with agent git commands, and the agent sees its branch renamed mid-turn.

Proposal

1. Fetch only the base branch (+refs/heads/<base>:refs/remotes/origin/<base>), and start that fetch in the background when the composer enters worktree mode (cache the result for about 60 s). Make the send path only wait if the fetch is still in flight. 2. Drop the client getConfig/getProjectPreferences/getSettings RPCs and let resolveBootstrapPreferences supply the prefix/setup defaults. 3. Fold thread.create/meta.update/worktree.create/attach into one decider command (one transaction). 4. For Codex, start the (shared) app-server and initialize in parallel with fetch+worktree add, then thread/start with the new cwd. 5. Generate the branch name in parallel with fetch+worktree-add and use it as -b if ready. Otherwise keep the temporary name and rename only when the first turn completes (agent idle), never during it.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Client: executeChatSendTurn.ts:499-513 awaits getConfig, a raw RPC every time (wsRpcClient.ts:797). It then awaits getProjectPreferences (projectPreferences.ts:26-29, only when the capability is present) and optionally getSettings, all serially. Server: fetchOrigin fetches all heads (GitVcsDriverCore.ts:2013-2020, called at 2336-2337). Missed: when the base is origin/HEAD there is an extra network git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD (2338-2352). A base-only fetch should resolve refs/remotes/origin/HEAD locally first. Four serial dispatches plus drainThrough (ws/context.ts:664-770) are confirmed. refreshGitStatus at 772 is forkDetach (ws/context.ts:965-968), so it does not block. Setup only runs when a setup script exists. Terminal open holds storageLifecycleLock (Manager.ts:2316). OrchestrationEngine.ts:599 also processes EVERY command under that same lock, so a PTY open briefly stalls all orchestration commands. The branch rename is forked mid-turn (PCR.ts:1839-1845, rename at 1310-1314) as described. Fetch and worktree-add timings were not re-measured.

Low impactEffort S◐ Partially confirmedClaude sends pay a client review RPC and an unconditional setPermissionMode control round trip on every turn-1 RTT per Claude send (9-20 ms server + RTT locally; estimated 50-200 ms over a hosted relay); -1 control RTT per turn; earlier turn.started on cold sessions (about 2.3 s earlier server-side state).
Category: Network / RTTRisk: lowInvestigator confidence: mediumRating changed by verifier: impact medium → low, effort S → Sgap-first-turn-latency:claude-per-turn-rtts
Expected gain

-1 RTT per Claude send (9-20 ms server + RTT locally; estimated 50-200 ms over a hosted relay); -1 control RTT per turn; earlier turn.started on cold sessions (about 2.3 s earlier server-side state).

What happens today

Every non-first Claude send on a server thread awaits getThreadWindow (messages 1, activities 40, checkpoints 1, plans 1) before thread.turn.start is dispatched. Real trace server time: p50 8.9 ms, p90 19.9 ms, plus one RTT, which is large on the hosted relay. The decision (assessClaudeCacheResume) uses data the client's live thread subscription already holds. Server side, sendTurnOnContext calls query.setPermissionMode on every turn whenever interactionMode is set, which is always, since it comes from the turn-start payload. There is no 'unchanged' check, unlike the ACP runtime, which short-circuits setMode/setConfigOption (AcpSessionRuntime.ts:398-412, 668-673). turn.started is offered only after that await, so on a cold session the server-confirmed turn start, and the CheckpointReactor/ingestion work tied to it, slip by the full CLI boot (2.3 s).

Proposal

Client: evaluate assessClaudeCacheResume from the subscribed thread state and call getThreadWindow only when that state is missing or stale (older than the last session event), or move the check into the decider as a typed 'needs-review' rejection so the happy path costs no extra RTT. Server: track context.currentPermissionMode, and only call setPermissionMode when the target differs from it. Emit turn.started before awaiting a mode switch if ordering allows.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

Review RPC confirmed. reviewClaudeResumeBeforeSend (claudeCacheReview.ts:52-80) is awaited first in commitSendTurnDispatchOnce (sendEngine.ts:361), but only for non-first Claude sends on server threads that are not slash commands. It uses window.workspaceCwd, which is server-resolved, and is intentionally fail-closed against fresh server state, so a local-subscription shortcut must keep that guarantee. setPermissionMode is unconditional (ClaudeAdapter.ts:5936-5946), and interactionMode is always present via its decoding default (orchestration.ts:2620-2622). However, on a cold session this does not delay the first token: the CLI cannot consume the queued prompt before boot anyway. On a warm session the saving is one local stdio control round trip of a few ms. Emitting turn.started before the mode switch would announce a turn that can still fail on setPermissionMode, so it is not recommended. The ACP short-circuit cited is at AcpSessionRuntime.ts:398-412. Missed: the first message on a server thread awaits an extra thread.meta.update title dispatch (sendEngine.ts:366-375) before thread.turn.start, which could fold into the turn-start command.

Low impactEffort S✓ ConfirmedTurn-start lane repeats thread/project reads, takes the node-wide storage lock 2-3 times, and runs a provider goal RPC every turn-1 provider RPC and about -6 SQL/realpath round trips per turn (estimate 3-15 ms); removes head-of-line blocking behind terminal opens.
Category: DatabaseRisk: lowInvestigator confidence: mediumgap-first-turn-latency:turnstart-redundant-reads-and-global-lock
Expected gain

-1 provider RPC and about -6 SQL/realpath round trips per turn (estimate 3-15 ms); removes head-of-line blocking behind terminal opens.

What happens today

One turn start calls resolveThread 4 times (1722, 1163, 711, 1041) and resolveProject 3-4 times (716, 1224, 1827). leaseThreadPath runs twice (717 and again inside ensureRecordedWorktreeAvailable at 562), and ProviderService.startSession takes another lease (1429-1439). Each acquireStoragePathUseLease runs realpath and SQL under storageLifecycleLock = Semaphore.makeUnsafe(1), the same lock terminal open/restart/guarded writes hold (terminal/Layers/Manager.ts:2316-2323), so a concurrent terminal spawn delays sends on any thread. reconcileThreadGoal issues a provider RPC (Codex thread/goal/get, bounded by the 30 s control timeout) before every turn/start, even when the thread has no goal and the provider has never reported one.

Proposal

Pass the resolved OrchestrationThreadShell/ProjectShell from prepareAndSubmitTurnStart into buildSendTurnRequestForThread / ensureSessionForThread / reconcileThreadGoal instead of re-reading them. Acquire the path lease once per turn start and hand it to startSession. Cache 'no native goal' per runtimeSessionId and skip getThreadGoal when the thread has no goal and the cache says none; or run reconcileThreadGoal concurrently with session start when no goal sync is pending. Narrow storageLifecycleLock for terminal writes and open, or switch path leases to a read/write lock so readers do not serialize.

Verifier (Confirmed)

resolveThread is called at PCR.ts:1722, 1163, 711, 1041; resolveProject at 716, 1224, 1827. leaseThreadPath runs twice on the same path (717, then 562 inside ensureRecordedWorktreeAvailable), plus the startSession lease when starting (ProviderService.ts:1429-1439). Each lease does a realpath and SQL under storageLifecycleLock (lifecycle.ts:10, 113-135). The lock is broader than stated: OrchestrationEngine.ts:599 runs every command's processEnvelope under it, and so do WorkspaceFileSystem writes (WorkspaceFileSystem.ts:656-662) and terminal open/restart/guarded writes (Manager.ts:2316-2323). Path leases therefore interleave with every dispatched command, including ingestion delta dispatches. reconcileThreadGoal calls getThreadGoal every turn (PCR.ts:1109-1111). For Codex that is a thread/goal/get RPC (CodexAdapter.ts:2689); for Claude it returns false cheaply (ProviderService.ts:1778). The impact estimate of a few ms is plausible.

Low impactEffort M◐ Partially confirmedSession-start hangs surface only after 120-300 s; Cursor's default binary name collides with another CLIFailure feedback in 15-30 s instead of 120-300 s; avoids spawning the wrong agent binary.
Category: ReliabilityRisk: lowInvestigator confidence: mediumRating changed by verifier: impact medium → low, effort M → Mgap-first-turn-latency:phase-deadlines-and-hangs
Expected gain

Failure feedback in 15-30 s instead of 120-300 s; avoids spawning the wrong agent binary.

What happens today

DEFAULT_SESSION_START_TIMEOUT_MS is 120 s (300 s for registry ACP), and turn acceptance is 90 s. ACP startOnce runs initialize, authenticate and session/new with no per-phase deadline. Measured: cursor-agent ACP initialize took 3,991 ms, and authenticate(cursor_login) did not reply within about 85 s, so a user would watch 'working' for 2 minutes before a generic timeout. ProviderService tracks progress.phase (lock/admission/adapter), but only for the final timeout text. Startup admission allows 4 concurrent starts per instance (ProviderService.ts:129), so 4 hung starts block the rest. Cursor's default binaryPath is 'agent' (settings.ts:318). On this machine which -a agent resolves ~/.grok/bin/agent (the Grok CLI) before Cursor's ~/.local/bin/agent. Text generation can hold a 1.3 GiB process tree for up to 3 x 180 s.

Proposal

Add per-phase deadlines inside adapters: ACP initialize/authenticate 20 s, session/new|load 30 s; Codex initialize 15 s, thread/start 30 s; Claude init/MCP gate 30 s. Report the phase to the client via a session.state.changed 'starting: authenticating…' activity so the UI can say what it is waiting on. Fail fast with an actionable message (e.g. 'Cursor login check did not answer; run cursor-agent login'). Default the Cursor binary to 'cursor-agent' (or verify the resolved binary's --version identity at probe time). Cap text-generation timeouts (see textgen finding).

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

Timeouts confirmed: 120 s start, 300 s registry, 90 s acceptance (providerOperationPolicy.ts:24-28). The phase is tracked only for the timeout text (ProviderService.ts:1362-1364, 1541-1561). ACP startOnce has no per-phase deadline (AcpSessionRuntime.ts:477-490). For the default Claude path, startSession returns right after createQuery, so a hung CLI boot surfaces through the 90 s turn-acceptance deadline, not the session-start one. Cursor is disabled by default; its spawn default is 'agent' (CursorAcpSupport.ts:40, settings.ts:318). On this machine which -a agent resolves ~/.grok/bin/agent before Cursor's ~/.local/bin/agent: confirmed, but machine-specific. There is no happy-path latency effect; this is reliability/UX only.

Prior work

The Aug report bounded queues; phase-level start deadlines are new.

Category: Process spawnsRisk: mediumInvestigator confidence: mediumRating changed by verifier: impact medium → low, effort L → Lgap-first-turn-latency:codex-shared-app-server
Expected gain

-140 to -250 ms (up to -0.9 s cold) per new Codex session; -125 MiB RSS per additional concurrent Codex thread; fewer spawns for resumes after idle reaping.

What happens today

makeCodexSessionRuntime spawns codex app-server per session (1169-1186) and runs initialize, then thread/start or resume. Measured: initialize 136-146 ms after spawn, first thread/start 825 ms cold / about 110 ms warm, about 125 MiB RSS per idle process. A second thread/start on the SAME process works and takes about 100 ms, so the protocol already multiplexes threads. MCP servers are per thread either way (measured 7 child processes, about 730 MiB per thread for this user's config). OpenCode already shares one server per instance via serverOwner (OpenCodeDriver.ts:128-131).

Proposal

Introduce a CodexAppServerOwner per provider instance (same shape as makeOpenCodeServerOwner): lazily spawned, initialised once, ref-counted by sessions, restarted on crash with per-thread session.exited fan-out. CodexSessionRuntime becomes a per-thread view: route server notifications and server requests by params.threadId into per-thread queues, and keep thread/start/resume, turn/*, goal and interrupt per thread. Keep a per-thread process only for computer-use/isolated cases and per-env overrides. This also makes Codex pre-warm (finding 1) cheap: a warm owner is shared, and only thread/start is speculative.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

Confirmed: there is one codex app-server spawn per session (CodexSessionRuntime.ts:1168-1175), and start() runs initialize then thread/start or resume (2110-2144). Per-thread settings (cwd, model, device tools, Agent Control) travel in thread/start params (openCodexThread, CodexSessionRuntime.ts:601-625), so multiplexing is feasible. OpenCode's serverOwner pattern is at OpenCodeDriver.ts:127-130. Not reproduced: no Codex timings were re-run. The 825 ms 'cold' thread/start may be first-ever disk/auth warm-up rather than a per-process cost, so the reliable latency saving is about 140 ms of spawn+initialize per new session. Reliability cost conflicts with 'reliability first': one crashed or wedged app-server would kill or head-of-line-block every Codex thread on the instance, and the capped protocol queues (256 items) become shared. The memory saving (~125 MiB per concurrent thread) is the stronger argument.

Terminal, diff, files panels 16 findings · 2 high · 10 medium · 4 low

Opening any side panel spawns 3 diff workers (each carrying 608 KiB of unused WASM) and tears them down on close. Terminal history is shipped on every connect (75% of boot WebSocket bytes) and again on every reopen.

How it works today (investigator's summary)

The first open of a thread side surface has two parts. The client loads chunks and creates workers. The server spawns git or a shell. Both parts are serialized behind the mount. Clicking the workspace toggle mounts LazyRightPanel (ChatRightPanel.tsx:70-124). It wraps every mode in DiffWorkerPoolProvider, so opening the launcher, terminal, files, simulator or agents tab immediately creates 3 @pierre/diffs workers on an 18-core machine. Measured: created 55 ms after the click, initialized at 72 ms. Each worker loads the same 835,418 B script, and 608 KiB of that is an inlined Oniguruma WASM that is never used, because the JS regex engine is selected. The pool is torn down 360 ms after every panel close, so the next open pays for the workers, the cold grammars and the caches again. Files mode opens text files in the @pierre/diffs editor and highlights them on the main thread, so it never uses the pool. Chunks form a waterfall: ThreadWorkspacePanel, then the mode chunk, then its static deps (modulePreload is off). Data RPCs (listEntries, readLocalChanges, getFullThreadDiff, terminal.open, device.read) start only after the panel has mounted and revealed. In the loopback runs: listEntries left 330 ms after the click, terminal.open 389 ms after it, and the first diff highlight arrived about 240 ms after the file rows. Nothing preloads panel chunks on hover, shortcut or idle.

Terminal: the drawer chunk is 361,106 B raw / 91 KiB gzip, almost all @xterm/xterm 6 using the default DOM renderer, plus 3.9 KB CSS. The PTY is spawned only after xterm mounts and fits (ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:866-881). The shell is the user's $SHELL, interactive but not login; zsh gets -o nopromptsp. Its rc startup (182–640 ms measured) runs after all the client work, so the cold first open showed a prompt at 1,058 ms. Each mount sends open plus 2 resize RPCs. History (5,000 lines / 2 MiB cap) has two problems. It is re-sent in full on every drawer reopen or tab switch, because xterm is disposed. It is also sent at every WebSocket connect for every running terminal through the subscribeTerminalEvents snapshot: measured 432 KB twice per reload, 75% of the boot WebSocket bytes. On the server, every output chunk queues a rewrite of the whole history file (coalesced to one per 40 ms). While any shell is alive, the server spawns ps over the whole process table every second.

Review/diff: getTurnDiff runs 5 git spawns, 4 of them sequential, before sending the whole patch (≤10 MB) in one RPC. There is no server cache, even though checkpoint commits are immutable. No full file contents are fetched up front: patches only, rendered through Virtualizer (overscroll 600, IntersectionObserver margin 1200). The only limits are the 10 MB / 2 MB output caps, the 200-untracked-file cap and tokenizeMaxLineLength 1000. Local-changes review runs 9 sequential git spawns plus 1 per untracked file. The client keeps every viewed patch forever in keepAlive atoms. File preview: the 265 KiB PreviewPanel chunk is about 150 KiB @pierre/diffs editor (editor.js 64.7 KiB, selection 21.2, pieceTable 11.7, tokenizer 9.9). The text read limit is 512 KiB and binary reads allow 4 MiB. listEntries ships up to 25k entries (757 KiB for this repo). Tree icons come from a 285 KiB lazy manifest chunk plus SVGs fetched from cdn.jsdelivr.net. The image-preview branch is dead code. These are lazy and well gated: mermaid (dynamic import when a diagram comes within 200px of the viewport, 601 KiB closure), the PDF viewer (React.lazy inside the dialog, 555 KiB plus the 1.2 MiB / 366 KiB gzip pdf.worker, loaded only when getDocument runs) and the HTML render panel (3 KiB).

High impactEffort S+ Added by verifierInitial terminal snapshots share the 4 MiB subscriber byte budget, so large combined histories cause a deterministic resync loop every 250 msFor affected users, eliminates a continuous loop of about 4 MiB every ~250 ms (≈16 MiB/s WebSocket/relay traffic plus server JSON.stringify and client decode), and restores live terminal events. Category: ReliabilityRisk: lowInvestigator confidence: mediumgap-right-panel-first-open:terminal-bootstrap-byte-budget-resync-loop

Part of Priority 17: Side panels: terminal, diff, files

Expected gain

For affected users, eliminates a continuous loop of about 4 MiB every ~250 ms (≈16 MiB/s WebSocket/relay traffic plus server JSON.stringify and client decode), and restores live terminal events. Estimated from code: threshold is a 4,194,304 B JSON sum of running snapshots.

What happens today

Each initial started event carries full history: up to 2 MiB of UTF-8 per terminal (Manager.ts:80-81), and more once JSON-escaped, since every ESC byte becomes \u001b (6 bytes). All of them are offered into initialQueue with the same ledger before the stream is returned (terminalRpc.ts:234-244). makeTerminalSubscriberOffer fails the queue with TerminalSubscriptionResyncError as soon as ledger.bytes + eventBytes > 4 MiB (:66). Queued items are delivered first and then the stream fails, as the existing test 'fails with the same resync signal when the queued byte budget trips' shows. The error message contains 'reconnect to resynchronize' (contracts terminal.ts:188), so the client classifies it as retryable (wsTransport.ts:80-86). It resubscribes after a constant 250 ms with no backoff (wsTransport.ts:41, 293). The server state has not changed, so every retry overflows again. Two terminals near the 2 MiB cap, or three or four with colour-heavy 1-1.5 MB histories, are enough. Progress-bar output with \r redraws reaches the byte cap well before 5,000 lines. Each cycle re-serialises the histories on the server (approximateJsonBytes does JSON.stringify plus TextEncoder per event) and pushes about 4 MiB over the WebSocket or relay, about 16 MiB/s. The client decodes it on the main thread, and live terminal events (activity, exit) never reach the client. Not reproduced. This is derived from code and the existing unit-test semantics.

Proposal

Exempt bootstrap snapshots from the live byte budget, or better, remove the reason for it by making replay snapshots metadata-only (see terminal-history-in-subscription-snapshot); the ledger then only counts live output. As a backstop, give resync retries exponential backoff with a cap in wsTransport for TerminalSubscriptionResyncError, and log once per connection. Add a terminalRpc test with two 2 MiB-history running sessions asserting that the subscription completes its bootstrap without failing.

Part of Priority 17: Side panels: terminal, diff, files

Expected gain

Per connect or reconnect, −(sum of the history of all running terminals across all threads), up to 2 MiB each, removed from ahead of the shell/config snapshot. Measured case: boot WebSocket bytes 1,145 KB → about 713 KB with one terminal. Matters most for hosted relay and mobile.

What happens today

subscribeTerminalEvents emits an initial started event per running session using snapshot(session), and that snapshot includes history (≤5,000 lines / 2 MiB each). It does this for all threads, on every WebSocket connect, reconnect and hosted relay attach. Measured on reload with one 421 KB-history terminal: the subscription chunk was 432,097 B at t=430 ms, ahead of the 130,482 B server-config snapshot at 438 ms. terminal.open then returned the same history again (431,900 B at 798 ms). Together that is 75% of the 1,144,673 B received at boot. The drawer discards the subscription copy: it hydrates from terminal.open and replays only events after that snapshot. Each event still lands in the client terminal store, whose zustand persist middleware JSON.stringifies and synchronously writes localStorage on every set (zustand middleware.mjs:365-368). partialize excludes events, so these writes are pure overhead: 3.5 µs at the measured 358 B, growing with thread count.

Proposal

Make initial subscription snapshots metadata-only. Send history: "" (or a new TerminalSessionSummary schema with historyBytes and cursor); terminal.open stays the only history source. Live started/restarted events from startSession can keep their (fresh, small) snapshot. Optionally add sinceCursor to terminal.open so a client with a buffer gets only the delta. Client side: keep terminal event buffers in a non-persisted store. Alternatively, wrap the persist storage so it skips setItem when the partialized JSON is unchanged.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

Waste confirmed. terminalRpc.ts:214-230 builds a started event with snapshot(session) for every running session (all threads). snapshot() includes history (Manager.ts:199-214), and listSessions is at Manager.ts:2305-2313. The subscription opens on every connection (connection.ts:278-279), and measured numbers are in measurements.json. However, the claim that 'the drawer discards the subscription copy' holds only at mount time (ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:866-904 filters with selectTerminalEventEntriesAfterSnapshot). An already-mounted drawer applies started events by calling writeTerminalSnapshot(event.snapshot) (ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:764-785), which resets xterm (\u001bc) and writes snapshot.history. That is the intended resync path; the comment at terminalRpc.ts:18-25 says the client 'resynchronizes from the session snapshot (which carries the retained history)'. Shipping history:"" as proposed would blank every open drawer on reconnect. The fix must mark replay snapshots (e.g. replay: true or a separate event type) and make a mounted drawer re-hydrate through terminal.open, ideally with sinceCursor, instead of writing the snapshot. Two bigger problems in this same path are reported as additional findings: replay started events force-open drawers, and a deterministic resync loop starts once histories exceed the 4 MiB subscriber budget. The persist-middleware overhead is real but negligible (3.5 µs). Impact stays high when combined with those problems.

Prior work

The Aug hardening capped terminal event buffering at 2,048 events / 2 MiB (docs/research/2026-08-12-performance-hardening-results.md:85). It did not address snapshot history in subscriptions.

Part of Priority 17: Side panels: terminal, diff, files

Expected gain

With (a)+(b): first diff highlight about 240 ms → about 70-90 ms (estimated from the measured 3.5x cold ratio), and warm per-file tokenization about 4-5x faster (37 → 8 ms per 200 lines; 360 → 75 ms per 1600 lines, measured in Node). With (a) only: −608 KiB raw / −231 KiB gzip per worker download (measured), about 3.5 s less at 1.6 Mbps uncompressed.

What happens today

vite.config.ts has no worker option, so ?worker builds as an IIFE (dist worker-B6jbnL_K.js starts with (function(){). The worker's createOnigurumaEngine(import("shiki/wasm")) gets inlined: sourcemap attribution puts 607.8 KiB of the 815.8 KiB worker in @shikijs/engine-oniguruma wasm-inlined. The provider does not set preferredHighlighter, so the default shiki-js engine runs and the WASM is dead weight in every worker download. Engine benchmark in Node 24 V8 (tsx, DiffPanel.tsx): JS engine cold 200 lines 658 ms, warm 37-43 ms, 1600 lines 337-460 ms. WASM engine cold 182-186 ms, warm 8-9 ms, 1600 lines 71-82 ms; it costs 35 ms more to create. In the browser, the first diff highlight landed about 240-250 ms after the file rows (n=3). Reliability risk (estimate, not reproduced): the local server serves assets uncompressed (transfer = 835,718 B). At 1.6 Mbps one worker takes about 4.2 s to download, and the pool has a 10 s init timeout that, if hit, sets workersFailed (WorkerPoolManager.js:25, 281, 342-349).

Proposal

Recommended: (a) set worker: { format: "es" } in vite.config.ts. The wasm then becomes its own hashed chunk, fetched once and served from HTTP cache to every worker, and the worker script shrinks to about 227 KiB raw / about 70 KiB gzip. (b) Set highlighterOptions.preferredHighlighter: "shiki-wasm" in DiffWorkerPoolProvider, so diff tokenization uses the 4-5x faster engine. The pool's main-thread highlighter, used only for plain-text placeholders, would then also instantiate the wasm (35 ms, once per pool). Accept that, or patch @pierre/diffs to take separate main and worker engines. If the WASM engine is rejected, still do (a) to drop the dead 608 KiB. Add a guard to apps/web/src/perf/webBundleSplitting.test.ts that the worker chunk contains no wasm-inlined source.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

(a) Verified. vite.config.ts has no worker option (build at :185-190). dist/assets/worker-B6jbnL_K.js (835,418 B) starts with (function(){. Its sourcemap lists @shikijs/engine-oniguruma/dist/wasm-inlined.mjs and shiki/dist/wasm.mjs as sources, and the bundle contains WebAssembly.instantiate*. worker.js:1768-1773 imports shiki/wasm only when preferredHighlighter==='shiki-wasm'. The constructor defaults to 'shiki-js' (WorkerPoolManager.js:58), and DiffWorkerPoolProvider never sets it, so the 608 KiB is dead in every worker isolate. ES-format workers are already a requirement: pdf.js loads pdf.worker.min.mjs as a module worker. So worker: { format: 'es' } is low-risk and the dead weight is solidly confirmed. (b) The engine switch is plausible but the estimate is speculative. 240 → 70-90 ms is extrapolated from a Node benchmark, and the 240 ms browser gap also includes main-thread grammar chunk loading, postMessage and DOM render. Each of up to 3 workers would also instantiate the wasm (about 35 ms each). Note that the main-thread getSharedHighlighter singleton (shared_highlighter.js:14-19) is shared with ChatMarkdown, so whichever caller comes first fixes its engine. The 10 s-timeout reliability concern is unreproduced. Plausibility: 3 concurrent uncached fetches of 835 KB on a slow, uncompressed remote link; the local server has no compression middleware. Downgraded to medium overall. (a) alone is a clear S win.

Part of Priority 17: Side panels: terminal, diff, files

Expected gain

Client patch memory bounded at about 16 MB instead of the sum of all viewed diffs. Example: 50 turns with a 1 MB conversation diff leaves about 50 MB retained today (estimate).

What happens today

checkpointDiffStateAtom is an Atom.family with keepAlive. watchCheckpointDiff's release only decrements refCount; entries and atom values are never removed (clearCheckpointDiffState runs only on hosted environment reset). The cache key contains toTurnCount and, for the default conversation view, conversation:<every turn id>. Each completed turn while the review panel is open therefore creates a new retained full-thread patch, and the older ones stay alive. Patches can reach 10,000,000 B (server cap).

Proposal

Evict inactive entries with an LRU and byte budget, using lib/lruCache.ts like DiffParseCache does. When refCount reaches 0, keep at most 8 inactive entries or 16 MB, reset evicted atoms to IDLE and delete them from checkpointDiffEntries/checkpointDiffKeysByThread. When a thread's conversation key changes, drop the superseded conversation entry immediately. Also evict on thread archive.

Verifier (Confirmed)

checkpointDiffStateAtom is Atom.family plus Atom.keepAlive (providerAtoms.ts:179-185). The watchCheckpointDiff release only decrements refCount (:297-303). invalidateCheckpointDiffEntry with refCount 0 keeps the data (:306-315). Only clearCheckpointDiffState (:336+) clears entries, and it runs only on hosted reset. DiffPanel's conversation cacheScope joins every turnId (DiffPanel.tsx:506-512), so each new turn with the panel open creates and retains another full-range patch, up to 10,000,000 B each (CheckpointStore.ts:22). The 50 MB example is an estimate. Typical patches are smaller, but growth is unbounded.

Prior work

DiffParseCache already bounds parsed payloads at 50 entries (apps/web/src/lib/diffParseCache.ts:35); the raw patch store is not bounded.

Part of Priority 17: Side panels: terminal, diff, files

Expected gain

For users who closed the drawer while a shell keeps running: −1 xterm chunk load (361 KB raw / 91 KiB gzip) and −1 terminal.open (measured 431,900 B with 421 KB history) per reload or reconnect of that thread. Also fixes the drawer unexpectedly reopening and the active split flipping on every reconnect.

What happens today

Closing the drawer only sets terminalOpen=false (ChatView.tsx:2602-2605), and the PTY keeps running. On every WebSocket connect, reload or reconnect, subscribeTerminalEvents replays one type: "started" event per running session across all threads (terminalRpc.ts:214-230). The web sink forwards it to the store (service.ts:851-865). For started/restarted, the store's applyTerminalEvent unconditionally adds the terminal, calls setThreadActiveTerminal(event.terminalId) and setThreadTerminalOpen(true) (store.ts:747-757). That behaviour is intended for genuinely new server-started terminals: terminalStateStore.test.ts covers a 'setup-bootstrap' terminal. Reconciliation accepts the replay because the snapshot cursor is ≥ the last seen cursor, and after a reload the reconciliation state is empty because partialize persists only terminalStateByThreadKey (store.ts:916-918; reconciliation.ts:39-47). Result: a drawer the user closed reopens after every reload or reconnect (laptop wake, relay re-attach). On the current thread, ChatTerminalShell then mounts the drawer during boot (:149-151), loading the 361 KB xterm chunk and issuing terminal.open, which returned 431,900 B of history in the measured reload. With split terminals, the active terminal flips to the last replayed one. listSessions sorts by updatedAt descending (Manager.ts:2305-2313), so that is the least recently updated terminal. Found by code reading, not reproduced in the UI. This replay behaviour also makes any hover or idle terminal prewarm unsafe.

Proposal

Distinguish replay from a real start in the contract: add replay: true to the initial snapshot events in terminalRpc.ts, or emit a separate snapshot event type. In store.applyTerminalEvent, apply replay events only to launch context, running/activity state and the reconciliation cursor, and never call setThreadTerminalOpen or setThreadActiveTerminal. Keep the force-open behaviour for live started/restarted from startSession. Combine this with the metadata-only replay from terminal-history-in-subscription-snapshot: replay events carry no history, and a mounted drawer that sees a replay cursor ahead of its own re-hydrates via terminal.open(sinceCursor). Add a store test asserting that a replayed started event leaves terminalOpen=false unchanged.

None. The Aug hardening (performance-hardening-results.md:85) bounded event buffers but did not address replay semantics.

Part of Priority 17: Side panels: terminal, diff, files

Expected gain

Non-diff modes (terminal, files, launcher, agents, simulator) stop spawning 3 workers: about 9 MB of worker heap and script copies, 3 isolates, and 51 ms (1x) to 230-320 ms (4x) of worker CPU per open (measured components). Reopening review keeps warm grammars and caches, saving about 240 ms of first highlight (measured) plus re-highlighting of every visible file.

What happens today

LazyRightPanel wraps every mode in DiffWorkerPoolProvider (ChatRightPanel.tsx:83). WorkerPoolContextProvider creates the singleton in a useState initializer. Its constructor calls queueInitialization (WorkerPoolManager.js:70), which spawns poolSize workers (min(3, floor(cores/3)) = 3 here) and loads the theme. Measured: opening the launcher created 3 workers at 55 ms (initialized at 72 ms). Opening straight into terminal mode created 3 workers at 578 ms of boot. Each idle worker holds ~1.36 MB used / ~2.2 MB JS heap plus an 835 KB script copy. At 4x CPU, init is 77-107 ms per worker plus a ~60 ms main-thread long task. Only review (DiffPanel FileDiff) and the PR tab (FilesTab, which already has its own provider) use the pool. Files mode opens text in the edit-mode editor, which tokenizes on the main thread: 0 worker messages measured. The provider's effect cleanup terminates the singleton when the panel unmounts (useDelayedUnmount 360 ms) and clears the AST caches (WorkerPoolManager.js:468-485). Measured: close terminated all 3 workers; reopen created 3 new ones, so compiled grammars and highlight caches are rebuilt every time. Even for a 2-file diff, only 1 of the 3 workers did any work.

Proposal

1) Remove DiffWorkerPoolProvider from LazyRightPanel. Wrap only the review branch in ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:1455-1456 (<DiffPanel>) and WorkspacePullRequestPanel; FilesTab already wraps itself. 2) Replace unmount-terminate with an app-lifetime owner. Add apps/web/src/lib/diffWorkerPool.ts with acquire()/release() ref-counting around getOrCreateWorkerPoolSingleton and render WorkerPoolContext.Provider directly. Terminate only after an idle grace (e.g. 3 min with no consumers, or when the document stays hidden), not 360 ms after close. Grammars and AST caches then survive panel close, tab switches and thread switches. 3) Default poolSize to 1 and cap MAX at 2, or size from the patch's file count before first acquire. 4) Prewarm: on requestIdleCallback after a thread with turnDiffSummaries renders, or on hover of the review toggle, acquire the pool and call primeFileHighlightCache with a 1-line snippet in the thread's dominant language. This compiles the grammar before the first real diff.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Checked ChatRightPanel.tsx:83 (DiffWorkerPoolProvider wraps every mode, including launcher, terminal, files, simulator, agents and render). WorkerPoolContext.js:9-15 creates the singleton in a useState initializer, and its effect cleanup at :24-28 terminates it once instanceCount reaches 0. The WorkerPoolManager constructor calls queueInitialization (:70). initializeWorkers (:293-352) spawns poolSize workers with a 10 s timeout (:25). terminate() clears the diff and file caches (:468-485). The panel unmounts through useDelayedUnmount(open, 360) at ChatRightPanel.tsx:144-147, gating at :250-251. The only pool consumers are DiffPanel FileDiff, the PR DiffFileSection (FilesTab already has its own provider, FilesTab.tsx:152) and the read-only DiffsFile branch of PreviewPanel (:946-952). That branch is reached only on the phone tier, for mixed line endings or before an edit session exists. Desktop text uses PreviewFileEditor (edit mode), so 'Files never uses the pool' is mostly true but not absolute. ChatMarkdown uses the main-thread getSharedHighlighter, not the pool. Review branch location: ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:1454-1455. Impact correction: most of the measured 51-320 ms is worker-thread CPU, not main-thread latency. The user-visible gain is the memory/CPU reduction (about 6.6 MB measured: 3×(1.36 MB heap + 0.835 MB source), plus isolate overhead) and warm grammars when review is reopened. The 240 ms 'first highlight' saving on reopen is an estimate. With hardwareConcurrency ≤ 8 the pool already has only 1-2 workers. Downgraded to medium.

None. The covered items are the 1.1 MiB ChatRightPanel chunk and the Suspense throttle, not the worker pool.

Part of Priority 17: Side panels: terminal, diff, files

Expected gain

Cold first open: prompt about 1,058 ms → about 650-700 ms (shell startup of 180-640 ms overlaps the 390 ms of chunk and reveal; estimate). With hover prewarm, the prompt is effectively ready at mount. −1 resize RPC per mount (measured 2 → 1).

What happens today

terminal.open runs inside usePaneEffect after new Terminal, open(mount) and fit(), because it needs cols/rows. The server spawns the user's $SHELL (zsh with -o nopromptsp, interactive, not login), so .zshrc time sits on the critical path. Measured cold first open of the drawer: chunk done at 45 ms, terminal.open sent at 389 ms, spawn returned at 402 ms, first prompt bytes at 1,041 ms and visible at 1,058 ms. node-pty spawn-to-prompt in isolation was 182-534 ms; zsh -i -c exit took 0.17-0.43 s. Each mount also sends 2 resize RPCs (30 ms timer at 927-945 plus the rAF effect at 1060-1083) even when dimensions match the open request. On reload with the drawer persisted open, terminal.open fires at 709 ms, 300 ms after the composer is visible.

Proposal

Add a non-xterm module apps/web/src/terminalPrepare.ts with prepareThreadTerminal({threadRef, terminalId, cwd, worktreePath, runtimeEnv}). It calls api.terminal.open with the last-known cols/rows (persist them next to terminalHeight in terminalStateByThreadKey) and memoizes the in-flight promise per (threadKey, terminalId). Call it on drawer-toggle click, the terminal.toggle shortcut, launcher card/tab click and pointerenter, and from ChatTerminalShell before the lazy chunk resolves. The mounted drawer awaits the same promise instead of issuing a second open, then sends a single resize only if fit() changed dimensions. Remove the duplicate 30 ms fitTimer resize. The server's open is already idempotent for live sessions (Manager.ts:2039-2096).

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

Waterfall confirmed. usePaneEffect (ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:426-453) constructs xterm, calls open(mount) and fit(). openTerminal (:866-881) then awaits api.terminal.open with the measured cols/rows. The fitTimer resize (:926-944, 30 ms) and the rAF resize effect (:1059-1082) each send an unconditional resize, so 2 resizes per mount. The server open is idempotent for a live session with the same cwd and env (Manager.ts:2039-2096). Overlapping the spawn with chunk load and reveal on click/shortcut is sound, and the ~650-700 ms estimate is plausible from the measured components. Two problems with the proposal: (1) a hover, pointerenter or idle prepare that spawns a new PTY makes the server publish started. The client store then forces terminalOpen=true and switches the active terminal (packages/client-runtime/src/state/terminal/store.ts:747-757), so hover would pop the drawer open. Only click and shortcut prepares are safe until that is fixed. (2) If the prepare uses a cwd or runtimeEnv different from what the drawer later sends, the server stops the process and wipes its history (Manager.ts:2046-2059). The prepare and the drawer must share one resolver for cwd and env (ChatTerminalShell's projectScriptCwd and projectScriptRuntimeEnv).

The 300 ms Suspense reveal throttle is covered; this overlaps it with the PTY start rather than removing it.

Part of Priority 17: Side panels: terminal, diff, files

Expected gain

Per reopen or tab switch: −432 KB WebSocket traffic (up to 2 MiB) and −68-90 ms long task at 4x CPU (measured); reopen becomes about one frame.

What happens today

PersistentThreadTerminalDrawer returns null when terminalOpen is false, and ThreadWorkspacePanel renders only the active mode, so the cleanup at 1018-1042 calls terminal.dispose(). Reopening sends terminal.open, the server returns snapshot.history in full, and the client writes it with a single terminal.write. Measured with a 421 KB history: 431,712 B per reopen; content visible at 65 ms (1x), and at 247-273 ms with a 68-90 ms long task (JSON decode plus write) at 4x CPU. PTYs keep running server-side, so only the view is discarded.

Proposal

Keep xterm instances alive. Add a module-level LRU of 2-4 entries keyed by (threadKey, terminalId) holding {Terminal, FitAddon, lastCursor}. On unmount, move terminal.element into a detached holder instead of calling dispose(); on remount, append it to the new container, fit, and call terminal.open with the sinceCursor from the history finding, so only events after the cursor are applied. Evict with dispose(). In the right panel, keep an opened terminal tab mounted but hidden (the drawer already supports visible=false via the hidden class) rather than unmounting on tab switch.

Expected gain

−2 to −4 spawns (about 30-55 ms) on every local review, and −13 ms per untracked file (up to about −2.6 s at the 200-file cap). Estimates use measured per-spawn cost.

What happens today

read(): rev-parse --git-path index, then identity() (symbolic-ref + rev-parse HEAD), copy index to a temp file, ls-files --unmerged, diff --cached, diff, ls-files --others, then git diff --no-index -- /dev/null <name> for each untracked file in a loop (≤200), then identity() again. That is 9 sequential spawns plus N. Measured RPC (0 untracked files): 125/96/83 ms, 107 KB. Measured spawn cost 12-14 ms, so 200 untracked files add about 2.6 s (estimate).

Proposal

In the disposable temp index (already a private copy, GIT_INDEX_FILE), run one git add --intent-to-add --pathspec-from-file=- --pathspec-file-nul for all untracked paths. The single diff then emits them as new files and the per-file loop goes away. Read branch and HEAD with one git rev-parse --verify HEAD plus a direct fs read of the HEAD file (the index is already read via fs), halving the identity cost. Keep before/after identity semantics unchanged.

Verifier (Confirmed)

GitIndexReview.read() was verified. The count is actually 10 sequential spawns plus N: authorizeGitReadWorkspace adds rev-parse --show-toplevel (GitReadWorkspace.ts:33-40) before gitPath index (:78-82). identity() runs symbolic-ref and rev-parse HEAD (:95-115) twice (:134 and :180), plus ls-files --unmerged, diff --cached, diff and ls-files --others (:149-161). The default first review open uses the checkpoint diff, so this is not on the default first-open path. Expected gain

What happens today

Measured on first Files open: vscode-icons-*.js (285,084 B, the 336,825 B manifest JSON) was requested at 428 ms, only after listEntries returned, because the first VscodeEntryIcon render starts it. Then https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/vscode-icons/vscode-icons@v12.17.0/icons/file_type_markdown.svg took 128 ms, and each further icon type is another third-party request. The same icons appear in the composer menu, timeline and markdown. Offline, air-gapped or proxied installs show broken icons, and the CDN learns which file types the user opens. That conflicts with the local-assets stance in pdfAttachmentAssets.ts:1-2.

Proposal

Self-host. A build step reads the manifest and emits (1) a slim lookup (extension/fileName/folderName → icon id; estimated 30-60 KiB versus 337 KiB) and (2) the referenced SVGs as Vite assets via import.meta.glob(…, {query: '?url'}), the same pattern pdfAttachmentAssets.ts uses, or as one sprite. These are served by the Ryco server or Vercel with immutable caching. Preload the resolver at idle after the thread route so tree rows render with icons on first paint.

Perf caveat: icons also render in the composer and timeline, so in a typical session the resolver and common SVGs are already loaded and HTTP-cached before Files opens. Part of Priority 17: Side panels: terminal, diff, files

Expected gain

−1 process spawn per second (≈20 ms sys CPU/s, measured) for anyone with a live terminal. Disk writes drop from O(history) per 40 ms to O(chunk) (estimate).

What happens today

While any session is running, pollSubprocessActivity spawns /bin/ps -eo pid=,ppid= every 1,000 ms (DEFAULT_SUBPROCESS_POLL_INTERVAL_MS). Shells keep running after the drawer closes, so this continues for the server's lifetime once any terminal has been opened. Measured: 50.7 ms wall per spawn from Node, 0.03 s real / 0.02 s sys, 1,337 processes. History persistence: every output chunk with visible text calls queuePersist with the entire history string. The keyed coalescing worker sleeps 40 ms and then writeFileString-rewrites the whole file (≤2 MiB). Under continuous output that is about 25 full rewrites per second per terminal (up to about 50 MB/s, estimate). On cold open, readHistory does exists, full read and a split of up to 2 MiB / 5,000 lines, and rewrites the file when it was capped.

Proposal

Detect subprocesses without spawning. node-pty's IPty.process (foreground process via the PTY fd on Unix) or tcgetpgrp(fd) compared with the shell pid answers 'is a child in the foreground'. Otherwise, poll only while a client subscribes to activity and back off to 5 s when nothing changed. For persistence, use an append-only log (fs.appendFile per chunk) with compaction once the file exceeds 1.5× maxBytes and on close or exit, or debounce full rewrites to ≥1 s trailing plus a flush on exit. In readHistory, trim in memory and defer the rewrite to the next compaction.

Verifier (Confirmed)

pollSubprocessActivity (Manager.ts:1861-1934) runs one ps -eo pid=,ppid= per tick (snapshotPosixProcessTable :589-618, 1 s timeout, 512 KiB buffer) while any session is running. Effect.forever with sleep(DEFAULT_SUBPROCESS_POLL_INTERVAL_MS=1000) is at :1936-1941. The drawer toggle never closes the PTY (ChatView.tsx:2602-2605), so polling continues indefinitely. Persist: the output path hands the whole history string to queuePersist (:1518-1525, :1561). The coalescing worker sleeps 40 ms and then writeFileString-rewrites the whole file (:1178-1211). readHistory does exists, full read, cap and conditional rewrite (:1245-1263). The spawn is async (no event-loop block), so the cost is background CPU, battery and disk, not first-open latency. Side issue: on hosts with very large process tables, the 512 KiB ps buffer truncates and logs a warning every second. Using node-pty process (foreground process name) changes semantics (background jobs go undetected). Acceptable, but should be noted.

Prior work

Manager.ts:1872-1874 already collapsed per-session pgrep into one ps per tick, and the Aug report capped buffering (performance-hardening-results.md:85). This proposal removes the tick itself.

Expected gain

About −40 ms per diff open (3 removed spawns × 13.5 ms, measured cost). Cached reopen, reconnect or second client: −84-115 ms of git diff for a 1.5 MB range (measured) plus the process spawns.

What happens today

getTurnDiff runs 2 parallel rev-parse --verify --quiet ref^{commit} calls (hasCheckpointRef), then diffCheckpoints resolves the same two refs again sequentially, then runs git diff --patch --minimal --no-color [--ignore-all-space]. Measured git spawn cost on this machine is about 13.5 ms. Diff of a 1.49 MB range: 84 ms default, 88 ms --minimal, 115 ms with --ignore-all-space (the default for turn diffs). The whole patch (cap 10,000,000 B) goes out in one RPC. Nothing is cached server-side, so a reopen, a second client, or flushProviderInvalidation's invalidateAllCheckpointDiffs re-runs every git process. The default 'conversation' view recomputes 0..N after every new turn.

Proposal

Pass the commit OIDs resolved in CheckpointDiffQuery into diffCheckpoints, and resolve both refs in one spawn (git rev-parse --verify --quiet A^{commit} B^{commit}). Alternatively drop the pre-checks and map git diff's 'bad revision' failure to CheckpointUnavailableError, leaving 1 spawn plus the diff. Add a bounded LRU (e.g. 32 entries / 32 MB) keyed by (cwd, fromOid, toOid, ignoreWhitespace) in CheckpointDiffQuery: checkpoint commits are content-addressed, so entries never go stale.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

Spawn count confirmed. CheckpointDiffQuery.ts:100-112 runs 2 parallel rev-parse calls through hasCheckpointRef (CheckpointStore.ts:195-198 → resolveCheckpointCommit :73-89). diffCheckpoints then resolves both refs again sequentially (:242-243) before git diff --patch --minimal (:262-277). VcsDriverRegistry.resolve is cached, so it adds no spawn. Critical path is 4 steps, of which about 27-40 ms is removable (measured 13.5 ms per spawn). The server LRU benefit is overstated. A same-client reopen does not refetch, because the client keeps every resolved diff forever in keepAlive atoms (providerAtoms.ts:179-185, 293-295). A new turn changes toOid and so always misses. The cache helps only second clients and the flushProviderInvalidation refetch (environments/runtime/service.ts:117-121). Keying by OID, as proposed, is correct: checkpoint refs can be rewritten after a revert, but OIDs cannot.

Expected gain

−10-150 ms main-thread time per Files open or refetch (6.5k entries; about 4x at 25k), measured sort cost. About −35% listEntries payload (estimate).

What happens today

listEntries returns every index entry with path, kind and a redundant parentPath: 757 KiB JSON for this repo's 6,503 entries (measured). The server sorts with plain localeCompare, which collates differently, so the client must re-sort on every data change and refetch using localeCompare(r, undefined, {numeric, sensitivity}) per comparison. Measured in V8: 15-17 ms on presorted input, 167-183 ms on random input, versus 6.3 ms with one hoisted Intl.Collator; at 25k entries, roughly 4x that. A cold index build on this 9.3k-path worktree runs git ls-files (46 ms) plus check-ignore (60 ms). The tree renders collapsed, showing only top-level nodes.

Proposal

Hoist const collator = new Intl.Collator(undefined, {numeric: true, sensitivity: 'base'}) and sort with collator.compare. Better, sort once on the server with the same collator and skip the client sort. Drop parentPath from the wire and derive it client-side. Longer term, back the collapsed tree with the existing per-directory WorkspaceEntries.browse and load children on expand.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

The client sort uses localeCompare with an inline options object per comparison (useProjectPreview.ts:40-50) and repeats it in refetch (:52-66). The server returns all index entries (WorkspaceEntries.ts:800-812, cap 25,000 at :29) including the optional parentPath (contracts project.ts:46-50). However, the server already sorts with localeCompare (WorkspaceEntries.ts:374, 382), so the client input is nearly presorted. The investigator's own sort-bench.txt shows 14.6-17.3 ms presorted versus 167-183 ms random, so the realistic saving at 6.5k entries is about 10-15 ms per open/refetch, not up to 150 ms. JSON.parse plus decode measured only 0.7-1.7 ms warm, so the payload gain is mostly transfer bytes.

What happens today

Images render only when richSelectedFileData.base64 is set. Files are read through projects.readFile, whose result contract has no base64, and the server rejects binary content with 'Binary files cannot be previewed.' Selecting a PNG therefore shows a refresh error instead of the image. projects.readFileBinary (4 MiB limit, MIME sniffing, dataBase64) exists and is used by ChatMarkdown and DiffImagePreview. The 512 KiB size guard reads sizeBytes and mimeType, which ProjectEntry never carries, so every click fetches and lets the server reject oversized files. Found by code reading, not reproduced in the UI.
