When detectPreviewFileKind(path) === 'image', use a projectReadFileBinary query and render through URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([decoded bytes], {type: mimeType})), revoking on change; this avoids multi-MB data: URL string copies. Remove the RichPreviewFileData casts. Either add sizeBytes to listEntries or delete the dead guard.

Expected gain

−6-15 ms per diff render at 1x and about −25-60 ms at 4x CPU (from measured Bun numbers); no re-parse on theme toggle.

What happens today

The renderableContent useMemo hashes the full patch twice (FNV over every character), splits it into files, hashes each segment, runs parsePatchFiles and sorts. diffSearchIndex is then built from every line on every patch change. parseScope includes resolvedTheme, so a theme toggle re-parses a patch whose parse does not depend on theme. Measured in Bun/JSC on real patches: 773 KiB / 553 files: key 2.5-9.6 ms, parse 10-20 ms, index 1.7-4.9 ms. 1.9 MiB / 791 files: key 5.5, parse 24.7, sort 1.9, index 5.8 ms, about 38 ms per pass.

Proposal

Build the search index lazily, only once the search input opens. Remove resolvedTheme from parseScope. Use a server-provided revision (from/to OIDs for checkpoint diffs, revision for local changes, which already exists) as the cache key instead of hashing multi-MB strings. For patches over 1 MB, parse in an idle slice or in the diff worker, which already bundles @pierre/diffs.

Correction: the memo runs per patch change, theme change or scope change, not 'per diff render', so the savings (measured in Bun: about 2-6 ms key and 2-6 ms index on 0.8-1.9 MiB patches) apply once per patch arrival. Composer @ and # menus 13 findings · 3 high · 3 medium · 7 low

The @-mention index has a 15 s TTL counted from build time, blocks on rebuilds (210 ms here, 0.7–0.9 s at 60k files) and is invalidated after every turn. Above 25k entries most files cannot be found. The '#' PR list uses the heaviest gh field set (2.2–2.7 s vs 0.6 s lean).

How it works today (investigator's summary)

First '@' in a cold project. Typing a bare '@' sends no request, because the client gates on a non-empty query (projectAtoms.ts:123-139) and the contract requires TrimmedNonEmptyString (project.ts:37-41). The menu therefore shows "No matching files or folders." After the first character and a 120 ms debounce (ComposerAttachmentMenus.tsx:35,83-87), projects.searchEntries reaches WorkspaceEntries.search. On a cache miss, buildWorkspaceIndexFromVcs runs these steps in order:

  • vcsRegistry.detect: 3 rev-parse calls plus an uncached walk up to the filesystem root looking for .ryco/vcs.json.
  • git ls-files -co --exclude-standard (20 s timeout).
  • K chunks of git check-ignore --no-index --stdin, one after another (K = ceil(bytes/256 KiB)).
  • About 100 ms of synchronous ancestor/sort work on the server event loop for a 60k-file repo.
  • Truncation to 25,000 entries, applied after the alphabetical sort.

Measured child processes: 6 for this monorepo (K=2), 18 for a 60k-file synthetic repo (K=14). The real WorkspaceEntries layer, driven through Node type-stripping, took 210 ms cold here and 785-875 ms cold at 60k. Warm searches took 1.5-12 ms. After 16 s idle the 15 s TTL expired and the next query blocked on a full rebuild (705 ms at 60k). There is no stale-while-revalidate, and the index is also invalidated after every agent turn (CheckpointReactor.ts:430,966). Per-keystroke scoring is cheap (2-9 ms over 25k entries), and each response is about 9-12 KB on the wire. The real problems are cold and post-expiry rebuilds, the redundant check-ignore pass, truncation hiding most of a large repo's files, and errors being shown as "no matches".

'#' issue/PR references. The composer fetches open issues and open PRs (limit 50, filtered locally, no per-keystroke network calls). The PR list uses the heaviest GitHub field set: comments, statusCheckRollup, additions/deletions/changedFiles and mergeable, followed by a stack-summary GraphQL call. On this repo (16 open PRs) that gh pr list took 2.2-2.7 s and 278 KB; a lean field set took 0.62-0.69 s and 5.6 KB. Because cache keys include the limit (20, 50, default and 100 across surfaces), different views make duplicate gh calls. Every list or search read also starts a project-wide sweep of linked worktrees with unbounded detached gh calls. The ContextPicker, Issues/PR tabs and work-item searches are already local-first, debounced 200 ms and need at least 2 characters; each server fall-through is one gh/Jira call (gh measured 0.55-0.83 s) with no cancellation.

Skills and slash commands come from the provider snapshot. There is no per-keystroke discovery, and the editor's derived maps are memoized by the React compiler (checked in the built ChatRightPanel chunk). However, they are probed at the server's process.cwd(), so project-scoped skills and commands are missing. The first model-picker open makes no RPC, refresh or probe; its only side cost is a global flag that re-renders the Sidebar.

Part of Priority 18: Composer @-mentions and # references

Expected gain

Removes the measured 210 ms (this repo) / 705-875 ms (60k files) from every '@' after more than 15 s idle and after every agent turn. The warm path is unchanged (1.5-12 ms).

What happens today

The index lives in Cache.makeWith with timeToLive 15 s and capacity 4. Once an entry expires, Cache.get makes the caller wait for a full rebuild; stale data is never served. Measured with the real layer: after 16 s idle, query 'comp' took 704.6 ms on a 60k-file repo, against 3-12 ms warm. Cold on this monorepo is 210.5 ms. invalidate() drops the entry after every turn's checkpoint capture (CheckpointReactor.ts:430), after reverts (:966) and after file writes (WorkspaceFileSystem.ts:592/647). So the first '@' after any agent turn is always a cold rebuild: 3 rev-parse + ls-files + K check-ignore processes. search and listEntries share the 4 keys, and each worktree cwd is its own key. With more than 4 active worktrees the LRU churns and every switch rebuilds.

Proposal

Replace Cache.makeWith with a small stale-while-revalidate store: Map<normalizedCwd,{index,builtAt,lastReadAt,dirty,inflight}>.

  • Reads return the current index immediately.
  • If the entry is dirty or older than the TTL and nothing is in flight, fork a single-flight rebuild (global limit of 1-2 concurrent builds).
  • invalidate() marks the entry dirty. If it was read in the last ~10 min, schedule a debounced (~250 ms) background rebuild instead of evicting.
  • After WorkspaceFileSystem writes, patch the index in place (insert or remove one path) so the new file shows up instantly without a rebuild.
  • Revalidation: on macOS and Windows, use one recursive fs.watch per hot root (ignoring .git internals other than index/HEAD, and IGNORED_DIRECTORY_NAMES) to mark entries dirty. On Linux, stat .git/index and HEAD mtimes (2 syscalls) on read.
  • Replace 'capacity 4' with an entry budget (e.g. at most 200k entries total, LRU by lastReadAt), so multi-worktree users keep warm indexes.
Verifier (Confirmed)

Checked WorkspaceEntries.ts:27-29 and 529-536 (Cache.makeWith, capacity 4, TTL 15 s on success and 0 on failure), invalidate at 554-564, and the call sites CheckpointReactor.ts:430 (right after captureCheckpoint) and :966 (after restore), and WorkspaceFileSystem.ts:592/647.

Effect 4.0.2 Cache.get (node_modules/.bun/effect@4.0.2/.../Cache.ts:430+) only moves the entry for LRU on a hit. It never extends expiresAt, and expired entries go through a blocking lookup. The TTL therefore runs from build time, not from idle time. Even while the user is typing, the first keystroke more than 15 s after a build blocks on a full rebuild. That is worse than the 'after 16 s idle' framing.

I reproduced the cold pipeline with .perf-research/gap-composer-pickers/index-build.mjs on this worktree: 191-216 ms total (7 processes now, K=3, because .perf-research/ untracked files are included).

One correction: 'the first @ after any agent turn is always cold' is not strictly true. After a thread.turn-diff-completed, the client force-refetches the last '@' query of every mounted composer scope (see the additional finding), which rebuilds the index in the background. Because the TTL is 15 s from build, any '@' typed later than that is cold again, so the conclusion mostly holds.

Proposal caveat: the Linux revalidation (.git/index and HEAD mtimes) cannot detect new untracked files, so it must be combined with a background revalidation on TTL. Prior perf docs do not cover stale-while-revalidate.

Prior work

The Aug 2026 hardening pass (docs/research/2026-08-12-performance-hardening-results.md, 'caches ... have explicit capacities and eviction behavior') introduced the explicit bound. Stale-while-revalidate, rebuild-on-invalidate, file watching and an entry budget are not covered anywhere, and this is not on the EVIDENCE covered list.

Part of Priority 18: Composer @-mentions and # references

Expected gain

First '#' PR section: about 2.2-2.7 s down to about 0.6-0.7 s on this repo (measured gh), plus one fewer GraphQL call. Saves 1-3 duplicate gh calls (0.6-2.7 s each) when moving between the composer, overview and PR tabs. The chip appears instantly instead of after about 1 s.

What happens today

The first '#' requests listIssues and listChangeRequests (state open, limit 50). The menu only uses number, title and state.

  • On the server, listChangeRequests uses GITHUB_PULL_REQUEST_LIST_JSON_FIELDS: every PR's comments (METADATA, GitHubCli.ts:80-89), statusCheckRollup, additions/deletions/changedFiles and mergeable. It then runs enrichChangeRequestsWithStacks, which adds more gh api graphql batches (concurrency 2).
  • Measured on this repo (16 open PRs): this field set took 2,227-2,695 ms and 278,465 B. A picker field set took 624-691 ms and 5,573 B (3.5x faster, 50x smaller), before counting the stack call.
  • listIssues also requests comments only to compute a count (gitHubIssues.ts:129-133).
  • Cache keys include the limit (sourceControlAtoms.ts:270-271, 300-301). The open-PR list is requested with limit 20 (ProjectOverviewTab), 50 (composer, branch selector, overview), no limit (ContextPickerPopup; server default 20) and 100 (PullRequestsTab, CreatePullRequestDialog). That is up to 4 separate gh calls for the same list.
  • Choosing an item waits for full detail before the chip appears. gh pr view with DETAIL fields measured 996-1,118 ms vs 483-535 ms lean.
Proposal

(a) Add a view: "picker" option to listIssues/listChangeRequests (contracts rpc.ts ~1093-1141). It should use a lean JSON field set (number,title,url,state,isDraft,updatedAt,author,headRefName,baseRefName) with includeStackSummary:false. Use it from ComposerAttachmentMenus and ContextPickerPopup.

(b) Canonicalize list fetching to one superset per (cwd,state,involvement), e.g. limit 100. Derive smaller views by slicing on the client: the binding resolves a limit-50 request to a fresh superset key when one exists.

(c) Drop comments from list queries, or fetch comments{totalCount} via GraphQL.

(d) When a '#' item is selected, add the chip immediately from the summary and fetch detail in the background (the detail cache already lasts 5 min).

Verifier (Confirmed)

Verified the composer requests issue and PR lists with state open, limit 50 (ComposerAttachmentMenus.tsx:99-112). The server uses GITHUB_PULL_REQUEST_LIST_JSON_FIELDS (GitHubCli.ts:99-109, including comments, statusCheckRollup, additions/deletions/changedFiles and mergeable), then enrichChangeRequestsWithStacks (GitHubSourceControlProvider.ts:348-408, GraphQL, concurrency 2) because the RPC handler never passes includeStackSummary:false. There is no server-side list cache (listFromHostingProvider, sourceControlRpc.ts:196-213).

Re-measured on this repo (16 open PRs): full field set 1,969-2,150 ms and 278,465 B; lean field set 652-930 ms and 5,573 B. This matches the claim.

listIssues requests comments only for a count (GitHubCli.ts:2589-2600, gitHubIssues.ts:129-133). On selection, the detail fetch is awaited before addSourceControlContext (ComposerAttachmentMenus.tsx:305-375).

Corrections:

  • The binding is at sourceControlAtoms.ts:258-311, with the keys at 266-267 and 300-301.
  • ProjectOverviewTab uses PROJECT_OVERVIEW_LIST_LIMIT=20 for PRs, not 50.
  • ContextPickerPopup passes no limit, so the server default is 20. That is the same gh call as the overview under a different client key.
  • Distinct open-PR keys: 20 / '' / 50 / 100. Of these, ''/20 make the identical gh call.

Proposal (a), a separate picker view, adds another key variant and is in tension with (b), canonicalization. Pick one superset shape.

Prior work

.perf-research/projects-loading/gh-fields.txt measured lean vs full for a per-branch PR list (~1.0 s -> ~0.6 s). This finding is the repo-wide open-PR list used by the composer '#' and the context picker (comments + statusCheckRollup + stack GraphQL), plus the limit-fragmented cache keys, which are not covered. EVIDENCE only covers gh/glab auth checks on composer mount.

Part of Priority 18: Composer @-mentions and # references

Expected gain

Fixes missing results for repos above about 20k files (66% of files unreachable in the 60k test). Adds about 5-15 MB of memory per large hot index.

What happens today

The VCS index is built as all directories sorted, then all files sorted, then .slice(0, 25_000). search() scores only that truncated array. Measured with the real layer on a 60,410-file repo: the index holds 4,630 dirs and 20,370 files, and the last file is copy3/apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts. The full path of copy9/.../ChatComposer.tsx returns no results while the copy1 file is found, so about 66% of files cannot be reached by any query. Directories always take the first slots. The filesystem fallback truncates in BFS order instead (499-501), which is inconsistent. ls-files output is also silently capped at 16 MiB (truncateOutputAtMaxBytes). The client ignores truncated, so the user gets no hint.

Proposal
  • Separate the corpus cap from the payload cap. Keep the full path list for search, stored compactly (lowercase NUL-joined buffer plus offsets, or plain string arrays; 60k paths is about 3.5 MB). Cap only listEntries/browse payloads.
  • If a hard cap is still needed (e.g. 300k paths), keep tracked files before untracked and shallower paths before deeper ones, not alphabetical order.
  • Raise the ls-files byte cap accordingly.
  • Return and render truncated ('Showing results from part of the workspace').
Verifier (Confirmed)

Verified WorkspaceEntries.ts:373-396: directories are sorted, then files are sorted with localeCompare, then [...dirs, ...files].slice(0, 25_000). search() (765-797) iterates only index.entries. The filesystem fallback truncates in BFS order (499-501), and ls-files is capped at 16 MiB with truncateOutputAtMaxBytes (GitVcsDriver.ts:249, 446-451).

ComposerAttachmentMenus.tsx:96 reads only data.entries; truncated is never shown.

The synthetic-repo result is consistent with the alphabetical cut (copy1, copy10, copy2, then part of copy3 kept, about 66% of files unreachable). I did not rebuild the 60k repo, to avoid polluting the shared worktree.

This is a correctness bug for repos above about 25k entries (directories count against the cap first). The 2026-07-27 relay framing plan only treats 25k as a listEntries payload problem.

Prior work

docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-relay-oversized-rpc-framing.md discusses the 25k cap only as a listEntries payload-size problem. Search correctness is not covered.

Category: Process spawnsRisk: lowInvestigator confidence: highRating changed by verifier: impact high → medium, effort S → Sgap-composer-pickers:check-ignore-redundant

Part of Priority 18: Composer @-mentions and # references

Expected gain

Cold '@': -60 to -70 ms (about 35%) on this repo; -330 to -360 ms (about 55%) and 16 fewer git processes at 60k files. First results in about 30 ms with the two-phase build.

What happens today

After ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard, the build sends every path through check-ignore --no-index -z --stdin in 256 KiB chunks, one chunk after another, each with a 20 s timeout. Untracked paths from --others --exclude-standard are by definition not ignored. The only paths check-ignore can remove are tracked files that match ignore rules (the contract test 'excludes tracked paths that match ignore rules').

  • Measured with the same commands: this repo K=2, check-ignore 59-72 ms of a 146-194 ms build (6 processes). At 60k files K=14, 348-378 ms of 668-748 ms (18 processes).
  • ls-files -z --cached --ignored --exclude-standard run in parallel returned an identical result in both repos, including a tracked file under a newly ignored directory. Total 45-60 ms here and 221-248 ms at 60k, with 2 processes.
  • If filterIgnoredPaths fails, lines 359-362 re-run the whole K-chunk pass through filterVcsIgnoredPaths on the same driver, doubling the worst case.
  • The ls-files cost is mostly the untracked walk: -c alone took 28-32 ms vs -o 164-209 ms at 60k (21-24 vs 45-52 ms here).
Proposal
  • In GitVcsDriver, make listWorkspaceFiles (or a new listSearchableFiles) run ls-files -z -co --exclude-standard and ls-files -z -ci --exclude-standard concurrently and subtract the second set, which is usually empty or tiny.
  • Remove filterIgnoredPaths from the VCS build path (keep it for the filesystem fallback) and delete the retry at WorkspaceEntries.ts:359-362.
  • Optional two-phase cold build: answer the first query from ls-files -c (about 30 ms even at 60k files), then merge untracked -o results when they arrive (published through the stale-while-revalidate store).
  • Apply IGNORED_DIRECTORY_NAMES at any depth in JS (indexOf scan). Pathspec exclusion inside git was measured 10-30% slower.
Verifier (Confirmed)

Verified listWorkspaceFiles (GitVcsDriver.ts:433-473: ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard, 20 s timeout, 16 MiB truncating cap) and filterIgnoredPaths (515-560: sequential for-loop over 256 KiB chunks, each a check-ignore --no-index with a 20 s timeout).

The retry exists: WorkspaceEntries.ts:359-362 catches the error and calls filterVcsIgnoredPaths, which re-detects and re-runs the same driver.filterIgnoredPaths. The contract test is at WorkspaceEntries.test.ts:220-237.

Re-ran index-build.mjs here: check-ignore x3 sequential took 83-87 ms of a 191-216 ms build. Parallel ls-files -co + ls-files -ci took 51-58 ms with 2 processes and produced an identical set (equal=true). The logic holds: untracked results from --exclude-standard are never ignored, so only tracked-but-ignored paths can be removed, which is exactly what -ci lists.

On this repo the gain is about 70-85 ms (about 35-40%). At 60k files it is the investigator's -330 to -360 ms, which I could not reproduce here. Once stale-while-revalidate moves rebuilds off the critical path, this mainly cuts background cost, so I rate it medium overall.

Prior work

None. The EVIDENCE covered list only includes the 3 rev-parse detection calls and the missing process-wide git concurrency limit.

Part of Priority 18: Composer @-mentions and # references

Expected gain

Hides the 210-875 ms cold build behind the time between typing '@' and the first character plus the debounce (about 150-300 ms + 120 ms), so results appear when the debounce ends. Also removes the misleading empty and error states.

What happens today

With query '' the client returns null from resolveInput (query.length > 0 gate), and the contract requires TrimmedNonEmptyString, even though scoreEntry already handles an empty query (directories first). The menu opens immediately with isLoading=false and renders 'No matching files or folders.'. The index build starts only after the first character and the 120 ms debounce, then costs 210 ms here or 785-875 ms at 60k files (measured), all after the user has committed to a query. The hook reads only .data, .isLoading and .isFetching, never .error. A failed RPC (missing cwd, git failure) therefore also renders 'No matching files or folders.'.

Proposal
  • Allow an empty query in ProjectSearchEntriesInput (or add a fire-and-forget projects.prewarmEntries).
  • When the path trigger opens, request query '' with limit 80. This shows top-level folders straight away and warms the index.
  • Optionally prewarm on composer focus for threads with a gitCwd. With the stale-while-revalidate store this is cheap and single-flight.
  • Show 'Indexing workspace…' while a build is in flight, and an error row with Retry when error is set.
Verifier (Confirmed)

Verified:

  • projectAtoms.ts:123-139 gates on query.length > 0.
  • The contract requires TrimmedNonEmptyString (project.ts:37-41).
  • scoreEntry handles an empty query (WorkspaceEntries.ts:95-98).
  • isComposerMenuLoading is false for an empty query (ComposerAttachmentMenus.tsx:249-255).
  • ComposerCommandMenu.tsx:202-224 renders the empty-state text.
  • The hook never reads .error (96, 249-255).

Additional nuance: the state atom is keyed per (env, cwd, limit), not per query (projectAtoms.ts:100-102, useProject.ts:66). Only the very first bare '@' in a scope shows 'No matching files or folders.'. Later bare '@'s show the previous query's results, which is stale and misleading.

commitError (197-205) keeps the previous data, so an RPC error shows another query's results, or 'No matching…' on first use.

The head-start estimate (time to first character plus 120 ms debounce) is plausible. It fully hides the build on this repo (about 200 ms) and partially hides it at 60k.

Part of Priority 18: Composer @-mentions and # references

Expected gain

About 90 ms less event-loop blocking per cold build at 60k files (about 10 ms here). Other sessions' streams stay responsive during indexing.

What happens today

In a CPU profile of the real cold build (60k files), WorkspaceEntries.ts self time is 127 ms:

  • isPathInIgnoredDirectory 45 ms. It splits the whole path for every file and every ancestor directory. The ancestor check at 366-368 is redundant: ancestors share the first segment already checked at 358.
  • directoryAncestorsOf 34 ms (split/slice/join per ancestor, O(depth^2)).
  • buildWorkspaceIndexFromVcs body 18 ms.
  • Two localeCompare sorts over all 65k entries, run before slicing to 25k.

The measured event-loop stall was 102-128 ms; WebSocket streams of other threads wait behind it. A single-pass ancestor walk (lastIndexOf, stopping at the first known parent) produced the same 4,631 dirs in 10.1 ms instead of 92.0 ms. The default code-unit sort took 4 ms instead of 17-20 ms.

Proposal

Rewrite lines 356-396 as one pass:

  • Get the first segment via indexOf.
  • Build ancestors with lastIndexOf and break when the parent is already in the set.
  • Drop the redundant ancestor ignore check.
  • Sort with a code-unit comparator, or a cached Intl.Collator if locale order is required, and only sort what is kept.

For very large repos, build in a worker_thread or yield every ~5k entries.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Verified isPathInIgnoredDirectory and directoryAncestorsOf (WorkspaceEntries.ts:130-145) and the synchronous block at 356-396. The ancestor ignore check at 366-368 is provably redundant: every ancestor shares the first segment that was already checked at 358.

I benchmarked the same code on 60,410 synthetic paths (10 copies of this repo's tracked list, pure JS):

  • filter 11-16 ms
  • ancestors 75-80 ms
  • localeCompare sorts 10-24 ms
  • map 8-11 ms
  • total 104-127 ms, synchronous

An optimized lastIndexOf walk with early break took 7.5-11 ms and produced the identical 4,630 dirs. A code-unit sort took 3-4.5 ms. On this repo the investigator measured 16-24 ms in total, so the gain is only meaningful for large repos.

Risk note: a code-unit sort changes listEntries order versus localeCompare. Check the explorer consumers.

This gets more relevant if stale-while-revalidate and the post-turn refetch make rebuilds more frequent.

Low impactEffort S◐ Partially confirmedA slow or failing git ls-files waits 20 s, then silently falls back to a whole-tree filesystem walk that runs check-ignore at every levelBounds worst-case '@' latency from over 20 s (unbounded with retries) to the deadline (≤5 s), and avoids an expensive tree walk on already slow volumes.
Category: ReliabilityRisk: lowInvestigator confidence: mediumRating changed by verifier: impact medium → low, effort S → Sgap-composer-pickers:ls-files-timeout-fallback
Expected gain

Bounds worst-case '@' latency from over 20 s (unbounded with retries) to the deadline (≤5 s), and avoids an expensive tree walk on already slow volumes.

What happens today

ls-files has a 20 s timeout. Any failure or timeout maps to null, which sends buildWorkspaceIndex to buildWorkspaceIndexFromFilesystem. Because the cwd is inside a work tree (431), every BFS level runs filterVcsIgnoredPaths: detect plus K check-ignore chunks, each with its own 20 s timeout. In the VCS path, a check-ignore failure re-runs all chunks once (359-362). The worst case is 20 s + Kx20 s (+retry) before the first result. Slow disks, network or cloud volumes and huge untracked trees are the likely triggers, and the fallback walk is heaviest exactly there. Meanwhile the menu shows 'Searching workspace files...', and any final failure renders as 'No matching files or folders.' (see prewarm-on-at). Failures are not cached (TTL 0 on failure), so every keystroke retries the whole thing.

Proposal
  • Give the build an overall deadline (e.g. 3-5 s).
  • On timeout, return a degraded tracked-only index (ls-files -c, measured 28-32 ms at 60k files) flagged partial, and complete it in the background.
  • Never fall back to a full readdir walk for paths inside a git work tree. Keep the walk for non-VCS folders.
  • Run check-ignore at most once (or not at all, per check-ignore-redundant).
  • Cache failures briefly (e.g. 5 s) so keystrokes don't stampede.
  • Emit a metric or log on timeout and surface the partial/error state in the menu.
Verifier (Partially confirmed)

The code path is real:

  • ls-files has a 20 s timeout (GitVcsDriver.ts:446-451; VcsProcess uses timeoutOption and fails).
  • A failure maps to null (WorkspaceEntries.ts:348-354), which leads to buildWorkspaceIndexFromFilesystem.
  • Inside a work tree, every BFS level runs filterVcsIgnoredPaths with chunked check-ignore (428-517).

Two claims are overstated:

(1) Effect Cache.get shares an in-flight lookup for the same key, so keystrokes during a slow build join it. There is no per-keystroke stampede while the build runs.

(2) The filesystem fallback normally succeeds (only a root readdir failure fails the build), so its result is cached for the full 15 s. 'Every keystroke retries' only applies to total failures.

Triggers (ls-files over 20 s) are rare: network volumes, huge non-ignored untracked trees. An overall deadline plus a tracked-only degraded index is still a sensible bound.

Expected gain

Bounded memory, versus an estimated ~10-30 KB retained forever per typed prefix. Zero-RTT updates for narrowing keystrokes (saves 120 ms debounce + RTT each). Large win over the hosted relay, where every keystroke is a relay round trip (not measured).

What happens today

ScopeRuntime.cache is a plain Map<query,{result,fetchedAt}>. Every response is stored (231) and only cleared by invalidateProjectSearchEntries or clearProjectAtomState, so it grows with every distinct prefix typed over the app's lifetime. The shared keyed queries, by contrast, are capped at 256/512 entries since the Aug pass. Each response is 8.6-11.9 KB on the wire (measured); typing 'composer' issues 8 requests, 75,479 B. Out-of-order responses are ignored by a token check (no cancellation; warm server search costs 1.5-12 ms, so that is acceptable). There is no narrowing: when the previous result had truncated=false, a longer query's matches are a subset (subsequence property), yet it still goes to the server after 120 ms. The project explorer already loads the full index into the client via listEntries (projectPreviewAtoms.ts:112-127), but the composer never reuses it. Ranking 25k entries locally costs 2.3-8.6 ms (measured, shared ranking code). The full path list is 69 KB gzip / 54 KB brotli for this repo, and 143 KB gzip / 47 KB brotli for 25k entries.

Proposal
  • (S) Bound the per-scope cache with the shared LRUCache (e.g. 64 queries or 2 MB) and drop entries older than staleTime.
  • (S) Local narrowing: if the cached result for any prefix of the current query has truncated=false, rank it locally with @ryco/shared/searchRanking and skip the RPC and the debounce.
  • (M) When listEntries data for the same environment and cwd is in the client cache, or the connection is a hosted relay, search locally (in a worker above 25k entries) and cut the debounce to 0-30 ms. Keep the server path as a fallback and push invalidation from the server when its index changes.
Verifier (Partially confirmed)

ScopeRuntime.cache is a plain Map (projectAtoms.ts:59-73), filled at 231 and never size-bounded. However, invalidateProjectSearchEntries() is called with no filter from flushProviderInvalidation (environments/runtime/service.ts:118-121) on every thread.turn-diff-completed or thread.reverted detail event (orchestrationEventEffects.ts:24-29). That clears every scope's cache, so growth is bounded to the queries typed between turns. 'Retained forever' is overstated.

The local-narrowing idea is valid, but the precondition is narrow. Server search sets truncated=true whenever matchedEntryCount > limit (80) (WorkspaceEntries.ts:791-794), so narrowing only applies once a prefix has 80 or fewer matches. Short prefixes always go to the server.

The relay benefit is not measured. Low impact.

Prior work

The Aug pass bounded the shared keyed-query registries. projectAtoms' custom scope runtime was not included. The relay framing plan (2026-07-27) covers the listEntries size limit only.

Expected gain

Removes about N open() calls per browse (211 in a typical source dir) and prevents unintended iCloud/Dropbox hydration.

What happens today

On macOS, filesystem.browse keeps every regular file whose name matches the prefix (all of them right after a '/'). It stat()s each one and does open()+read(4)+close on every file between 4 B and 64 KiB, only to detect Finder bookmark aliases. Measured: browsing apps/web/src/components/chat issued 214 stat + 211 open per request (4.7-9.6 ms locally); apps/web/src issued 180 stat + 178 open. In File Provider locations (~/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox, where this user keeps projects), reading the bytes of an online-only file makes macOS download it. Browsing a folder can therefore pull many files over the network and stall the picker.

Proposal
  • From the stat already taken, skip dataless files (stats.blocks === 0 && stats.size > 0).
  • Skip names with obvious content extensions (.ts/.js/.json/.md/.png, …). Finder aliases normally have no extension or end in ' alias'.
  • Cache probe results per (dir, name, mtime).
  • Only probe when the directory has fewer than about 500 candidates, or move probing behind an explicit 'show aliases' action.
Verifier (Partially confirmed)

The code matches the claim:

  • On darwin, every regular file matching the prefix is a candidate (WorkspaceEntries.ts:657-667).
  • isMacOSBookmarkAlias calls stat, then open+read(4) for sizes between 4 B and 64 KiB (220-241).
  • Concurrency is 16.

Scope correction: filesystem.browse is not used by the composer '@' menu (that uses searchEntries). Its consumers are CommandPaletteDialog (add-project folder browser, with parent-path prefetch at :798-815) and PromoteChatDialog. That is a folder picker which usually browses directories of project folders, not source directories.

The dataless-file hydration risk in CloudStorage/Dropbox is plausible but not demonstrated. Skipping when stats.blocks===0 is a cheap guard.

Part of Priority 18: Composer @-mentions and # references

Expected gain

Estimated: removes one full index rebuild (7 git processes and about 200 ms here; about 18 processes, 0.7-0.9 s and a 100 ms event-loop stall at 60k files) plus a 9-12 KB response per turn completion on subscribed threads, for users who have used '@' at least once in the mounted composer.

What happens today

Trace of what happens today:

  • A thread.turn-diff-completed or thread.reverted detail event sets needsProviderInvalidation (orchestrationEventEffects.ts:24-29).
  • After a 100 ms trailing throttle, flushProviderInvalidation calls invalidateProjectSearchEntries() with no environment or cwd filter (service.ts:118-121).
  • That clears every scope cache. For every scope with observerCount > 0 and a lastInput, it calls requestProjectSearchEntries(lastInput, {force:true}) (projectAtoms.ts:329-332).
  • useProjectSearchEntries retains the scope whenever environmentId and cwd are non-null, regardless of enabled (useProject.ts:42-53). So once the user has typed any '@' query in a composer scope, every later turn completion on any subscribed thread re-sends that stale query with the menu closed.
  • On the server, CheckpointReactor.ts:430 has just invalidated the index for a turn in the same cwd, before dispatching thread.turn.diff.complete. For other cwds the 15 s TTL (counted from build) has usually expired. Either way the refetch triggers a full rebuild: 3 rev-parse + ls-files + K check-ignore.

Measured cost of one rebuild: 191-216 ms and 7 git processes on this repo (index-build.mjs). The investigator measured 700-875 ms, 18 processes and a 100-130 ms synchronous block at 60k files (the synchronous part I re-benchmarked at 104-127 ms). The response (about 9-12 KB) is discarded unless the menu reopens within the client staleTime. It also serves as an accidental prewarm, but that only helps an '@' typed within 15 s of the rebuild.

Proposal
  • Scope the invalidation to the event's environment and the thread's cwd. The thread to cwd mapping is available in the client thread store.
  • For retained scopes whose path menu is not open, only drop the cache and mark it stale. Do not force a refetch; refetch the next time the trigger opens.
  • Let the server own rebuild timing. With the stale-while-revalidate store from workspace-index-swr, invalidate() marks the entry dirty and schedules one debounced background rebuild only if the cwd was read recently. The client then never needs to drive rebuilds via forced searches.

This finding was added by the adversarial verifier while checking the investigator's report. It has not been verified a second time.

Prior work

None. Not in EVIDENCE.md or the Aug hardening doc. It interacts with the investigator's workspace-index-swr finding, which assumed post-turn '@' is always cold.

Part of Priority 16: Projects and Pull Requests pages

Expected gain

Estimate for 10 linked worktrees: from about 10 concurrent gh pr view calls (0.5-1 s each) plus about 40 git detection processes per '#' open to 1 GraphQL call per sweep.

What happens today

listIssues, searchIssues, listChangeRequests and searchChangeRequests all Effect.tap(refreshLinkedWorktreeSourceControlStates). When cwd is a project root, that resolves every worktree of the project and calls Effect.forkDetach(refresh(id)) in a loop with no concurrency bound, debounced 5 s per project+cwd. Each refresh calls provider.getPullRequestState (one gh pr view) for each open or current link, in sequence. It also runs PR discovery (gitWorkflow.remoteStatus) every 5 min, and resolves the provider for each worktree cwd (3 rev-parse + git remote -v, 5 s cache). So the first '#' in the composer, or opening the Issues tab, spawns about N gh processes plus about 4N git processes for N linked worktrees. These compete with the list the user is waiting for.

Proposal
  • Stop piggybacking sweeps on reads. Let the existing source-control poller or lifecycle hooks own linked-state refresh.
  • If the coupling stays, use Effect.forEach with concurrency 2 instead of forkDetach in a loop.
  • Batch PR state reads for all linked numbers of one repository into a single GraphQL query (aliases p123: pullRequest(number:123){state isDraft closedAt mergedAt}), giving one gh call per repository per sweep.
Verifier (Partially confirmed)

The taps exist on listIssues, searchIssues, listChangeRequests and searchChangeRequests, and the sweep uses forkDetach in a loop with no bound (context.ts:367). Three things are narrower than claimed:

(1) Worktrees with origin 'main', no PR links and no issue are skipped (context.ts:338-349), so the sweep is not 'every worktree'.

(2) The sweep runs in Effect.tap after the list has resolved, so it does not delay that RPC's gh call. It only adds the scope and worktree DB lookups to the response, then forks. When the composer opens with '#', the issues list usually finishes first and its sweep runs alongside the slower PR list.

(3) It is debounced 5 s per project+cwd (constants.ts:2). Discovery is rate-limited to 5 min per worktree for sweeps (refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.ts:54-55). Per-link getPullRequestState calls are sequential within each worktree.

The '~10 gh + ~40 git per # open' figure is an unmeasured upper bound. Batching PR states into one aliased GraphQL query is a reasonable proposal.

Line corrections: the taps are at sourceControlRpc.ts:318-323, 409-414, 465-470, 494-499.

Expected gain

A correctness fix. Cost is bounded to about one discovery per cwd per 5 min, off the keystroke path.

What happens today

Q4: the composer reads selectedProviderStatus.skills and .slashCommands from the provider snapshot. There is no per-request discovery or decoding on mount or keystroke. Ranking is local (providerSkillSearch: 5 lowercases per skill per keystroke, negligible for about 100 skills). The editor's skillSignature and skillMetadataByName are memoized by the React compiler (verified in the built ChatRightPanel chunk). However, the Codex probe calls skills/list with cwds: [process.cwd()], and the Claude capabilities probe runs the SDK with settingSources ['user','project','local'] and no cwd. Project-scoped skills and commands therefore reflect wherever the server process was started, not the thread's project; for the desktop app that is not a project at all.

Proposal

On the first '$' or '/' trigger for a cwd, discover project-scoped skills and commands lazily. Codex: skills/list with the thread cwd over the running app-server. Claude: read <cwd>/.claude/commands and skills directly, or a cwd-scoped probe. Cache per cwd with stale-while-revalidate (about 5 min) and merge into the global snapshot list on the client. Don't do this eagerly on thread open.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Verified:

  • The Codex probe is called with cwd: process.cwd() (CodexProvider.ts:516-520) and passes cwds:[input.cwd] to skills/list (380-395).
  • The Claude capabilities probe (ClaudeProvider.ts:330-345) uses settingSources ['user','project','local'] with no cwd.
  • Slash commands and skills flow through the global provider snapshot (makeManagedServerProvider.ts:169-172).
  • There is no per-thread or per-cwd discovery anywhere (grep for skills/list and slashCommands).

This is a correctness gap, not a performance cost. The composer path itself is cheap.

C. Dedicated pages and loading projects

Statistics, Projects, Settings, PRs 17 findings · 5 high · 8 medium · 4 low

The time goes to server work. Statistics usage takes 2.5–8.2 s on every open, the Activity tab stalls the whole server for 2.6–8.5 s, and the Projects map runs git status --ignored=traditional per worktree (13 s for 17 worktrees).

How it works today (investigator's summary)

Every dedicated page (Statistics, Projects, Settings, Pull Requests, Command palette) follows the same sequence. The route component calls React.lazy() inside its render (routes/*.tsx), so the page chunk only starts downloading after the route renders. The router has no defaultPreload, no route loaders and no intent preloading; Settings is the only page warmed on idle (SettingsRouteBridge). After the chunk evaluates, the page mounts, and only then do its effects fire the first RPCs. There is no cache across mounts or restarts, so every first open goes chunk, then mount, then data. Statistics and Pull Requests also show the full-screen boot logo ("Ryco is starting") while the chunk loads. The bundle lead in EVIDENCE overstates the client cost: RootAppShell is always loaded first, so the true extra bytes per page (measured) are Statistics 457 KiB raw / 133 KiB gzip (82% of it recharts), Projects 318/111, Pull Requests 1,022/311, Settings 247/87, and Command palette only 54.5/18.9.

The real time goes to server work that is recomputed from scratch on each open and often runs synchronously on the single Node event loop.

  • **Statistics, Usage tab (default):** an extra getConfig round trip per environment, then UsageService.readSummary. On first open after boot it synchronously parses and decodes a 22 MB scan cache. If pricing is older than 24 h it blocks on a 2.75 MB LiteLLM download. It walks about 2,600 transcript files, re-parses changed transcripts (up to ~1 s per 190 MiB active codex file) and aggregates 228.7k records (~160 ms). It then re-serialises and rewrites the full 22 MB cache synchronously on almost every open.
  • **Statistics, Activity tab:** six synchronous node:sqlite queries run inside a transaction on the only DB connection. On the user's 9.2 GB state.sqlite they take ~2.6 s warm and ~8.5 s cold, during which every WebSocket client, provider stream and DB write is stalled. Any DB write invalidates the cached result, so it is recomputed nearly every time.
  • **Projects (map view, default):** one listWorkspaces per checkout. On the server that runs ~9 git processes per worktree, including git status --ignored=traditional, which costs ~0.75–1.2 s per worktree (measured 12.9 s sequential for 17 worktrees). The ryco project has 55 non-main worktrees.
  • **Pull Requests:** three gh list calls of ~1.3–1.7 s each, each followed by a second stack-summary gh call. The authored and review-requested lists wait for git status to report the provider, and every list pulls full comment bodies only to count them.
  • **Settings:** mostly fine. The MCP section fetches twice on open (a hook-dependency bug), and each fetch spawns a fresh codex app-server.

Note: these scripts imported the real repo modules (Node 24 type stripping) and ran SQL read-only against the user's live DB. Only one earlier lead turned out to be a non-issue: palette message search over 32.7k messages takes about 20 ms.

Part of Priority 9: Statistics: memoize, aggregate incrementally, never block the server

Expected gain

Fallback query -1.43 s warm / -1.78 s cold (measured). Tool-use query est. 0.70 s → <50 ms warm and 4.69 s → <0.2 s cold. JS -40-130 ms. All of this is synchronous event-loop time today.

What happens today

The fallback branch of listTokenActivityRows compares json_extract(e.payload_json,'$.activity.id') = a.activity_id and ... = a.created_at. The TEXT affinity of the column operands stops SQLite from using the expression columns of idx_orch_events_statistics_usage. EXPLAIN shows SEARCH e USING INDEX idx_orch_events_statistics_usage (stream_id=?) only, so each of the 98,567 context activities rescans its thread's events and re-extracts JSON from the table: 1.67 s warm / 2.10 s cold on the user's live 9.2 GB DB. With +a.activity_id and +a.created_at (affinity stripped), EXPLAIN uses all three index columns and the same query takes 0.24 s warm / 0.32 s cold with an identical result. listToolUseRows (WHERE kind='tool.completed' GROUP BY thread_id, substr(created_at,1,10)) has no usable index on kind. It walks all 560,773 activity rows (large payload_json rows) through idx_..._thread_sequence plus a temp b-tree: 0.70 s warm / 4.69 s cold.

Proposal

1. In StatisticsQuery.ts:268-269 write = +a.activity_id and = +a.created_at. Values are TEXT on both sides, so semantics are unchanged. Add a test that runs EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN and asserts the <expr>=? AND <expr>=? search.

2. Add a migration with a partial covering index CREATE INDEX idx_projection_thread_activities_tool_completed_day ON projection_thread_activities(thread_id, substr(created_at,1,10)) WHERE kind = 'tool.completed'. The GROUP BY then reads ~117k small index entries instead of 560k table rows.

3. Parse each payloadJson once: StatisticsQuery.ts:503/513/525/538 re-parse the same rows in up to four loops. Keep the parsed object next to the row; each extra pass costs 41-46 ms measured.

Verifier (Confirmed)

I re-ran EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN read-only on the live 9.29 GB state.sqlite (sqlite3 3.54).

  • Original NOT EXISTS: SEARCH e USING INDEX idx_orch_events_statistics_usage (stream_id=?).
  • With +a.activity_id/+a.created_at: (stream_id=? AND <expr>=? AND <expr>=?).
  • Timed: original 5.40 s (colder run), + variant 0.31 s. Both return 0 rows, so on this DB the fallback branch contributes nothing yet costs seconds.
  • Tool-use query: SCAN ... USING INDEX idx_projection_thread_activities_thread_sequence + USE TEMP B-TREE FOR GROUP BY, 3.24 s semi-cold. Activities: 565,009 rows, 117,493 tool.completed, 98,567 context-window.updated.
  • The JS re-parse loops at StatisticsQuery.ts:503/513/525/538 are as described.

Addition: the outer SCAN a for kind='context-window.updated' in the fallback also has no kind index. The proposed partial index should cover that kind too, or use a second partial index.

Prior work

Migration 071 added the partial index specifically for this query but it is not used for the correlated lookup; performance-efficiency-size-improvements.md only says 'tune query/index shape' generically.

Part of Priority 9: Statistics: memoize, aggregate incrementally, never block the server

Expected gain

Fixes silently truncated 90d/all usage for codex today. Avoids a future multi-second, partial first open after every boot (est. +5-10 s per source once the cap is crossed).

What happens today

SOURCE_SCAN_RECORDS = 100,000 is meant to bound parse work, but scannedRecords is incremented for reused cache records too (UsageService.ts:612, 624). This user has 131,505 codex records cached, so any 90d/all request stops adding records at 100k and marks the source partial: Statistics silently under-reports. Separately, decodeUsageScanCache skips any file whose records would push the decoded total past 250,000 (usageScanCache.ts:198). The cache holds 228,700 records and grows ~7k/day (Oct: 76.9k in 11 days), so within ~3 days every boot will drop the newest files from the decoded cache. The first Statistics open then has to re-parse them (GBs of codex transcripts at ~170-350 MiB/s), which hits SOURCE_SCAN_DURATION_MS (5 s per source) and returns partial data. The re-persisted cache is again over the cap, so this repeats on every boot.

Proposal

1. Count only freshly parsed bytes/records toward SOURCE_SCAN_RECORDS/BYTES/DURATION. Aggregating cached records costs ~0.7 µs each (measured 160 ms per 228.7k), so a separate high bound such as 2M is fine for cached ones.

2. Make the decode cap byte- or time-based and order eviction by mtime (oldest first) instead of insertion order. Rely on the existing 120-day retention prune, which only runs for windowed requests, and also run it on load.

3. Surface 'limited by budget' distinctly from 'failed' in coverage so the UI can say so.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Confirmed at UsageService.ts:612-629: scannedRecords counts reused cache records. Per-window counts from the live scan cache (files with mtime ≥ window - 36 h):

| Window | Codex records | Claude records |

|---|---|---|

| 7d | 2,914 | 68,705 |

| 30d | 29,949 | 94,524 |

| 90d | 124,856 | 97,195 |

| all | 131,505 | 97,195 |

  • Codex 90d and all-time are therefore already truncated at 100k and marked partial.
  • Worse than reported: the DEFAULT range is 30d (statisticsSearch.ts:51), and Claude is within ~5.5k records of the cap there. Almost all Claude history is inside 30 days, so the default view will start silently under-reporting Claude within about a day.
  • Decode cap: usageScanCache.ts:198 skips any file that pushes the total over 250k. Iteration follows Map insertion order, so the newest files are dropped. The cache holds 228,700 records and the last 14 days averaged ~6.4k/day, so '~3 days' is plausible.

This is a correctness bug as well as a performance issue.

Part of Priority 16: Projects and Pull Requests pages

Expected gain

Git status time for 17 worktrees drops from ~13 s to ~1 s (measured). Workspace states on the Projects map arrive ~5 s sooner for the ryco project at concurrency 4, and agent preflight/lifecycle preview using inspectCheckout benefit too.

What happens today

The map is the default Projects view. Each checkout's CheckoutSource calls lifecycle.listWorkspaces (useProjectWorkspaceInspection), and on the server list() runs inspectWorkspace for every non-main worktree of the project at concurrency 4. Each live checkout runs git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=normal --ignored=traditional (checkoutInspection.ts:213). Traditional mode has to descend into ignored trees such as node_modules to decide whether a directory is wholly ignored. Measured on 17 live ryco worktrees: 12.9-13.1 s sequential and 5.9 s wall at concurrency 4 (29 s on the first cold pass). The same command with --ignored=matching takes 0.97 s and produces equivalent output (31 KB vs 29 KB); without --ignored it takes 0.63 s. The ryco project has 33 live non-main checkouts, so a Projects open costs roughly 6-12 s of git work on the server. It is repeated on every page mount, every project switch and every lifecycle revision bump (useWorkspaceLifecycleChanges), because there is no cache.

Proposal

Change line 213 to --ignored=matching. With --untracked-files=normal, a directory that matches an ignore pattern (node_modules/, dist/) is still reported as one !! dir/ entry, so the protected/regenerable classification in packages/shared/src/workspaceLifecycle.ts:70-90 keeps working per entry. Only fully ignored but unmatched directories are reported per file, and output is already bounded by maxOutputBytes plus the truncated flag. Add a parseWorktreeStatus test for both shapes. A stronger option is to compute ignored classification only on preview/apply (which re-inspect anyway) and have list() report changes without the ignored sample.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

The cost is confirmed. checkoutInspection.ts:197-231 runs status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=normal --ignored=traditional. list() (WorkspaceLifecycle.ts:1153-1165) inspects every worktree of the project at concurrency 4. The map is the default view (projectsSearch.ts:49-51), and each CheckoutSource calls list(projectId) (useProjectMapCheckouts.tsx:140-148). The requestKey includes the lifecycle revision (useProjectWorkspaceInspection.ts:47-50), so a revision bump re-runs it. My own read-only timings on 7 live ryco worktrees: traditional 1.64-2.21 s each, matching 0.15-0.21 s, no --ignored 0.17-0.20 s (each figure includes ~30-60 ms of timer overhead). That is ~10x. The live DB has 33 unarchived, present, non-main ryco worktrees.

The proposal is NOT semantics-preserving. The comment at lines 203-205 chose traditional on purpose. Diffing the !! entries showed that matching mode reports extra ignored directories that contain only empty subdirectories (apps/server/caches/, claude-mcp-test/, userdata/, worktrees/ in 3 of the 7 worktrees I checked). classifyIgnoredPath (packages/shared/src/workspaceLifecycle.ts:71-81) labels these 'protected'. checkoutHasBlockingChanges would then flip to true and block remove-checkout or suggestions. It would also change summary action availability, because blockers at WorkspaceLifecycle.ts:308 feed summarize() at 477-528. Unmatched directories whose contents are all ignored would also be listed per file, which can hit the 256 KiB bound, and truncated counts as blocking.

A correct fix: use matching mode and drop !! dir/ protected entries that contain no files (a bounded fs walk over a handful of directories). Or run list() without --ignored and classify only in preview/apply, which already re-inspect via loadState.

Part of Priority 16: Projects and Pull Requests pages

Expected gain

First PR-page open for the ryco project: est. ~45-80 gh + ~33-70 git processes removed or serialized from the burst that overlaps the page's own gh calls, and steady-state ≥12 gh pr view calls per list poll removed (estimate from code paths and live DB counts; not timed end to end).

What happens today

The sourceControlListChangeRequests handler taps refreshLinkedWorktreeSourceControlStates after every list (sourceControlRpc.ts:464-471). The same tap follows list/search issues and search change requests. For a project-root cwd, the scope is the whole project. After a 5 s debounce per project+cwd (constants.ts:2), the code forks refreshWorktreeSourceControlState with for (...) yield* Effect.forkDetach(refresh(id)), i.e. unbounded concurrency (context.ts:332-368), for every unarchived non-main worktree.

Each refresh does the following:

  • It re-reads every open or current PR link through getPullRequestState, which runs gh pr view with the full SUMMARY field set: comments, statusCheckRollup, mergeable, assignees and labels (GitHubSourceControlProvider.ts:1029-1045, GitHubCli.ts:91-97, 2507-2511). Only state, isDraft and mergedAt/closedAt are used.
  • When discovery is due, it calls GitManager.readRemoteStatus: git statusDetails, probeBranchPublished, then findLatestPr. findLatestPr runs one gh pr list --head <sel> --state all --limit 20 with the full LIST fields per head selector (GitManager.ts:844-881, 1039-1070). The sweep interval is 5 min, and lastDiscoveryAtByWorktree starts empty after boot, so every worktree is due on the first open.

The live DB (read-only) shows 56 worktree rows for the ryco project, 33 of them unarchived, present and non-main, and 12 with PR links. So the first PR-page open after boot launches ≈33 discovery passes (33+ git status, 33-66 gh pr list --state all) plus ≥12 gh pr view at once (estimate from code and DB, not timed). Measured gh pr list here takes 1.3-2.8 s. The burst competes with the page's own authored/review-requested lists and stack-summary calls, which start later because they wait on git status, and it risks GitHub secondary rate limits. Link re-reads are not interval-gated, so every list poll more than 5 s apart repeats ≥12 gh pr view calls. For open PRs, those link states are already in the list result that triggered the sweep.

Proposal

1. Bound the sweep. Run one forked Effect.forEach(refreshIds, refresh, { concurrency: 2 }) and start it after the page's list group settles, or at low priority.

2. Satisfy link refreshes from the rows the list RPC just returned (state, isDraft, mergedAt for open PRs). Batch the remaining numbers into one GraphQL query per repository, the way getPullRequestStackSummaries already batches by number.

3. Make discovery one repo-wide gh pr list --state all --limit N --json number,headRefName,state,updatedAt,... per sweep, matched to worktree branches locally, instead of one or more gh calls per worktree and head selector.

4. Give getPullRequestState a lean field list (state, isDraft, mergedAt, closedAt).

5. Gate link re-reads with the same interval map used for discovery.

Category: Blocking I/ORisk: mediumInvestigator confidence: highdedicated-pages:statistics-blocks-event-loop-and-connection

Part of Priority 9: Statistics: memoize, aggregate incrementally, never block the server

Expected gain

Removes 2.6-8.5 s of whole-server stall per Activity open on this DB. Repeat opens cost O(changed threads), i.e. ms instead of seconds.

What happens today

NodeSqliteClient uses DatabaseSync, so statement.all() runs synchronously on the main thread with one connection behind a semaphore. getStatistics wraps the six queries plus JS aggregation in sql.withTransaction, which takes the semaphore for the whole compute. Effect.all(..., {concurrency:'unbounded'}) gives no parallelism because every query is synchronous. Measured on the live DB, one Activity-tab open blocks the event loop and every other DB reader/writer for ~2.6-3.0 s warm or ~8.5 s cold. That freezes provider stream ingestion, WebSocket pushes, terminal output and event appends for all clients, which is also a reliability problem. The snapshot cache key is total_changes()/data_version, which changes on any write, so while any agent is active it misses on essentially every open. The whole history (109k token rows, 33.9 MB of payload JSON) is reprocessed each time. The client keeps no cache across mounts either.

Proposal

1. Make the aggregation incremental. orchestration_events is append-only, so keep per-thread partial aggregates in memory or in a small statistics_thread_rollup table keyed by (thread_id, last event sequence, turns/activities revision). On request, recompute only threads whose max stream sequence or projection updated_at changed, using WHERE stream_id IN (...) (the partial index already leads with stream_id).

2. Run analytics on a read-only connection in a worker_thread. WAL allows concurrent readers, so the writer connection and the event loop are never held, and the transaction wrapper is no longer needed for consistency.

3. Serve stale-while-revalidate: return the last snapshot immediately with its generatedAt, refresh in the background with a minimum interval (e.g. 30-60 s), and push or poll the update.

4. On the client, keep a module-level last snapshot so a reopen paints instantly.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Confirmed:

  • NodeSqliteClient uses synchronous statement.all (NodeSqliteClient.ts:121-140) on one connection behind Semaphore(1) (219-230). The transactionAcquirer holds the permit for the whole scope.
  • getStatistics wraps computeStatistics in cacheLock + sql.withTransaction (StatisticsQuery.ts:736-769). Effect.all with unbounded concurrency (331-384) cannot overlap synchronous calls.
  • The cache key is total_changes()/data_version (749-758), so any write invalidates it.
  • useStatistics (useStatistics.ts:19-52) holds the snapshot only in component state.
  • My cold-ish timings of just two of the six queries (5.4 s + 3.2 s) back the 8.5 s cold claim.

Scope note: Activity is the non-default tab; parseStatisticsSearch defaults to view 'usage'. It is also used by the settings StatisticsPanel. Line ranges corrected: the statement runner is 121-140, not 117-135, which is the prepare cache.

Part of Priority 9: Statistics: memoize, aggregate incrementally, never block the server

Expected gain

-250-300 ms on the first open each day on a good network; -up to 10 s offline or captive-portal; no queueing of other summary requests behind a network fetch.

What happens today

readSummaryUnlocked awaits ensureRates() before any scanning, inside the scanSemaphore(1) permit. When ratesFetchedAtMs is older than RATES_TTL_MS (24 h), it does a blocking GET of the LiteLLM model_prices JSON (2,750,280 B; measured 248-293 ms on a fast link) with a 10 s timeout, even though valid cached rates are already loaded from pricing-cache.json. Offline, behind a captive portal or on a slow network, the first Statistics open of each day waits up to 10 s, and concurrent requests queue behind it on the semaphore. ratesRevision also JSON.stringifies the whole document again (5.7-7.8 ms).

Proposal

Use stale-while-revalidate. If any rates are loaded (memory or disk), price with them immediately and fork a background single-flight refresh (Effect.forkDaemon guarded by a Deferred). Block only when no rates exist at all, and even then run the fetch in parallel with resolveTranscriptSources and the directory walk: pricing is needed only in the aggregator, so collect records first and price after. Also kick the refresh once in the background ~30 s after server boot when the cache is stale. Compute the revision from the raw response text (or an ETag) instead of re-stringifying.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Confirmed: ensureRates (UsageService.ts:243-281) is awaited at line 455 inside scanSemaphore (806-808) before any scanning, with a 10 s timeout. It fetches whenever the cache is older than 24 h. pricing-cache.json on disk is dated Oct 10 21:06.

Missed bug that makes it worse: when the fetch fails (document===null, 256-259), ratesFetchedAtMs is NOT advanced. So while offline, behind a captive portal or on a slow network, EVERY summary request, not just the first of the day, re-attempts the download and can block up to 10 s, with other requests queued behind it on the semaphore. A fix needs a failure backoff, for example recording lastAttemptAtMs, as well as stale-while-revalidate.

Part of Priority 16: Projects and Pull Requests pages

Expected gain

-1 codex app-server spawn + MCP status round per MCP-settings open (seconds when MCP servers are slow to start; exact ms not measured); removes the stale-workspace race.

What happens today

loadWorkspaces is a useCallback with selectedWorkspaceId in its deps, and useEffect(() => void loadWorkspaces(), [loadWorkspaces]) re-runs whenever its identity changes. The first run sets selectedWorkspaceId from null to the first workspace, the callback changes, and the effect fires again: 2× listWorkspaces plus 2× listServers({detail:'full'}) per open. Selecting a workspace calls loadServers explicitly and also re-triggers the effect (listWorkspaces plus a second loadServers), so two responses race and the last to resolve wins, which may be the wrong workspace. For Codex workspaces, withClient builds a new CodexClient.layerCommand for codex app-server per call, then sends initialize and paginated mcpServerStatus/list with detail 'full' (25 s timeout).

Proposal

Run the initial load once per mcpApi: effect deps [mcpApi], read the current selection from a ref. Guard loads with a generation/abort token so only the latest response applies. On the server, keep a short-lived pooled codex app-server per workspace runtime (idle-close after ~60 s) and/or cache the status list for a few seconds, so Settings navigation does not respawn codex.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Confirmed:

  • loadWorkspaces deps include selectedWorkspaceId (McpServersSettings.tsx:881-903), and the effect at 905-907 depends on loadWorkspaces. The first run moves null to the first workspace id, so it runs a second time: 2× listWorkspaces and 2× listServers('full'), then it settles.
  • The workspace selector handlers (1037-1040, 1174-1177) call loadServers and also re-trigger the effect, so they race.
  • CodexMcpService.withClient (667-693) builds a fresh codex app-server per call, then initializes and pages mcpServerStatus/list (700-726).
  • findWorkspace also re-runs discoverWorkspaces on every listServers.

This only applies when the MCP section is opened.

Part of Priority 16: Projects and Pull Requests pages

Expected gain

~400 → ~45 git spawns per ryco listWorkspaces (≈ -4-5 s of process time, ≈ -1 s wall at concurrency 4). Reopening Projects within the TTL becomes near-instant instead of repeating all git work.

What happens today

inspectCheckout runs, for every worktree, these commands against the project root:

  • rev-parse --git-common-dir
  • rev-parse --verify HEAD
  • worktree list --porcelain
  • rev-parse refs/heads/<branch>
  • rev-list --count base..branch

The first three are identical for every worktree of the project. For live checkouts it adds rev-parse HEAD, status, symbolic-ref and a second --git-common-dir. That is ~5 spawns for each of the 22 removed and ~9 for each of the 33 live ryco worktrees, ≈ 400 git processes per listWorkspaces at ~12-16 ms each (measured spawn cost), excluding status. Each call also rebuilds the full shell snapshot plus listTrashed(10,000) in loadContext. lifecycle.suggestions() (settings view) inspects up to 20 more worktrees at concurrency 2 with a second loadContext, in parallel with listWorkspaces for overlapping worktrees.

Proposal

1. Hoist project-level facts out of the per-worktree loop. Compute common-dir, root HEAD and worktree list once per list() call. Get all branch heads plus ahead/behind in one git for-each-ref --format='%(refname) %(objectname) %(ahead-behind:HEAD)' refs/heads (git 2.41+; this machine has 2.55), with a fallback for older git. Pass the results into inspectCheckout as a precomputed ProjectGitFacts.

2. Skip worktree-level git for checkoutRemovedAt rows (they are already 'removed').

3. Add a per-worktree inspection cache keyed by (worktree HEAD oid, .git/worktrees/<id>/index mtime, worktree dir mtime) with a short TTL (e.g. 30 s), shared by list(), suggestions() and preview(). Single-flight per project.

4. Return summaries progressively, or at least the cheap ones first, so the map renders before the slow status calls finish.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

Confirmed facts:

  • checkoutInspection.ts:151-167 runs rev-parse --git-common-dir, rev-parse --verify HEAD and worktree list against the root for every worktree.
  • Lines 186-194 resolve the branch head and 232-234 run rev-list.
  • Live checkouts add rev-parse HEAD (196), status (197-231), symbolic-ref (239) and a second common-dir (243-247).
  • Removed rows still run ~5 spawns, because inspectWorkspace (WorkspaceLifecycle.ts:422-455) skips inspectCheckout only for main/null paths, not for checkoutRemovedAt.
  • loadContext (366-371) rebuilds the shell snapshot plus listTrashed(10,000) on every call. suggestions() (1172-1213) inspects up to 20 worktrees again.
  • The DB counts (56 rows, 33 live non-main) make the ~400 spawns estimate plausible.

The '~400 → ~45 spawns' claim is inflated. Hoisting only the 3 project-level commands plus one for-each-ref leaves rev-parse HEAD, status, symbolic-ref and common-dir per live worktree: 4×33 ≈ 132, plus ~4, so ~140. Reaching ~40 needs the per-checkout HEAD, branch and common-dir to come from the worktree list --porcelain output, which weakens the independent re-verification the code does on purpose. Skipping removed rows saves ~110 spawns. The wall-time win is ~0.5-1 s at concurrency 4, small next to the status fix. The TTL cache is the bigger win for reopen. useAutomationCentre.ts:116-121 has nothing to do with this finding.

Part of Priority 9: Statistics: memoize, aggregate incrementally, never block the server

Expected gain

First open after boot: -80-115 ms sync. Every open with an active session: -50-55 ms sync CPU and -22 MB disk write. -45-60 MiB resident after Statistics has been opened once.

What happens today

On the first summary after boot, loadScanCache reads scan-cache.json (22,036,341 B for this user), then runs JSON.parse (37-46 ms) and decodeUsageScanCache (33-68 ms), all synchronous: ~80-115 ms. persistScanCache runs whenever scanCacheDirty is set, which happens whenever any transcript changed, i.e. always while a session is active. It runs encodeUsageScanCache plus JSON.stringify of the whole cache (~50-55 ms sync) and writes 22 MB atomically on every Statistics open or range change. The decoded cache retains 62.9 MiB of heap for the process lifetime. 30% of the file is 64-char sha256 dedupe keys (6.5 MB). The server holds this alongside the ~32 MiB transcript checkpoint map (usageTranscriptReader.ts:146-179).

Proposal

1. Replace the monolithic JSON with per-file entries in a small SQLite table, either a separate usage.sqlite or a table in state.sqlite written from the usage service: (file_key, root_key, size, mtime, fingerprint, provider, records BLOB). Write only changed rows and load lazily per root. Alternatively, shard JSON files by root and write only dirty shards.

2. Encode records columnar/binary (Float64Array timestamps, Uint32 token counts, interned model/session indexes). Truncate dedupe/session hashes to 64-bit (16 hex chars or a BigUint64), which is ample for <10^6 records.

3. Persist off the request path: debounce, run after the response, and use a worker for encoding if it stays large.

4. Drop the in-memory cache after an idle period, or keep only per-file pre-aggregated (UTC hour, model, speed) sums plus dedupe keys for providers that need cross-file dedupe.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Confirmed:

  • loadScanCache (UsageService.ts:183-199) parses and decodes the whole file. ~/.ryco/userdata/usage/scan-cache.json is 22,036,341 B: version 4, 2,155 files, 228,700 records.
  • readFileRecords sets scanCacheDirty=true on every non-reused parse (372-418). persistScanCache (201-212) re-encodes and stringifies the whole Map, and runs on every summary at line 769.
  • Nit: the file read is async (readBoundedUsageFile through Effect.promise). Only JSON.parse/decode and encode/stringify are synchronous; the 22 MB write is async I/O. The sync-CPU figures stand.
  • I did not re-measure the 62.9 MiB heap figure.

Part of Priority 9: Statistics: memoize, aggregate incrementally, never block the server

Expected gain

-1 RTT (+~10 ms server CPU) per environment per open or range change. Local usage paints as soon as the local node answers. Rapid range switching no longer queues N full scans (each ~0.4-1 s server time).

What happens today

wsRpcClient.server.getUsageSummary first awaits a full serverGetConfig only to assert usageContractVersion, so every request costs 2 serial round trips. On the server, loadServerConfig rebuilds providers, settings, auth, diagnostics metrics and resolveAvailableEditors() (6-7 ms sync, measured). useUsageSummary waits for Promise.all over every connected environment, so a slow remote node (summary budget up to 30 s, SUMMARY_SCAN_DURATION_MS) hides the local result. Results live in component state only, so every reopen starts again from the skeleton. Range or environment changes start new requests without cancelling old ones. The server serialises them on scanSemaphore(1), so clicking 7d→30d→90d queues three full walks, aggregations and 22 MB persists before the last answer arrives.

Proposal

1. Read the contract version from the connection's already-received server config/descriptor (environments/runtime keeps one per connection, service.ts:1143), or let the server reject mismatches with a typed error, which the code already maps.

2. Merge per-environment results progressively with setState per settled environment and show a per-environment pending marker.

3. Add a module-level SWR cache keyed by (environmentId, request) so a reopen paints the last result immediately and refreshes in the background.

4. Coalesce or cancel: keep one in-flight request per environment and drop superseded ones. On the server, make readSummary latest-wins per client, or pass an interrupt when the RPC is abandoned.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Confirmed:

  • wsRpcClient.ts:804-819 awaits serverGetConfig before every getUsageSummary.
  • loadServerConfig (context.ts:884-918) recomputes keybindings, providers, settings, auth, diagnostics metrics and resolveAvailableEditors (open.ts:267-295).
  • useUsageSummary (useUsageSummary.ts:76-116) uses Promise.all across environments and keeps results only in component state. UsageRequestGeneration drops stale results on the client, but nothing cancels server work, and readSummary serialises on scanSemaphore(1).
  • Saved environments already store serverConfig in the runtime store (service.ts:1140-1153), so proposal 1 is feasible.
  • I also checked that the connection-registry subscription emits only on register/remove (supervision.ts:274-277, 547/557), so it does not cause extra refetches.

Part of Priority 1: Remove the 300 ms React Suspense reveal delay from every navigation

Expected gain

Removes chunk fetch+parse from the time-to-data on first open (est. 50-150 ms local, several hundred ms over hub relay or slow networks). Hover preloading usually hides chunk time entirely. Also removes the 'Ryco is starting' flash.

What happens today

createRouter sets no defaultPreload, and tanstackRouter() runs without autoCodeSplitting. Route components wrap React.lazy, so <Link to="/statistics"> in the sidebar and router.preloadRoute cannot warm the chunk. No route defines a loader, so data requests start only after the lazy chunk downloads, evaluates and mounts. Measured incremental JS beyond boot + RootAppShell: Statistics 457 KiB raw / 133 KiB gzip, Projects 318/111, PRs 1,022/311. Statistics and PRs use AppBootLoadingSurface (min-h-screen logo, aria-label 'Ryco is starting') as the Suspense fallback, so first open looks like an app restart. Projects and Settings already use a blank SidebarInset. Only Settings has an idle preload (SettingsRouteBridge.tsx:33-43).

Proposal

1. Convert these routes to component: lazyRouteComponent(() => import('../components/statistics/StatisticsPage'), 'StatisticsPage'), or enable tanstackRouter({ autoCodeSplitting: true }).

2. Set defaultPreload: 'intent' and defaultPreloadDelay: 50 in router.ts so sidebar and palette Links warm chunks on hover/focus.

3. Add route loaders (or preload hooks) that start the page's first data requests into the SWR caches from the other findings: usage summary for the current range, getStatistics, the three PR lists. These run in parallel with the chunk download.

4. Replace AppBootLoadingSurface with a page-shell skeleton (SidebarInset plus header) for statistics and pull-requests.

5. Optionally idle-preload the Statistics/Projects chunks after RootAppShell settles, as Settings does, but only for local/desktop sessions.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Confirmed:

  • router.ts:7-14 has no defaultPreload. vite.config.ts:92 calls tanstackRouter() without autoCodeSplitting.
  • statistics.tsx, pull-requests.tsx and projects.tsx wrap module-level React.lazy, so it cannot be warmed via router preload. No route has a loader.
  • Only Settings is idle-preloaded (SettingsRouteBridge.tsx:33-43, settingsRoute.ts:13-15).
  • Statistics and PRs use AppBootLoadingSurface (min-h-screen logo, 'is starting'); Projects uses a blank SidebarInset.

Corrections and caveats:

  • The scenario summary's wording that lazy() is called 'inside its render' is wrong; it is called at module scope. The consequence (no router-driven preload) holds.
  • The sidebar stays visible, so the flash is a page-area logo rather than a full app restart.
  • Local gains are bounded by chunk parse time; the server work after mount dominates time-to-data. The 50-150 ms local estimate is an upper bound; the larger benefit is over hosted/relay.

The Aug hardening report made statistics/diagnostics lazy route boundaries (done); performance-efficiency-size-improvements.md suggests retesting modulePreload. Intent preloading and loaders are not covered.

Part of Priority 16: Projects and Pull Requests pages

Expected gain

Complete grouped list arrives ~1 gh round earlier (~1.3-1.7 s measured per gh call). -79% list stdout bytes (278 KB → 59 KB) and ~-0.4 s per list call. ≥6 → 1-3 gh processes per first open.

What happens today

The authored and review-requested lists are enabled only when capabilities.involvementFilters is true. Capabilities come from gitStatus.data.sourceControlProvider; before git status arrives the provider kind is 'unknown' (involvementFilters false). Those two gh calls therefore start one git-status round trip after the state list, even though the server resolves the provider and capability itself (listFromHostingProvider). Every list runs gh pr list --json with GITHUB_PULL_REQUEST_LIST_JSON_FIELDS. That set includes 'comments' (full bodies) only to derive commentsCount, and 'mergeable'. Measured on this repo for 100 open PRs: 1,730 ms / 278,126 B with those fields vs 1,342 ms / 59,461 B without; state=all took 6.3-9.5 s. After each list, enrichChangeRequestsWithStacks makes a second sequential gh GraphQL call for stack summaries, which repeats for overlapping PR numbers across the three groups. The first open after boot therefore makes ≥6 gh calls in two waves. Nothing is cached across restarts.

Proposal

1. Enable the involvement lists immediately and let the server answer unsupported hosts with an empty or typed result, or derive capability from the cached git status when available.

2. Replace comments with a count. One gh api graphql query can return all three groups in one round trip with comments { totalCount }, statusCheckRollup and stack info, which also removes the separate stack-summary call. If staying on gh pr list, drop comments/mergeable from the list fields and fetch them in detail only.

3. Add a server-side TTL cache keyed by (repo, state, involvement) and dedupe stack summaries by PR number across groups.

4. Seed the client cache from that server cache on first open (SWR).

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

Code confirmed:

  • Involvement lists are gated on capabilities derived from gitStatus.data.sourceControlProvider (usePullRequestsModel.ts:78-110, pullRequestsModel.logic.ts:98-102).
  • LIST fields include 'comments' and 'mergeable' (GitHubCli.ts:68-109). Comments are used only for the count (gitHubPullRequests.ts:351-355).
  • enrichChangeRequestsWithStacks runs another gh call after each list (GitHubSourceControlProvider.ts:348-408, 469-497).
  • The server already returns empty for 'unknown' providers (sourceControlRpc.ts:196-213).

My measurements:

  • Byte sizes reproduce exactly: 278,465 B full vs 59,461 B without comments/mergeable.
  • The repo has only 16 open PRs, not 100.
  • The time win is not reproducible: full 1.64/1.68/2.81 s vs lean 1.26/1.53/1.79 s, dominated by network noise. Treat '~-0.4 s per call' as unproven.

The investigator missed the bigger cost: each list RPC also triggers the unbounded project worktree sweep (see additional finding).
