Category: CPURisk: lowInvestigator confidence: mediumdedicated-pages:usage-transcript-reader-throughput
Expected gain

Parsing changed or uncached transcripts ~3x faster (195 MiB: 710 → ~200-250 ms). Listing ~75-100 → ~25 ms. Matters most for the first open after boot with active large sessions.

What happens today

For every line, readTranscript copies the segment (Buffer.from), grows long lines with Buffer.concat(pending, segment) (quadratic for multi-MiB tool-output lines spanning many 64 KiB reads), feeds sha256 per line, and decodes it to a JS string. Only then does mightCarryUsage(line) reject the ~99% of lines without usage. Measured on real codex transcripts: 155-195 MiB files take 561-1,092 ms (170-350 MiB/s). A floor implementation (1 MiB reads, chunk-level sha256, Buffer.indexOf for the marker) does the 195 MiB file in 189-201 ms. Changed active transcripts are re-parsed fully after every boot because checkpoints are memory-only, and each file has a 2 s cap (12 files >100 MiB, max 463 MiB). listUsageTranscriptFiles awaits lstat serially per entry (49-73 ms for 1,342 Claude files).

Proposal

Scan with 1 MiB reads and hash whole chunks (the checkpoint digest can be over raw bytes up to the last newline). Find line boundaries with indexOf(10) and test the provider markers on the Buffer slice ("usage", "token_count", "turn_context" etc. as pre-encoded Buffers) before any toString. Accumulate long-line pieces in an array and concat once. In listing, batch lstat calls with bounded concurrency (e.g. 32) or use opendir plus Promise.all per directory.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Confirmed:

  • Per line, readTranscript does Buffer.from(segment) or Buffer.concat([pending, segment]), so a long line spanning many 64 KiB reads grows quadratically (usageTranscriptReader.ts:330-332).
  • It also updates sha256 per line (340), then toString and mightCarryUsage (341, 214-239). The per-file 2 s cap is at 282 and 307.
  • Listing awaits lstat serially per entry (86-87).
  • 12 codex transcripts are over 100 MiB; the largest is 485,131,234 B. All 12 are currently in the scan cache (matched by size), so re-parse matters only for changed or evicted files, which ties into the decode-cap finding.
  • I did not re-run the throughput floor.

Loading projects 15 findings · 1 high · 9 medium · 5 low

Each visible sidebar thread row runs the full VCS pipeline, ~40 processes including a git fetch and a gh call per feature-branch folder, just to show a branch name and PR badge. Repository identity, icons and repo facts are recomputed on every connect.

How it works today (investigator's summary)

Projects reach the client in two stages. First, subscribeShell (apps/server/src/ws/orchestrationRpc.ts:489-518) does two things. It forks reconcileAllWorktrees, and it builds getShellSnapshot: 7 SQL reads, plus a repository-identity lookup for every project root. That lookup spawns 2 git processes per root, at concurrency 4, with a 60 s in-memory TTL and a 1 s overall budget. The thread route cannot render until the snapshot arrives (bootstrapComplete). After a cold boot the identity cache is empty, and any snapshot taken more than a minute after the last one repeats the git work. The forked reconciliation adds work on the same connection: for each project it builds 2 more full shell snapshots and runs 4 git spawns. With 29 projects that is about 59 snapshots and 116 spawns, all competing for the SQLite connection and the event loop while the client loads.

Second, the sidebar renders every project eagerly. Each project header requests its icon over RPC. The server has no icon cache: every request spawns a Node/Electron child process, two at a time. Measured: 58 ms per child, 755 ms for 26 projects, repeated on every reconnect or new tab. Each visible thread row with a branch then subscribes to the full VCS status stream for its folder (the worktree path, or the project root), even though the row only shows the branch name and PR badge. For a feature-branch worktree that is about 20 git spawns of local status, followed by a remote status. The remote status runs a network git fetch, recomputes the local status (about 15 more spawns), does several git config reads, and runs a heavy gh pr list. That totals about 44 child processes per feature-branch folder, with no process-wide limit. Each spawn costs about 1.3 ms of main-thread time.

On the user's real data (29 projects, 57 worktrees, 274 live branch threads across 53 distinct git folders) and in the requested scenario (30 projects × 5 worktrees), most of the cost is in the server spawning git, gh and node children. SQL is cheap: 3.7 ms warm per snapshot. Almost nothing is persisted: repository identity, icons, repo facts (remotes, default branch, config) and PR lookups are all in-memory with TTLs of 2 s to 60 s, so a restart or reconnect recomputes everything. There are no filesystem watchers on repositories; freshness is TTL polling only.

Part of Priority 10: Sidebar and projects: stop running the full VCS pipeline per row

Expected gain

First sidebar render with ≈30 visible folders: ≈1,000-1,300 → ≈0-30 git spawns. gh calls drop to ≤ 1 per distinct repo, and no fetches. ≈1.3 s less event-loop blocking. PR badges arrive after one cached per-repo lookup instead of the fetch → status → gh chain (≈1-3 s)

What happens today

Every thread row whose thread has a branch subscribes subscribeVcsStatus for its folder (the worktree path, or the project root). Rows are visible-gated. The row reads only refName, pr and sourceControlProvider (resolveThreadPr, ThreadStatusIndicators.tsx:52-61).

Local status: on first subscription, streamStatus loads local status (repo detection 3 spawns + status + diff HEAD --numstat + symbolic-ref + remote get-url + 2× base-branch resolution + rev-list + rev-parse + diff numstat + 2 config reads). Measured: 20 spawns / 213-360 ms on a feature branch, 9 / 98 ms on main.

Remote status: with no fresh remote cache, it then runs readRemoteStatus. That does rev-parse @{upstream} + git remote + rev-parse --git-common-dir + git fetch, then readStatusDetailsLocal again (≈15 spawns), then provider detection (git remote -v), 3 config reads and gh pr list (measured 586-1003 ms). Total ≈44 processes per feature-branch folder and ≈24 per default-branch root.

Scale: the user's DB maps 274 live branch threads to 53 folders. With about 30 visible folders the first sidebar render launches ≈1,000-1,300 child processes, about 30 gh calls and up to 30 fetches. At the measured 1.31 ms of main-thread time per spawn, that is ≈1.3-1.7 s of event-loop blocking in spawn calls alone.

Related: VcsStatusBroadcaster keeps an unbounded cacheRef Map holding full file lists (line 141), and fans every change through one shared PubSub.sliding(64) filtered per folder (lines 134-137 and 570-573). A subscriber that falls more than 64 messages behind loses updates, including its own folder's.

Proposal

Add a lean sidebar summary channel, for example vcs.subscribeSummaries({ cwds }): one batched stream per client carrying only {cwd, refName, pr, provider}.

  • refName: read the checkout's HEAD directly. Resolve the .git file to the gitdir and read HEAD, with no spawn; revalidate by stat/fs.watch on that HEAD file.
  • PR for worktree threads: use the worktree projection's persisted pull_requests links, already maintained by refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.
  • PR for project-root threads: use a per-repository PR index. One lean gh pr list --state all --limit 100 per gitCommonDir, single-flight, cached 60 s, shared by all folders, clients and worktree discovery (see pr-lookup-heavy-fields-per-worktree).

Keep the full status stream only for the focused thread's surfaces (ChatView, GitActionsControl, DiffPanel). Bound the broadcaster cache (LRU about 256 folders) and replace the shared sliding PubSub with a per-folder subscriber map so publications are O(subscribers of that folder) and cannot be dropped by unrelated bursts.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Checked the code path end to end.

Client:

  • SidebarThreadRow.tsx:120-130 gates useGitStatus on isActive || isIntersecting (useIsIntersectingViewport).
  • SidebarProjectItem.tsx:202-231 resolves the target as worktreePath ?? member cwd, only when branch is non-null.
  • The row reads only refName, pr and sourceControlProvider (SidebarThreadRow.tsx:207-208; ThreadStatusIndicators.tsx:52-61).

Server:

  • streamStatus (VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:517-577) blocks the first emit on getOrLoadLocalStatus, then runs getOrLoadRemoteStatus when no fresh remote cache exists (30 s).
  • readRemoteStatus (GitManager.ts:844-881) calls gitCore.statusDetails. That runs refreshStatusUpstreamIfStale and then the full readStatusDetailsLocal again (GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1612-1620).
  • It then runs probeBranchPublished (+2 spawns when there is no upstream), provider detection, and findLatestPr. findLatestPr loops over every head selector (1-3 gh calls; it does not stop at the first hit).
  • The spawn counts match status-pipeline.txt: 20 local on a feature branch.

Corrections:

  • On the remote leg, the 2 s detection cache usually saves 3 spawns, so ≈40 per folder rather than 44.
  • The fetch is single-flighted per (gitCommonDir, remote) for 15 s and runs only when the branch has an upstream. That means ≤1 fetch per distinct repo, not 'up to 30' when the folders are worktrees of the same repos.
  • The 1.3-1.7 s of spawn-time main-thread blocking is cumulative and spread out, not one stall.

Supporting evidence for the proposal: the worktree header already renders persisted PR badges from the projection (SidebarWorktreeList.tsx:581-604, WorktreeSourceControlBadges with prNumber/prState). The per-thread-row status stream therefore duplicates data the client already has for worktree threads.

Part of Priority 10: Sidebar and projects: stop running the full VCS pipeline per row

Expected gain

Ahead/behind and PR-badge latency on first render: minus the fetch time (typically 0.3-2 s, up to 5 s) per repo. R fetches at boot → ≤1-2

What happens today

A new status stream with no fresh remote cache (30 s) runs getOrLoadRemoteStatus. That calls statusDetails → refreshStatusUpstreamIfStale → git --git-dir <common> fetch --quiet --no-tags <remote>. The fetch takes all branches of the remote (ryco has 1,112 refs), times out at 5 s, and is cached for 15 s per (commonDir, remote). The PR lookup and the ahead/behind counts wait for it.

On the first sidebar render with R visible repos this means R concurrent SSH/HTTPS fetches. These can trigger SSH-agent or hardware-key approval prompts despite GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. Every refreshStatus after an agent action repeats the fetch at most once per 15 s per repo. The default poll setting of 0 implies 'no automatic network', yet loading still fetches.

Proposal

Serve remote status from the current remote-tracking refs immediately, then fetch in the background only for: the focused thread's folder, an explicit refresh, or a poll interval > 0. Publish a second update when the fetch completes. Limit fetches with a small network semaphore (about 2), coalesced per gitCommonDir across worktrees. This combines with sidebar-pr-badge-runs-full-vcs-pipeline, which removes the fetch from sidebar rows entirely.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Verified:

  • streamStatus (VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:563-569) runs getOrLoadRemoteStatus whenever no fresh remote cache exists and no poller is retained. That holds with the default gitStatusPollIntervalMs = 0 (settings.ts:54-56).
  • loadRemoteStatus → GitWorkflowService.remoteStatus → GitManager.readRemoteStatus → gitCore.statusDetails → refreshStatusUpstreamIfStale (GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1104-1118). That runs rev-parse @{upstream}, git remote, rev-parse --git-common-dir, then git --git-dir <common> fetch --quiet --no-tags <remote> with a 5 s timeout and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 / SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never (66-73, 1043-1059).
  • The result is cached 15 s on success and 5 s on failure, keyed by (gitCommonDir, remote).
  • The PR lookup and ahead/behind are sequential after it.

Nuances:

  • Branches without an upstream skip the fetch entirely.
  • Worktrees of one repo share a single fetch, so the count is ≤1 per distinct repo, as the finding states.
  • The fetch result is allowNonZeroExit, so failures are silent but still cost up to 5 s.

The fix is small: use the no-fetch read for the initial load and fork a background refresh that publishes. Effort S-M.

Part of Priority 10: Sidebar and projects: stop running the full VCS pipeline per row

Expected gain

Removes index.lock contention between Ryco background reads and agent or user git commands. Avoids one index rewrite per status on large repos

What happens today

readStatusDetailsLocal runs git status --porcelain=2 --branch with the inherited environment. By default git status refreshes and rewrites the index as a side effect, holding .git/index.lock while it does.

Ryco runs status for every visible row, and again after every agent action and git RPC, while agents run git add, commit and rebase in the same checkout. That is a recipe for transient 'Unable to create .../index.lock: File exists' failures and extra index writes.

Other read-only paths in this codebase already set GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0: GitReadWorkspace.ts:37, GitComparison.ts:35, GitLineBlame.ts:68, checkoutInspection.ts:136, storage/filesystem.ts:245. The hottest read path does not.

Proposal

Add a readOnly: true option to executeGit that sets GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 centrally. Use it for status, the diff numstats, rev-list, rev-parse, for-each-ref, listRefs and listWorktreePaths. Optionally match checkoutInspection's -c core.fsmonitor=false for predictability.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Verified:

  • readStatusDetailsLocal runs git status --porcelain=2 --branch through executeGit (GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1423-1446, 933-960).
  • That goes through gitCommand → VcsProcess.spawn with env {...process.env, ...input.env} (VcsProcess.ts:108-120). Nothing sets GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS.
  • A grep shows GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 only in checkoutInspection.ts:136/218, storage/filesystem.ts:245/286, GitLineBlame.ts:68, GitIndexReview.ts:76, GitComparison.ts:35, GitReadWorkspace.ts:37 and GitImageBlob.ts:37. The hot status, numstat and rev-list path is missing it.

This is a genuine reliability bug: concurrent agent git add/commit can hit an index.lock held by Ryco's background status. The perf gain is secondary.

Expected gain

Fixes permanently-null repository identity (broken grouping/labels) for Windows users whose project paths contain spaces. Removes 1 cmd.exe spawn per identity probe (2 per project per 60 s) on Windows

What happens today

RepositoryIdentityResolver calls runProcess("git", ["-C", cwd, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"]) and runProcess("git", ["-C", cacheKey, "remote", "-v"]). runProcess spawns with shell: process.platform === "win32" (processRunner.ts:150-155) and does no argument quoting.

With shell:true, Node joins [file, ...args] with spaces and runs it through cmd.exe /d /s /c. A root such as C:\Users\Jane Doe\proj reaches git as -C C:\Users\Jane plus a stray Doe\proj, so git exits non-zero. resolveRepositoryIdentityCacheKey then returns null, which is negative-cached for 60 s and recomputed forever.

Effects on Windows:

  • Every project under a profile path with a space gets repositoryIdentity null in every shell snapshot and project event.
  • The client falls back to physical-path keys (deriveLogicalProjectKey), so 'repository' grouping (the default), group labels and provider and remote metadata silently never work for those users.
  • Each probe spawns cmd.exe and then git, roughly doubling process-creation cost on the platform where it is most expensive.

The rest of the VCS stack (VcsProcess) spawns git without a shell and is unaffected. Not measured here (macOS host). This is derived from Node's documented shell:true argument concatenation (DEP0190).

Proposal

Stop routing git through processRunner for identity. Use VcsProcess or the git driver (no shell), or call runProcess with cwd: root and no -C path argument, and set shell: false for git specifically.

More broadly, make processRunner quote arguments, or refuse args when shell:true, for any caller that passes filesystem paths. This combines naturally with persist-repository-identity's 'route the resolver through VcsProcess' step, and with a combined git rev-parse --show-toplevel --git-common-dir plus git config -z --get-regexp '^remote\..*\.url$'.

This finding was added by the adversarial verifier while checking the investigator's report. It has not been verified a second time.

Commit 2ae63f4aa ('Fix shell: true side effects on Windows') addressed orphaned processes and swallowed ENOENT but kept shell:true with unquoted args; the investigator noted the extra cmd.exe but not the path-with-spaces failure

Part of Priority 5: Cut database work at boot (it scales with DB size)

Expected gain

Removes 2×P git spawns (60 for 30 projects: ≈130-300 ms, up to the 1 s cap) from the cold-boot and reconnect shell snapshot that gates the thread view. Also from every migration pass, priority refresh, worktree creation, and turn start after 60 s idle. Removes the null-identity grouping flips, and the result survives restarts

What happens today

How it works today: RepositoryIdentityResolver runs git -C cwd rev-parse --show-toplevel, then git -C root remote -v, through processRunner.runProcess (shell:true on Windows). Two Effect Caches hold the results with a 60 s positive/negative TTL and no stale-while-revalidate. getShellSnapshot resolves every live root at concurrency 4 under Effect.timeoutOption(1000). Measured for 26 real roots: 118 ms at concurrency 4, 450 ms serial. The cache is empty after a cold boot, so the first client's snapshot (which gates bootstrapComplete and the thread route) waits for this.

Who pays it:

  • the managed-worktree migration pass (right after startup, then every ≤5 min);
  • the thread-priority snapshot refresh, run separately for each connected client (orchestrationStreams.ts:558-564);
  • ≈25 internal getShellSnapshot callers;
  • getProjectShellById / getActiveProjectByWorkspaceRoot. These run twice per turn start (ProviderCommandReactor.resolveProject), on worktree creation (gitRpc.ts:178-190, 354), on source-control scope lookups and on project.meta-updated event enrichment.

Only AgentControlProjectPlans reads identity server-side; the other callers only need workspaceRoot.

Correctness bug: on timeout the partial map leaves some projects with repositoryIdentity: null. The client builds the logical project key and group label from repositoryIdentity (logicalProjects.ts:96-123; default grouping mode is 'repository'). Sidebar grouping, labels and per-group order/expand state can therefore differ between connects on slow filesystems (the user has roots under ~/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox) or on Windows, and no later event repairs it.

Proposal

Persist identity in projection_projects as new columns: repository_identity_json, repository_identity_fingerprint (gitCommonDir + mtimeMs/size of <commonDir>/config) and repository_identity_checked_at.

  • Resolve in a background, concurrency-limited task on project.create, on project.meta.update that changes workspaceRoot, and in one startup sweep. Use one git rev-parse --show-toplevel --git-common-dir, then read remotes with one git config -z --get-regexp '^remote\..*\.url$'.
  • When the value changes, dispatch an event (for example project.repository-identity-updated) so connected clients update live and grouping never depends on a timeout.
  • getShellSnapshot and getProjectShellById become pure SQL. Revalidation becomes a cheap fs.stat of the config file, with no spawn.
  • Expose an identity-free getProjectRowById / getShellRows for internal callers, and route the resolver through VcsProcess (no cmd.exe wrapper).
  • Consider honouring project.preferredRemoteName when picking the primary remote; today the resolver ignores it.
Verifier (Partially confirmed)

The mechanics are correct:

  • RepositoryIdentityResolver.ts:92-95 and 103-179: 2 runProcess git spawns, two Caches with a 60 s TTL, no SWR.
  • getShellSnapshot resolves all live roots at concurrency 4 under timeoutOption(1000) (ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:560-598, 2658-2661).
  • getActiveProjectByWorkspaceRoot and getProjectShellById resolve with no timeout (2794-2845).
  • ProviderCommandReactor.resolveProject (511-515) is called at 716 and 1224.
  • toShellStreamEvent and enrichProjectEvent resolve on project events.
  • Only AgentControlProjectPlans reads identity server-side.

Overstated:

1. The cold-boot cost is bounded and measured at 118 ms for 26 roots (git-timing.txt). The managed-worktree migration pass that runs right after startup (serverRuntimeStartup.ts:1060-1079, managedWorktreeMigration.ts:326) also calls getShellSnapshot and warms the same cache, and concurrent callers coalesce in the Cache. That is ≈100-300 ms on the first snapshot, not a large share of boot.

2. A reconnect with resumeFromSequence skips the snapshot entirely (orchestrationStreams.ts:512-515), so 'every reconnect' is wrong.

3. 'No later event repairs it' is too strong. The next full snapshot (priority refresh at orchestrationStreams.ts:558-564, a non-resumed reconnect) or any project.meta-updated event re-resolves without a timeout and sends a project-upserted. The grouping flip is a transient glitch rather than a permanent one.

Additional bug the investigator only half-noted: on Windows, processRunner uses shell:true with unquoted args, so git -C <root> fails for roots that contain spaces (see the additional finding).

The proposal (persist identity plus a fingerprint, emit an update event, pure-SQL snapshot) is sound and not already done.

Part of Priority 5: Cut database work at boot (it scales with DB size)

Expected gain

First connect: 2P+1 → 1 shell-row read (≈ -0.5 to -0.9 s of SQLite/event-loop time at 30 projects). Git spawns 4P → about 0 to P (changed repos only, with combined detection). No contention with the first shell and thread load

What happens today

subscribeShell forks reconcileAllWorktrees, throttled to once per 5 min process-wide. That is on the first connect after boot and on any reconnect after 5 min. It loads one getShellSnapshot, then for each available project at concurrency 4 runs reconcileProjectWorktrees:

  • getProjectShellById (SQL + identity);
  • listWorktreePaths: repo detection with 3 sequential rev-parse spawns, then git worktree list --porcelain;
  • ensureProjectMainWorktree: a full getShellSnapshot, plus a 9-20-spawn localStatus when the main row is missing;
  • another full getShellSnapshot.

Totals: 26 existing roots in the user's data give 53 snapshots; P=30 gives 61. Each snapshot is 7 SQL statements in one transaction over all thread rows, including deleted ones: measured 3.7 ms warm / 37 ms cold, plus ≈3-10 ms schema decode and JS mapping, plus identity. That is ≈0.5-0.9 s of SQLite and event-loop time and ≈4P git spawns, contending with the connecting client's own shell and thread loads.

Proposal

1. Load data once per pass. Use the single top-level snapshot (or narrow SQL: worktree rows for all projects, and SELECT thread_id, project_id, branch, worktree_path, worktree_id FROM projection_threads WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND worktree_path IS NOT NULL), group by project, and pass the rows into ensureProjectMainWorktree and planWorktreeReconciliation; refresh only after a dispatch. This part is effort S.

2. Move the sweep off the client-connect path into a background startup phase after the command gate opens.

3. Replace the time throttle with change detection: stat <gitCommonDir>/worktrees (mtime) per repo, persist the last seen value, and only run git worktree list for repos that changed or were never seen.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Verified:

  • orchestrationRpc.ts:489-518 forkDetaches reconcileAllWorktrees on every subscribeShell, with a module-level 5-minute throttle (worktreeOperations.ts:64, 75, 1003-1008).
  • reconcileAllWorktrees takes one getShellSnapshot, then runs reconcileProjectWorktrees at concurrency 4 for each available root.
  • reconcileProjectWorktrees does: loadProjectForGitWorkflow (getProjectShellById → identity), listWorktreePaths (detection, 3 sequential rev-parse or the 2 s cache, plus worktree list --porcelain), ensureProjectMainWorktree (another full getShellSnapshot at 257-266, plus localStatus when the main row is missing), and another full getShellSnapshot (861-867). That is 2P+1 snapshots.

My read-only bench (.perf-research/verifier-projects-loading/shell-decode-bench.mjs) shows the second whole-snapshot Schema decode costs only ≈1.9 ms warm for 282 live threads. With 3.7 ms SQL plus ≈3 ms row decode, that is ≈9-10 ms warm per snapshot, so ≈0.45-0.6 s total for 53 snapshots. The investigator's 0.5-0.9 s is plausible at the low end; the cold-cache number is higher.

The work is forked, so it does not block the client's own snapshot directly, only through SQLite connection and event-loop contention.

The proposal (load once, pass rows down, move off the connect path, detect changes via <commonDir>/worktrees mtime) is not implemented anywhere.

Part of Priority 10: Sidebar and projects: stop running the full VCS pipeline per row

Expected gain

30 projects: ≈0.9 s of serialized child processes (and 30 transient 40-60 MB processes) per connection → 0-1 child per server lifetime. Reconnects and new tabs: 30 RPCs → 0. No more timed-out fallback icons

What happens today

Client side: every sidebar project header renders ProjectFavicon immediately (not visibility-gated). That calls projects.readIcon. The client cache is keyed to the connection generation, and requestKey includes connectedAt, so every reconnect or new tab re-requests every icon.

Server side: no cache. Each call spawns process.execPath --eval <worker> -- cwd (the Electron binary with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE in desktop) under Semaphore(2), with Effect.timeout('5 seconds') wrapped around both the permit wait and the child.

Measured on the user's 26 roots: Electron child p50 58 ms → 755 ms for all 26; the identical probing in-process takes 1.1 ms. Only 3 of 26 roots have an icon, so 23 children per connection return null.

Reliability: past roughly 170 projects (fewer on a cold disk or slow Electron startup), queued requests exceed 5 s and return null. The client then caches null for 5 min and shows the folder fallback. Over a hub relay, icons travel base64-encoded inside RPC frames (up to 512 KiB, ≈683 KiB encoded).

Proposal

1. Server cache keyed by workspaceRoot: {path|null, bytes hash, fingerprint}. The fingerprint is the mtimes of root/public/app/src/assets, validated by stat. Keep it in-memory (LRU) and persisted (small table or state-dir JSON); cache negative results too.

2. Batch worker: one child resolves many roots, keeping per-root deadlines and the cloud-file isolation → 1 spawn instead of P.

3. Add an iconRevision (hash) to the project shell. Clients then cache across reconnects and tabs (Cache Storage/IndexedDB keyed by environment+project+revision) and skip the RPC entirely. On local/desktop, serve a GET with ETag and immutable caching.

4. Gate sidebar icon requests on the existing useHasIntersectedViewport.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Verified:

  • SidebarProjectHeader.tsx:105-111 renders ProjectFavicon unconditionally.
  • ProjectFavicon.tsx:35-67 issues an RPC when connected and capabilities.projectIcons is true. ServerEnvironment.ts:95 sets it true.
  • The requestKey includes connectedAt. The client cache (client-runtime/connection/projectIconSource.ts:14-46) is reset whenever the generation (the connection status object) changes, with a 5 min TTL, so it is lost on reconnect or new tab.
  • Server: projectRpc.ts:29-50 → readProjectIcon.ts:21-36 → ProjectFaviconResolver.ts:10-20, with Semaphore(2) and a 5 s timeout around both the permit wait and the child. No cache.
  • readProjectFavicon.ts:42-57 execFiles process.execPath with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE and a 1.5 s per-child timeout.
  • Measured numbers in favicon-timing.txt match: 755 ms per 26 projects with the Electron binary, 1.2 ms in-process.

The child-process design is deliberate isolation for blocking cloud-backed file opens (projectFaviconWorker.ts:1-6). Any parent-side stat fingerprint must preserve that guarantee, and timed-out results must not be negative-cached as 'no icon'.

This is not on any critical render path (icons fill in late), so it costs CPU/RAM churn and repeated work per connection rather than latency to first paint.

Part of Priority 10: Sidebar and projects: stop running the full VCS pipeline per row

Expected gain

Feature-branch local status: 20 → ≈6 spawns (≈210-360 ms → ≈80-120 ms here; more on Windows). Remote status: ≈24 → ≈4 spawns + gh. ≈ -35 spawns per feature-branch folder on first load, and on every refresh after agent actions

What happens today

For a non-default branch, readStatusDetailsLocal runs resolveBaseBranchForNoUpstream twice: once via computeAheadCountAgainstBase and once via readCommittedAgainstBase. Each run is 4 sequential spawns: config gh-merge-base, remote get-url origin, symbolic-ref origin/HEAD, show-ref. As a result remote get-url origin runs 3× per status and symbolic-ref origin/HEAD 3×. GitManager.readLocalStatus adds 2 git config --get spawns (resolveHostingProvider).

GitManager.readRemoteStatus then calls gitCore.statusDetails, which re-runs readStatusDetailsLocal (≈15 spawns) instead of reusing the local result it just cached. It adds 3 more config reads (resolveBranchHeadContext) and provider detection (git remote -v, 5 s TTL). The same remote -v data is cached separately by RepositoryIdentityResolver (60 s) and resolveHostingProvider (uncached).

Measured: 20 spawns / 213-360 ms for a feature-branch local status vs 9 / 98 ms on main. The remote half adds ≈24 more.

Proposal

Introduce a per-repository RepoFacts cache keyed by gitCommonDir and validated by stat of <commonDir>/config, packed-refs and refs/remotes/*/HEAD. It holds remotes+URLs, primary remote, default branch, and branch.*.{remote,merge,gh-merge-base,pushRemote}, loaded from ONE git config -z --list --local plus ONE git for-each-ref over the candidate refs. Use it from GitVcsDriverCore, GitManager, SourceControlProviderRegistry.detectProviderContext and RepositoryIdentityResolver.

Memoize the base branch per (commonDir, refName). For remote status, consume GitManager's cached local details and compute ahead/behind with a single git rev-list --left-right --count @{upstream}...HEAD. Validate with the existing VcsDriverContractHarness.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Verified in GitVcsDriverCore:

  • For a non-default branch, readStatusDetailsLocal (1423-1604) calls computeAheadCountAgainstBase (1303-1324) once and readCommittedAgainstBase (1352-1385) once. Each calls resolveBaseBranchForNoUpstream (1250-1300), which runs config gh-merge-base, then resolvePrimaryRemoteName (remote get-url origin), then symbolic-ref, then show-ref. These are sequential.
  • remote get-url origin therefore runs 3× (originRemoteExists in the status wave plus 2 base resolutions), and symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD also runs 3×.
  • GitManager.readLocalStatus adds 2-3 config reads (resolveHostingProvider at 894-912).
  • readRemoteStatus re-runs the full readStatusDetailsLocal through statusDetails, and resolveBranchHeadContext adds 3 config reads.
  • Measured 20 vs 9 spawns (status-pipeline.txt) matches this accounting.

Minor inaccuracy: resolveHostingProvider uses git config --get reads, not remote -v. The remote -v duplication is between RepositoryIdentityResolver and SourceControlProviderRegistry.detectProviderContext (listRemotes, cached 5 s per cwd).

The proposal is sound and nothing like a RepoFacts cache exists.

Part of Priority 10: Sidebar and projects: stop running the full VCS pipeline per row

Expected gain

PR network calls become per repo instead of per branch (5× fewer at 5 worktrees per repo). ≈100-350 ms less per call and ≈7× fewer bytes

What happens today

findLatestPr loops over 1-3 head selectors, running gh pr list --head X --state all --limit 20 --json GITHUB_PULL_REQUEST_LIST_JSON_FIELDS for each. That field set includes mergeable (which makes GitHub compute mergeability), comments, statusCheckRollup, reviewDecision, additions/deletions/changedFiles, labels, assignees and author. toStatusPr keeps only number/title/url/baseRef/headRef/state. Worktree PR discovery (refreshWorktreeSourceControlState → discoverPullRequest) goes through the same remoteStatus path.

Measured on ~/Code/ryco: full fields 702-1003 ms / 2,462 B vs a lean set 586-674 ms / 329 B. One repo-wide lean list (100 PRs) took 807-876 ms and covers every branch in that repo.

Each call is also a Go process start. 30 projects × 5 worktrees means up to 150 per-branch calls, at unbounded concurrency.

Proposal

1. Add a lean field set for status and discovery: number, title, url, state, headRefName, baseRefName, updatedAt, isDraft, isCrossRepository, headRepositoryOwner.

2. Add a per-repository PR index service keyed by (provider, owner/repo) that serves every worktree and folder of that repo. Back it with one gh pr list --state all --limit 100 --json <lean> (or one GraphQL query batching several heads), single-flight and cached 60 s. Fall back to a per-branch query only for branches missing from the recent 100.

3. Apply the same to the GitLab, Forgejo, Bitbucket and Azure list calls.

The '150 per-branch calls' figure is an upper bound that needs every folder visible or swept. Discovery is interval-gated by claimDiscovery.

Part of Priority 10: Sidebar and projects: stop running the full VCS pipeline per row

Expected gain

Peak concurrent children: hundreds → ≈8-12. Bounded spawn bursts keep the event loop responsive, and interactive git operations no longer queue behind background sweeps

What happens today

VcsProcess.spawn has no semaphore. Status sub-steps use concurrency: 'unbounded'. Single-flight in VcsStatusBroadcaster prevents duplicate work per folder, but not across folders. refreshLinkedWorktreeSourceControlStates forks one detached fiber per worktree.

Only identity (4), reconcile (4) and favicons (2) have local limits. RepositoryIdentityResolver bypasses VcsProcess entirely, using processRunner.runProcess with shell:true on Windows (an extra cmd.exe per git call) and no metrics.

Measured: 1.31 ms of main-thread time per spawn() in a 466 MiB process. A first sidebar render can launch about 1,000 git processes in a burst, competing with agents' builds for CPU and disk.

Proposal

Add a ProcessGovernor service used by VcsProcess, processRunner and the forge CLIs. Give it global permits (git ≈ min(8, cores); gh/glab/az ≈ 4) and two lanes: interactive (focused thread, user-initiated RPC) and background (sidebar, reconcile, discovery, migration), with background yielding to interactive. Record queue-wait and in-flight metrics. Move RepositoryIdentityResolver onto VcsProcess.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

Verified:

  • VcsProcess.spawn (VcsProcess.ts:105-160) has no semaphore.
  • The status sub-wave uses concurrency 'unbounded' (GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1449-1468).
  • Single-flight is per cwd only (VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:144-210).
  • refreshLinkedWorktreeSourceControlStates forkDetaches one fiber per worktree (context.ts:350-366).
  • RepositoryIdentityResolver uses processRunner.runProcess with shell on win32 (processRunner.ts:150-155).
  • The only Semaphores in vcs/git/sourceControl are per-destination locks; the local limits are identity (4), reconcile (4) and favicon (2).

Overstated: 'hundreds' of peak concurrent children. Each folder's pipeline is mostly sequential, peaking at about 3 concurrent git processes per folder. With 30 folders loading at once, a realistic peak is ≈30-90 git children plus gh, not hundreds. The ≈1,000 figure is the total over the load window, not a simultaneous burst.

The proposal (a global governor with interactive/background lanes) is still valuable and not implemented.

Expected gain

-2 spawns and ≈20-25 ms per detection. This applies to every status refresh, every listRefs call, and each project in a reconcile pass (30 per pass)

What happens today

detectRepository spawns rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree, then --show-toplevel, then --git-common-dir, one after another. VcsDriverRegistry caches the result for 2 s; VcsProjectConfig.resolveKind also walks up directories looking for a config file. Every GitWorkflowService status, localStatus, remoteStatus, listWorktreePaths and listLocalBranchNames call goes through detection first, so nearly every non-burst operation pays it.

Measured: 31.5-37.7 ms for the three spawns vs 10.9-12.0 ms for one git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree --show-toplevel --git-common-dir, which prints the same three lines.

Proposal

Use the single combined rev-parse (a non-repo shows up as a nonzero exit code). Cache per folder for minutes, validated by fs.stat of <cwd>/.git (file or directory: inode/mtime). Invalidate explicitly on worktree create/remove and project init.

  • Measured 31-38 ms vs 11-12 ms (detect-repo.txt).

Note: the 2 s cache already absorbs the remote leg that follows a local status load, so the saving applies to each independent load or refresh, not to every call. Still a clean quick win.

Expected gain

≈60% fewer rows decoded per shell snapshot on real data (≈2-6 ms each); multiplied by the call counts in reconcile-worktrees-snapshot-amplification

What happens today

listThreadRows has no WHERE clause and evaluates the correlated latestCompletedTurnAt subquery for every row. listThreadSessionRows returns sessions for all threads. getShellSnapshot then filters deletedAt === null after decoding.

On the user's DB: 753 thread rows vs 282 live (63% wasted). The thread query drops from 3.55 ms to 1.37 ms with WHERE deleted_at IS NULL; sessions drop from 702 to 280 rows when joined to live threads. Approximate decode cost is 3.0 ms per 753 rows.

This runs per client subscription, per priority refresh and per internal caller, and 2P+1 times in each reconcile pass.

Proposal

Add WHERE deleted_at IS NULL to a dedicated shell thread query. Keep the unfiltered query for getCommandReadModel and getSnapshot, which also use listThreadRows. Join sessions to live threads. Compute the snapshot's updatedAt with SELECT MAX(updated_at) aggregates so its semantics are unchanged. Optionally add a partial index on (created_at, thread_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Verified:

  • listThreadRows (ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:625-666) has no WHERE clause and evaluates the correlated latestCompletedTurnAt subquery (515-527) for every row.
  • listThreadSessionRows (941-962) returns all sessions.
  • getShellSnapshot filters deletedAt === null only after decoding (2690-2700). The updatedAt loop (2628-2655) does include deleted rows, so the proposal's MAX() aggregate is needed to keep semantics.
  • Row counts 753 vs 282 are consistent with my bench (282 live threads).

The gain is small per snapshot (a few ms); it is multiplied only by the reconcile amplification.

What happens today

listRefs runs git branch, then concurrently git branch --remotes, git remote, git symbolic-ref origin/HEAD, git worktree list --porcelain and for-each-ref … committerdate. It then stats every worktree path sequentially (yield* in a loop) and paginates in memory (limit 100). Each next-page request repeats the whole listing, and the client refetches every 60 s while the list is visible.

Measured on ~/Code/ryco (1,112 refs, 32 worktrees): 63-85 ms for this pattern vs 28-30 ms for one git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)%09%(committerdate:unix)%09%(HEAD)%09%(worktreepath)%09%(symref)' refs/heads refs/remotes, which yields the same data.

Proposal

Replace with a single for-each-ref, with remote names coming from the RepoFacts cache proposed in status-pipeline-redundant-git-calls. Cache the parsed list per gitCommonDir, validated by packed-refs and refs mtimes, so later pages and polls are free. Stat worktree paths concurrently, or use the prunable marker from worktree list --porcelain.

Expected gain

Removes repeated 9-20-spawn recomputations per row when scrolling the sidebar; fewer observers to allocate on first render

What happens today

Every thread row mounts its own IntersectionObserver. With 30 projects × 5 worktrees × 5-thread previews expanded that is up to ≈750 rows; the project list is not virtualized, only per-project thread lists above 20 rows are.

When a row leaves the viewport plus its 160 px margin, enabled turns false, the watch refCount drops to 0 and the RPC stream unsubscribes. Scrolling back resubscribes. The server recomputes local status if it is older than 5 s (9-20 spawns) and remote status if older than 30 s (fetch + gh), so fast scrolling through the sidebar produces bursts of status recomputation.

Proposal

Use one shared IntersectionObserver for the sidebar (a Map from element to callback). Keep status subscriptions alive for about 60 s after a row leaves the viewport, and delay enabling by about 150 ms so fling-scrolling never subscribes. On the server, check local-status freshness by stat of the gitdir's HEAD and index mtimes instead of a 5 s TTL, so unchanged checkouts are served from cache. Most of this becomes moot once sidebar-pr-badge-runs-full-vcs-pipeline lands.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

Verified:

  • useIsIntersectingViewport (useHasIntersectedViewport.ts:48-86) creates one IntersectionObserver per row and toggles back to false.
  • shouldEnableSidebarRowGitStatus (Sidebar.logic.ts:436-441) is isActive || isIntersecting.
  • watchGitStatus returns NOOP when disabled and unsubscribes at refCount 0 (gitStatusState.ts:121-147, 295-308).
  • The server TTLs are 5 s local and 30 s remote (VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:35-36, 340-363).
  • The project list is not virtualized; only thread lists above a threshold use LegendList.

Mitigations the finding underplays:

  • refCount is per folder across all rows, so a folder unsubscribes only when every row for it leaves the viewport.
  • Previews are limited to 6 per project and 5 per worktree.
  • The fetch is cached 15 s per repo, and the client keeps the last data on re-subscribe.

The '≈750 rows' figure needs everything expanded. Real churn is bounded and low impact. Hysteresis and a shared observer are reasonable small polish.

D. Hub connection and mobile

Connecting to a Hub 20 findings · 2 high · 8 medium · 10 low

~9–10 sequential browser↔Hub round trips plus 3–4 Hub↔node (≈0.9 s at 50 ms RTT, ≈2.4 s at 150 ms; estimates). Every relay drop establishes the connection twice.

How it works today (investigator's summary)

Hosted Hub cold start (installed PWA, deep link /node/<id>/<env>/<thread>) runs as one long chain of sequential round trips. The service worker serves offline.html, a boot document with no inline boot shell, along with the 75-file main closure. Root beforeLoad then awaits hostedHubController.bootstrap(), which is GET /api/auth/session on a fresh TCP+TLS connection followed, serially, by GET /api/nodes. Only after beforeLoad resolves does React start the lazy HostedHubRoot import (66 files, 1,796 KiB raw / 570 KiB gzip beyond boot, including a static RootAppShell import). The node-route orchestrator and connection coordinator that start the relay connection run in HostedHubRoot effects, so they wait for that chunk too. The connect itself is also serial: POST /api/relay/tickets (two POSTs against Hubs that reject minor 3), then a logical stream on the account Hub-session WebSocket. That WebSocket is opened only after the session check succeeds (TCP+TLS+upgrade, then ready). Next come relay auth→ready→channel.open/accept (Hub↔node) with the node's signed capability carrier, the client statement verification, and the Noise NX hello/ServerAccept round trip. Only then do the buffered subscriptions flush and the full shell snapshot plus thread window come back. Any unary read waits until the shell snapshot is accepted.

My count is about 9–10 sequential browser↔Hub RTTs plus 3–4 Hub↔node RTTs after JS boot. That is roughly 0.9 s at 50 ms RTT on desktop and roughly 2.4 s at 150 ms RTT on a mid-range phone (estimates; wire timing not observed). On top of that comes main-thread CPU. All relay/E2EE crypto is pure-JS @noble on the main thread: the cold first handshake measured about 25 ms on desktop V8 (estimated 100–150 ms on a phone). Each inbound 256 KiB chunk costs about 7 full copies, a strict CBOR re-encode-and-compare (189 µs on V8), and noble ChaCha20-Poly1305 open (about 770 µs). Nothing is compressed, and ciphertext defeats WebSocket deflate. For this user's DB I estimate the shell snapshot at about 363 KiB JSON, which deflates 8.9x to 41 KiB.

Reconnect is the worst case. A relay drop first completes a full transport-level re-establishment (ticket + stream + E2EE handshake). Once that reports online, the client is torn down and rebuilt with a second ticket, stream, handshake and full snapshot. Hosted connections never use the existing shell-sequence resume. The first ready of the Hub session always triggers a synthetic invalidation, which re-fetches the directory and every node's thread-cache shell. The node side does its HTTPS challenge and WebSocket open serially, and uses noble even though node:crypto is 6–30x faster for the same algorithms. The PWA install precaches about 713 files / 7.3 MiB gzip right at boot and re-downloads all of it on every deploy.

Category: WaterfallRisk: mediumInvestigator confidence: mediumhub-connection:relay-reconnect-double-establishment

Part of Priority 19: Connecting to a Hub

Expected gain

Saves ~3 RTT + 2 Hub↔node RTT + one E2EE handshake (est. 200-550 ms at 50-150 ms RTT) and one wasted shell-snapshot transfer + close exchange per relay drop. Halves ticket issuance and handshakes on the Hub/node during reconnect storms. Reliability: removes the case where the second attempt fails right after the first succeeded.

What happens today

On an unintentional close, HostedRelayAttemptFactory sets #requiresClientRecreation (transport.ts:493-501). WsTransport then reconnects on its own: fresh ticket, stream auth, channel accept and a full E2EE handshake. Only when that channel reports online (relayEngine #applyModeLock, after flushing the buffered resubscriptions) does connectionRecovered call recoverHostedRelayConnection → retrySelectedNode (transport.ts:244-269, 401-408). That bumps the generation and calls activateHostedNode. Because previous === node.environmentId, activateHostedNode calls resetRelayAttemptFactory + disconnectPrimaryEnvironment, then connectPrimaryEnvironment (environment.ts:75-90): a second ticket, a second stream, a second NX handshake, and a second shell snapshot + thread window on a brand-new client. The first channel is discarded mid-sync and still runs its authenticated E2EE close exchange. connectionClosed keeps the role precisely so the first channel's shell/session streams can resubscribe (state.ts:2347-2352), so the node very likely also starts producing a snapshot on the throwaway channel (inferred; not observed on the wire). The comment at transport.ts:257-262 shows this is a deliberate probe to avoid racing the node's ticket renewal.

Proposal

Make the re-establishment happen once. Preferred: adopt the reconnected channel as the replacement session. Keep the WsTransport client, let its already-resubscribed shell/thread streams run the existing replaying path (onResubscribe → markHostedSessionReplaying), and have the controller publish the new generation for that same attempt instead of disconnect+connect. Alternative, if a fresh client is mandatory: set persistentReconnect false for hosted transports and let the single owner (hostedHubController.retrySelectedNode with its HostedReconnectPolicy) perform the only reconnect. Handle the ticket-renewal race by treating one retryable channel_rejected inside that attempt as backoff rather than terminal, not by spending a whole handshake as a probe. Either way, add a test asserting one ticket and one handshake per drop. This touches the hosted lifecycle owner and must stay inside hostedHubController (AGENTS.md boundary).

Verifier (Confirmed)

Checked the cited code and the line numbers match. transport.ts:493-501 onClose sets #requiresClientRecreation and calls connectionClosed. WsTransport keeps reconnecting by itself (persistentReconnect:true at transport.ts:465, protocol.ts:272-287), with a fresh nextUrl ticket on every attempt. relayEngine #applyModeLock (relayEngine.ts:962-978) emits onTransportStatus('online') and then events.onOpen(), and that 'online' fires connectionRecovered (transport.ts:401-408), which runs recoverHostedRelayConnection → queueMicrotask → retrySelectedNode (transport.ts:244-269). #retrySelectedNode bumps the generation and calls activateHostedNode (state.ts:2225-2272). With previous===node.environmentId, activateHostedNode runs resetRelayAttemptFactory + disconnectPrimaryEnvironment + connectPrimaryEnvironment (environment.ts:75-90), so the result is a second ticket, stream, handshake and snapshot. The behaviour is deliberate, introduced in f16f62a71 (#430) to avoid racing the node's relay-ticket renewal. That commit's comment says the subscriptions 'belong to that client session'. In practice wsTransport.subscribe already re-runs streams on the same transport with onResubscribe (wsTransport.ts:205-230), and admitHostedRequestForState admits the 7 session-sync streams while the session is 'stale' (transport.ts:76-87), so the throwaway channel very likely resubscribes. The wasted snapshot depends on timing and is inferred, not observed. The node does not reconnect on a periodic schedule (no rotation in hubConnector), so how often this happens depends on how often the network drops or the Hub drains. Hub drain/deploy storms double ticket and handshake load, which is why the impact stays high.

Part of Priority 19: Connecting to a Hub

Expected gain

Removes the HostedHubRoot load+parse+mount time from the connect critical path. Est. 150-400 ms on a mid phone with a warm SW cache, 0.5-1.5 s on first visit at 150 ms RTT / 10 Mbit/s.

What happens today

Root beforeLoad awaits bootstrapWithHostedReadCache(() => hostedHubController.bootstrap()), which is 2+ RTTs (__root.tsx:121-131). Only then does RootRouteView render <HostedHubRoot/>, whose lazy import pulls 66 files / 1,795.7 KiB raw / 570.1 KiB gzip beyond boot, including a static RootAppShell import (HostedHubRoot.tsx:35; graph.txt). The code that starts the relay connection lives in HostedHubRoot effects: useHostedNodeRouteOrchestrator() and startHostedWorkspaceCoordinator() (HostedHubRoot.tsx:212-219). Both already exist as non-React start functions (nodeRouteOrchestrator.ts:427, hostedConnectionCoordinator.ts:428). So route-derived demand → selectNode → ticket cannot begin until that chunk graph is downloaded, parsed and mounted.

Proposal

(1) Fire void import("../components/hostedHub/HostedHubRoot") at the top of the hosted branch of resolveRootBeforeLoadContextAsync so the download/compile overlaps the session and directory RTTs. (2) Start startHostedNodeRouteOrchestrator() and startHostedWorkspaceCoordinator() from the hosted boot gate, right after ensureWebHostedRuntimeConfigured(), and have HostedHubRoot only subscribe. The controller remains the only lifecycle owner; it is just invoked earlier. (3) Make HostedHubRoot load RootAppShell lazily, so sign-in, directory and account surfaces do not parse the workspace shell.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Confirmed: __root.tsx:121-131 awaits bootstrapWithHostedReadCache(bootstrap), and HostedHubRoot is a React.lazy rendered only in RootRouteView after beforeLoad resolves (__root.tsx:32-36, 226-233). HostedHubRoot.tsx:35 imports RootAppShell statically. The relay connect owners start only in HostedHubRoot effects: useHostedNodeRouteOrchestrator at :212 and startHostedWorkspaceCoordinator at :213-219. useHostedBrowserLifecycle at :222 (the lifecycle listeners) is also late. startHostedNodeRouteOrchestrator (nodeRouteOrchestrator.ts:427-443) depends only on the store and the installed hosted history (main.tsx:27-28), so starting it at the gate is feasible. graph.txt:137-138 confirms 66 files / 1,795.7 KiB raw / 570.1 KiB gzip beyond boot (standard build). The routed thread chunk (~0.9 MiB gzip per EVIDENCE) likewise starts loading only after root beforeLoad, so prefetching it too during bootstrap is worth adding. The impact estimates are plausible but not measured.

Prior work

Bundle composition is covered in EVIDENCE.md (HostedHubRoot 66 files / 1,796 KiB beyond boot). The orchestration ordering and prefetch are new.

Part of Priority 19: Connecting to a Hub

Expected gain

-1 RTT on every cold start and every foreground resume (50 ms @50 ms RTT, 150 ms @150 ms). Early socket: up to -1 more RTT on the connect critical path when WebSocket is not multiplexed over HTTP/2.

What happens today

#restoreAccess awaits restoreSession(GET /api/auth/session), patches authenticated, then awaits refreshDirectory(GET /api/nodes) (state.ts:621-636). #resumeBrowser does the same serial pair on every foreground/online recovery (state.ts:1850-1860). Both requests carry the same ambient cookie or bearer token, so the second does not depend on data from the first. watchWebHostedHubSession opens /v1/relay/session only once accountStatus is authenticated (hubSession.ts:44). On a non-H2 WebSocket that is a new TCP+TLS+upgrade (~3 RTT) starting one RTT later than necessary, and it gates every logical stream (createSocket waits for ready).

Proposal

Inside the single owner, start listNodes concurrently with restoreSession under the same AbortController. Hold the nodes result and only commit it via the existing #refreshDirectory path after the session answer validates (discard it on 401 or a different account/session id). Do the same in #resumeBrowser. Optionally start the Hub-session socket at bootstrap begin, but publish neither readiness nor failure (a 4401 must not call expireSession) until restoreSession settles. This keeps lifecycle authority with hostedHubController.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Confirmed that #restoreAccess awaits restoreSession and then awaits refreshDirectory (state.ts:621-636), and #resumeBrowser does the same at state.ts:1850-1860. listNodes (api.ts:2418) needs nothing from the session response in cookie mode. Two caveats. (1) In bearer mode #restoreNativeSession may rotate the token (api.ts:2312-2318). A parallel listNodes sent with the pre-rotation token could get a 401 if the Hub revokes the old token at once, so a speculative 401 must not count as authoritative (or bearer mode stays serial). (2) The Hub-session socket already opens as soon as accountStatus becomes authenticated: configureWebHostedRuntime → watchWebHostedHubSession (runtime.ts:87, hubSession.ts:44). That runs in parallel with GET /api/nodes, not after it. Starting it earlier saves at most 1 RTT on socket readiness, and only matters when socket readiness, rather than directory + chunk + ticket, is the critical path. The main gain of -1 RTT per cold start and per foreground resume holds.

Part of Priority 19: Connecting to a Hub

Expected gain

Worst-case time to an actionable UI on a stalled network drops from 30-60 s to ~8 s. No change on healthy networks.

What happens today

Every Hub request uses REQUEST_DEADLINE_MS = 30,000 (api.ts:161, 2963-2968). Root beforeLoad awaits bootstrap (__root.tsx:128). Unless a remembered-browser local restore wins the race (readCache.ts:526), it waits for restoreSession and then for refreshDirectory, because #restoreAccess awaits refreshDirectory (state.ts:635). On a black-holed network (captive portal, dead Wi-Fi without an RST) the user sees only AppBootLoadingSurface for up to 30 s, or ~60 s if the session answers and /api/nodes then stalls. Only then does the access-retry state render.

Proposal

Use a short boot-phase deadline for the gate-critical reads (e.g. 8 s), passed as an option to #request. Do not await refreshDirectory inside the beforeLoad gate: the directory already has its own loading/stale states. Let the existing access-retry backoff take over sooner, so HostedHubRoot renders its checking/unavailable surface with Retry.

Verifier (Confirmed)

REQUEST_DEADLINE_MS = 30_000 (api.ts:161) applies to every #request (api.ts:2963-2968). beforeLoad awaits bootstrap (__root.tsx:128), and #restoreAccess awaits refreshDirectory inside it (state.ts:635). #refreshDirectory swallows errors into 'stale' rather than throwing, so a stalled /api/nodes after a good session holds the gate for up to another 30 s. readCache's local race (readCache.ts:526) helps only users who opted into 'remember this browser' (default false). On networks that fail fast (offline, RST, captive portal answering quickly) fetch rejects early, so the 30-60 s worst case applies to black-holed links only. This is a real reliability issue.

Part of Priority 19: Connecting to a Hub

Expected gain

Dead-socket detection after a network change drops from ≤45 s to ~5 s. Recovery then follows the normal fast path.

What happens today

HostedHubSession detects loss only through its 20 s ping / 45 s lastReceived bound (hostedHubSession.ts:358-387). recoverAfterConnectivity returns early for a store that looks healthy (transport online, session ready/synchronizing; state.ts:684-694). After a Wi-Fi→cellular handoff or NAT rebinding without an offline event, the account socket and all logical streams can be dead while the UI shows online and RPCs stall, for up to 45 s. The node connector solves the same problem with a 5 s probe on suspicion (LIVENESS_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000, HubConnector.ts:66-76).

Proposal

Add HostedHubSession.probe(timeoutMs = 5000): send a ping immediately and call #lost('network', true) if no pong arrives in time. Call it from the web lifecycle binding on visibility→visible, online, pageshow and NetworkInformation change, and when an RPC has been pending longer than ~5 s. Failures flow through the existing #lost → onFailure → controller path, so lifecycle ownership is unchanged.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

The 20 s / 45 s heartbeat bound is confirmed (hostedHubSession.ts:358-387; contracts/hubSession.ts:13-14), as is recoverAfterConnectivity skipping healthy states (state.ts:680-697) and the node's 5 s probe (HubConnector.ts:66-76). One overstatement: each logical relay channel also runs Effect RpcClient's pinger, defaulting to an 8 s interval and 16 s timeout (effect/src/rpc/RpcClient.ts:1087, 1276-1279; no override in client-runtime or web). A dead path therefore usually takes the selected node's transport out of 'online' within about 16-24 s, not 45 s. Recovery still cannot finish until HostedHubSession notices: new logical streams are opened on the dead account socket because #ready is still true, and directory and thread-cache invalidations stop. So up to 45 s to a working reconnect still stands, and the probe proposal is valid.

Prior work

Part of Priority 19: Connecting to a Hub

Expected gain

First visit: up to ~7 MiB less competing download during startup. Updates: re-download only changed chunks instead of ~7.3 MiB. Installed launch: immediate branded paint plus a flatter module waterfall (est. tens to 150 ms on phones).

What happens today

resolveHostedPwaPrecache walks every dynamicImport from the entry (buildArtifacts.ts:78-91), so the install-time cache.addAll covers essentially every fingerprinted asset. On the current dist that is approx. 713 files, 26.09 MiB raw, 7.33 MiB gzip. Registration starts at boot (main.tsx:70-72; register immediately when readyState is complete, lifecycle.ts:217-221), so the install competes with first-visit critical requests (session, nodes, HostedHubRoot, thread chunks). addAll is all-or-nothing on flaky mobile links. Every deploy changes CACHE_NAME and the new worker refetches all URLs instead of reusing unchanged immutable entries from the previous ryco-pwa-shell-* cache (activate deletes it, 140-146). Navigations are answered with offline.html (164-166), whose boot variant has only a background style and <script type=module src=main> (offlineDocument.ts:14-16): no inline boot shell/logo (dist/index.html has one) and no modulepreload. Installed PWAs show a blank screen until the 75-file main graph is discovered level by level through the SW and executed.

Proposal

(1) Precache only the boot closure plus HostedHubRoot and the thread-route closure at install. Cache other fingerprinted chunks on first fetch inside the fetch handler (same allowlist pattern, immutable static assets only; no API/relay/authenticated data, so the SW boundary is respected). (2) During install, copy each URL already present in an older ryco-pwa-shell-* cache into the new cache and fetch only the missing ones. (3) Defer registration until hosted browserStatus is current or the first idle period. (4) Generate the boot document from the built index.html (inline themed boot shell) and add <link rel=modulepreload> for the boot closure so the SW serves all 75 files in parallel.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

Confirmed that resolveHostedPwaPrecache walks dynamicImports/imports/css/assets from the entries (buildArtifacts.ts:67-100), install does cache.addAll (136-138), activate deletes the old ryco-pwa-shell-* caches (140-146), registration starts at boot (main.tsx:70-72, lifecycle.ts:217-221), and the boot offline document has no boot shell or modulepreload (offlineDocument.ts:14-16). Corrections: (a) precache-size.mjs counts every fingerprinted file in dist rather than the reachable set, so 713 files / 7.33 MiB is an upper-bound approximation. (b) 'Re-downloads all on every deploy' is overstated: addAll fetches go through the HTTP cache, so unchanged immutable assets may come from disk cache, depending on the Hub's Cache-Control headers. The Hub is not in this repo, so this is unknown. (c) The SW answers every navigation cache-first with offline.html (buildArtifacts.ts:164-166), so the missing boot shell affects every SW-controlled hosted visit, not only installed PWAs. The precache-bandwidth contention on a first mobile visit is real.

Part of Priority 14: Trim the JS on the boot and thread paths

Expected gain

≈320 KiB raw (est. ~100 KiB gzip) less boot JS for every standard/desktop launch. Hosted boot graph shrinks by the noble/E2EE share (≈120 KiB raw) without adding latency.

What happens today

service.ts statically imports hostedHubController/useHostedHubStore from ~/hostedHub/state and helpers from ~/hostedHub/transport. state.ts statically imports configureWebHostedRuntime (./runtime) just to register a 'lazy' configurator. runtime.ts imports e2eeAttempt.ts, which imports the @ryco/client-runtime/relay barrel. That barrel re-exports relayE2eeInitiator/Channel, dpop and webauthn (index.ts:1-12), which pulls shared/relayE2eeHandshake, Noise, Session and Close and @noble/{curves,hashes,ciphers}. main.tsx statically imports hostedHub/nodeRoutes and pwa/lifecycle. EVIDENCE attributes ≈320 KiB raw of this (authorization 74, relay 45, noble 65, relayE2ee ≈57, components/hostedHub 25, HostedConnectionControls 34, coordinator 11, readCache 8) to every standard and desktop boot. In hosted builds, the same E2EE/noble code is eager although it is first needed at channel.accept.

Proposal

Split @ryco/client-runtime/relay into subpath exports (engine/session, e2ee, dpop, webauthn) with no barrel re-export of E2EE. Make the web configurator an async dynamic import of ./runtime guarded by the build-time constant import.meta.env.VITE_RYCO_CLIENT_MODE === "hosted-hub" so Rolldown drops hosted modules from standard builds. Do the same for main.tsx's hosted imports. In hosted builds, start import() of the E2EE initiator when the account becomes authenticated so it is ready before channel.accept. Extend webBundleSplitting.test.ts to guard against regressions.

Verifier (Confirmed)

The chain is verified. service.ts:90-101 statically imports ~/hostedHub/state and ~/hostedHub/transport. state.ts:17 imports ./runtime statically, then registers the lazy configurator at :26. runtime.ts:13 imports ./e2eeAttempt, which imports makeRelayE2eeInitiator from the @ryco/client-runtime/relay barrel (e2eeAttempt.ts:2-9). The barrel re-exports dpop, ecdsa, webauthn, relayE2eeInitiator and relayE2eeChannel (relay/index.ts:1-12). main.tsx:9-10 imports nodeRoutes and pwa/lifecycle. Splitting the barrel alone is not enough, because e2eeAttempt needs the initiator directly; the cut that matters is state.ts→runtime.ts (and service.ts→hostedHub/transport). isHostedHubMode reads the build-time constant import.meta.env.VITE_RYCO_CLIENT_MODE (env.ts:12-18), so guarded dynamic imports can be dead-code-eliminated. EVIDENCE.md already records the eager presence; the chain and the split plan are new. The benefit mostly lands in the standard/desktop boot scenario, not Hub connect.

Part of Priority 19: Connecting to a Hub

Expected gain

-1 RTT per connect/reconnect/resume (50-150 ms) and one fewer authenticated HTTP request per attempt on the Hub.

What happens today

nextUrl() awaits POST /api/relay/tickets (with CSRF) before any socket exists (transport.ts:332-341). Only then does createSocket open a logical stream on the account Hub-session socket, which the Hub authenticated from the session cookie at upgrade. The stream's first relay frame then presents the ticket (relayEngine.ts:484-496, 734-753). The ticket is therefore a full extra browser↔Hub RTT on every connect, every reconnect, and every foreground resume. hub-session-protocol.md v1 defines open with an empty payload.

Proposal

Hub-session protocol v2 (Hub + client change, versioned through the ready protocol byte): an open frame carrying {nodeId, capability, protocolMinor}. The Hub mints and consumes the single-use ticket internally under the socket's cookie session and answers with the relay ready. Keep the v1 HTTP ticket path for older Hubs. Ticket custody stays server-side and nothing new is persisted. Until then, for route restore, request the ticket in parallel with the directory refresh and discard it (single-use, short-lived) if the routed node fails validation. That variant touches the documented restore order in hosted-hub-client.md, so flag it.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Confirmed: nextUrl awaits issueRelayTicket (POST /api/relay/tickets, csrf:true; api.ts:2621-2663) before createSocket (transport.ts:303-372). The Hub-session open frame has an empty payload (hub-session-protocol.md:23), and the ticket travels in the stream's first relay auth data frame (relayEngine.ts:484-496, 735-753). open is pipelined without an ack (hostedHubSession.ts:258-269), so the extra cost is exactly the ticket RTT. This needs a Hub-side protocol change (the Hub is not in this repo). The fallback variant of issuing the ticket in parallel with the directory changes the documented restore order. Estimate of -1 RTT per connect is plausible.

Part of Priority 19: Connecting to a Hub

Expected gain

Reconnect transfer drops from ~363 KiB (est.) to the event delta (typically a few KiB). That saves ~300 ms at 10 Mbit/s, ~1.2 ms decrypt on desktop (est. ~6 ms on phone) and the snapshot Schema decode and hydrate per reconnect.

What happens today

createEnvironmentConnectionHandlers enables readShellResumeSequence only when options.resumeShell === true && hostedGeneration === null (service.ts:807), and the primary connection passes { resumeShell: hostedGeneration === null } (1187). Hosted connections are therefore always excluded. Combined with activateHostedNode rebuilding the client on every recovery (environment.ts:75-90), each hosted reconnect, foreground resume and node revisit downloads, decrypts, parses and hydrates the full OrchestrationShellSnapshot plus thread windows. The shell for this user's DB is an estimated ~363 KiB JSON (282 live threads). The node already supports resumed replies with fromSequence (connection.ts:224-233).

Proposal

Let hosted connections offer resumeFromSequence when account session, environment, node identity and effective role are unchanged since the baseline. Persist the baseline sequence in memory only, keyed by environment and generation lineage. Treat the node's resumed reply as the authoritative current baseline: it is issued by the node, and the Hub cannot forge it on an E2EE channel. Keep mutations gated until it arrives. Fall back to a full snapshot on any mismatch, role change or delivery-unknown. This changes the 'accept a current shell snapshot' rule in AGENTS.md / hosted-hub-client.md, so it needs explicit sign-off.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

service.ts:807 and :1187 do exclude hosted connections. This is a deliberate policy, not an oversight: commit 63a7f714a ('perf: resume the shell stream after a reconnect') says 'Hosted sessions keep taking a fresh snapshot: they must accept a current shell before regaining mutation authority', and docs/hosted-hub-client.md:381 says 'Nothing is resumed'. Enabling readShellResumeSequence alone would not help. connection.ts:215-219, 253-258 resume only on top of a baseline 'this connection established itself' (hasShellBaseline is per connection), and hosted recovery always builds a new connection: activateHostedNode on drop, suspendHostedNode/resume on foreground. A cross-connection baseline is therefore required, or finding #1 (keep the client) has to land first. Prior work should cite 63a7f714a. Risk stays high, and effort is larger than stated.

docs/research/performance-efficiency-size-improvements.md:265 suggests making shell snapshots more selective. This is different: it enables the existing resume for hosted connections.

Part of Priority 19: Connecting to a Hub

Expected gain

Shell snapshot 363 → ~41 KiB (est. ~300 → ~35 ms at 10 Mbit/s). Proportionally less AEAD, codec and copy CPU, and slower transfer-budget consumption.

What happens today

Records are sealed directly over raw RPC JSON (Session:1181-1185) and no compression exists anywhere in relay/E2EE code (grep). ChaCha20-Poly1305 ciphertext is incompressible, so permessage-deflate on browser↔Hub or Hub↔node sockets cannot help E2EE channels. Measured on this user's data: the estimated 363 KiB shell compresses to 41 KiB with deflate-raw (8.9x) or 31 KiB with brotli; deflate L1 takes 1.43 ms and inflate 0.27 ms on desktop. The capacity doc measures base64 PNG screenshot frames at 3,053,100 B (phone) and 5,569,884 B (tablet), which exhaust the 50 MiB per-channel transfer budget in 17-18 / 9-10 frames.

Proposal

Add negotiated compress-then-encrypt for large server→client RPC messages: an RPC-level or inner-record flag, only for bodies ≥ ~16 KiB, using a fresh deflate-raw context per message (CompressionStream/DecompressionStream in the browser, zlib on node). Keep it off for client→node traffic and small interactive messages. Separately, send screenshot frames as binary instead of base64 JSON (-25%). Security flag: compression before encryption leaks plaintext length to the Hub, which is the adversary in the E2EE threat model (CRIME/BREACH class). It needs explicit review and must exclude messages that mix Hub-influenced data with secrets.

Verifier (Confirmed)

No payload compression exists in the relay or E2EE paths. grep finds 'compress' only in key/point-encoding and deviceFrame contexts. Records seal raw RPC bytes. shell-size.txt (363 KiB → 41 KiB deflate-raw) is an estimate built from DB rows mapped to the thread-shell shape, with projects and worktrees left empty, so the real snapshot is probably somewhat larger. Base64 PNG frames gain only about 25% from deflate, so the binary-frame suggestion matters more there. The compress-before-encrypt length-leak concern against an adversarial Hub is correctly flagged and needs crypto review. Kept medium impact for slow mobile links, with L effort and high risk.

Expected gain

-1 GET /api/nodes, -N thread-cache shell GETs (N ≤ 16 eligible nodes, ≤3 concurrent) and -1 thread GET per cold start and per session (re)connect, plus fewer store patches and re-renders while the first connect is in progress.

What happens today

HostedHubSession.#receive calls #notifyInvalidation({directory: true, threadCache: true}) on every ready, including the very first one (hostedHubSession.ts:202). The intent is to catch changes missed while disconnected, but on a cold start nothing was missed. The web binding forwards this to notifyDirectoryInvalidated, which starts a second GET /api/nodes, or queues a follow-up read if one is in flight (state.ts:1941-1974). The thread-cache controller bumps invalidationVersion, re-queues every node shell read (including in-flight ones, via the version check in finally, threadReadCache.ts:139-149) and re-reads the routed thread (271-276). Separately, #refreshDirectory always patches a new nodes array (state.ts:2054-2065) even when nothing changed. That invalidates identity-based checks (readCache.ts:334, 341) and re-renders every nodes selector.

Proposal

Synthesize the reconnect invalidation only after a loss (track an #everReady flag in HostedHubSession, or pass {reconnect: true} through onInvalidate). Alternatively, skip it when the last successful directory/thread-cache read started after the socket's connect began. In #refreshDirectory, keep the previous array when the new list is deep-equal by id, environmentId, effectiveRole, presence and capabilities.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Confirmed: hostedHubSession.ts:196-202 calls #notifyInvalidation({directory:true, threadCache:true}) on every first ready. hubSession.ts:65-69 forwards it to notifyDirectoryInvalidated, which starts a refresh or queues a follow-up (state.ts:1941-1974). The thread cache bumps invalidationVersion and re-queues reads (threadReadCache.ts:139-149, 196-200, 271-276). #refreshDirectory always patches a new nodes array (state.ts:2054-2065), which fails readCache's identity checks (readCache.ts:334, 341). Caveats: the duplicate thread-cache reads happen only if the coordinator (HostedHubRoot effect, hostedConnectionCoordinator.ts:900) has subscribed before the Hub session's ready arrives, which depends on timing. All of these requests run off the connect critical path. The cost is Hub load, bandwidth and re-renders, not latency on the critical path.

Expected gain

Opted-in users avoid est. 20-50 ms main-thread work every 750 ms on phones during streaming, and about 10-15 redundant encrypted IndexedDB writes per connect.

What happens today

When the opt-in feature is enabled: every hostedHubStore patch queues reconcile() (readCache.ts:482-503). With directoryStatus ready, reconcile publishes a new snapshot object, which re-renders useHostedReadCache consumers including HostedHubRoot, and writes the encrypted catalog to IndexedDB (348-380). A single connect produces roughly 10-15 patches (requesting-ticket, connecting, authenticating, opening-channel, role, online, synchronizing, ready…). useStore.subscribe(scheduleSave) (505) runs save() every 750 ms during streaming. save() rebuilds metadata for every node, captures up to 32 threads of messages, and runs JSON.stringify + TextEncoder of a record up to 1.9 MB inside a while loop that deletes one thread and re-stringifies each time (437-441, O(n²) worst case). It then AES-GCM encrypts and writes IndexedDB (hostedReadVault.ts:118-130). This is unconditional on whether anything changed.

Proposal

Track dirty environments and threads (compare message ids / updatedAt) and skip unchanged records. Skip the catalog write when the node id list is unchanged. Compute record size incrementally from cached per-thread serialized lengths instead of re-stringifying in a loop. Schedule saves with requestIdleCallback (keeping pagehide/hidden flushes). Publish only when nodes or snapshots actually change.

Verifier (Confirmed)

The code is as described. Impact is downgraded because the feature is default-off. For users who opt in, the during-streaming cost is real but its magnitude is estimated, not measured.

Expected gain

-2 to 3 Hub↔node RTT (TCP+TLS+upgrade; est. 60-450 ms) per node (re)connect after sleep/network change, shortening the window hosted users see the node offline.

What happens today

#authenticate first awaits createRelayAuthenticationFrame: POST /api/node/auth/challenges over undici with a new TLS connection on reconnect, then the identity signs (possibly a keychain read). Only afterwards does it call transport.open (RelayConnectionSession.ts:282-318). The auth frame goes out on open (336-351), and the connector then awaits readState and publishes the E2EE statement before going online (HubConnector.ts:1003-1033). During this window hosted clients get node_offline and back off.

Proposal

Open the WebSocket concurrently with the challenge request. Keep the auth bytes pending and send them in onOpen or when the proof resolves, whichever comes last. If the proof is not ready within (RELAY_AUTHENTICATION_DEADLINE_MS − 1 s) after open, close and retry serially. Longer-term (Hub change): let the Hub send the node challenge as the first WebSocket frame and drop the HTTPS preflight entirely.

Verifier (Confirmed)

#authenticate awaits createRelayAuthenticationFrame first (RelayConnectionSession.ts:282-290). That runs stateStore.readOrCreate, key selection, the HTTPS challenge request and the signature (HubNodeProofClient.ts:~173-215). Only after that is transport.open called (RelayConnectionSession.ts:314-324), and the auth frame is sent onOpen (336-351). This matters only on node (re)connect after sleep or a network change, which is outside the browser's cold-start path. The 2-3 RTT saving is plausible. The proof must still be sent before the challenge expires, and opening in parallel only shortens that window.

Expected gain
