What happens today

admitHostedRequestForState allows a non-stream request only when transport is online, browser is current and hostedSessionAdmits() is true, which requires sessionStatus === "ready" (capabilities.ts:27). That flips only after the shell snapshot is accepted (markHostedSessionReady). Only the 7 session-sync subscriptions in HOSTED_SESSION_SYNC_SUBSCRIPTIONS are admitted while synchronizing (transport.ts:35-43, 76-87). Every other read issued while the thread view mounts is held in awaiting-session, then sent, so it pays an extra browser↔Hub↔node round trip after the snapshot instead of being pipelined with it. RPC_DELIVERY_EFFECT_POLICY classifies 106 methods as read. capabilities.ts:18-25 itself states that reads only observe node state.

Proposal

In admitHostedRequestForState, admit requests whose rpcDeliveryEffectFor(tag) === "read" and whose role check passes with a fresh directory while transportStatus is online and browserStatus is current or synchronizing (the same window session-sync streams already get). Keep mutation and receipted methods gated on ready. The node still enforces role per request. This is read admission, not mutation readiness, but it lives in the hosted admission policy, so get owner sign-off.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

The waterfall exists, but the stated mechanism is wrong. Unary reads are not 'held then sent': protocol.ts:396-397 throws RpcRequestRefusedError('awaiting-session') at request start, so nothing is queued. Read freshness comes from two other places. First, environmentQueryRefresh fences active queries when a connection begins and refetches them only once isHostedEnvironmentQueryRefreshReady is true, which requires sessionStatus==='ready' (environmentQueryRefresh.ts:36-50, 96-107; service.ts:786-806; queryClient.ts:357-387). Second, capability hooks gate on hostedSessionAdmits (hostedHub/capabilities.ts:28, rpc/sourceControlReadAdmission.ts:51, settings/useDiagnosticsCapability.ts:34). Changing only admitHostedRequestForState would therefore not pipeline the reads. The fence/refresh coordinator and the capability hooks would also need changes, and the post-ready refresh could double-fetch. The thread view's primary data already comes through admitted sync subscriptions (subscribeThreadWindow, VCS status, server config), so few first-paint reads are affected. The 106 'read' count is correct (rpcAccessPolicy.ts).

Part of Priority 19: Connecting to a Hub

Expected gain

First connect: ~20-25 ms desktop, est. 80-140 ms mid phone off the main thread or overlapped with network. Each reconnect: ~2-3 ms desktop, est. 10-20 ms phone.

What happens today

A web NX connect performs one x25519 keygen, two DH, at least two Ed25519 verifies (statement signature at CapabilityVerify:303, prekey cross-signature at Transcripts:1865, plus one per continuity-chain link at :921), all through noble and all through the single sync choke point verifyE2eeSignature (Keys:430-450). Measured warm on V8: keygen 182 µs, DH 574 µs, Ed25519 verify 637 µs, ≈2.6+ ms. Measured cold in a fresh process: ≈25 ms on V8 (first x25519 ~13 ms, 2 verifies 8.9-9.9 ms) and ≈14 ms on JSC. Est. 100-150 ms on a mid Android phone. Native WebCrypto measured: X25519 deriveBits 31 µs, Ed25519 verify 51 µs (V8). The same statement bytes are fully re-verified on every reconnect.

Proposal

(a) S: pre-warm noble off the critical path. When accountStatus becomes authenticated (≥2 RTTs before channel.accept), run one throwaway x25519.getPublicKey on random bytes and one ed25519.verify on a fixed vector in requestIdleCallback. This fills noble's lazy precompute tables and JIT tiers. No security impact. (b) M: add a capability-detected WebCrypto fast path for X25519 (deriveBits) and Ed25519 verify on the client initiator, with noble fallback. The initiator's intercept is already async, so only the client call sites need an async variant of verifyE2eeSignature. Wire bytes are unchanged, but it needs crypto review (strict RFC 8032 / zip215:false semantics must be preserved, e.g. pre-check canonical encodings with the existing validators). (c) S: per tab, memoize the verified-statement verdict keyed by sha256(statement bytes), re-running only the time/policy checks on reconnect.

Verifier (Confirmed)

verifyE2eeSignature uses noble ed25519/p256 (relayE2eeKeys.ts:430-450). DH/keygen goes through noble x25519 (relayE2eeNoise.ts:921-968). Verify call sites are relayE2eeCapabilityVerify.ts:303 and relayE2eeTranscripts.ts:921 and :1865. Measurements in .perf-research/hub-connection/cold.txt add up to the claim: V8 is keygen 0.4-0.6 + 2xDH 2.1-2.7 + 2xverify 8.9-9.9 + aead 0.9 ms, plus about 13 ms first-call setup, so roughly 25 ms. JSC comes to about 14 ms. The phone figure of 100-150 ms is unmeasured. This adds a few tens of ms on desktop to a connect chain of about 1-2.4 s, so it is a small share. The pre-warm idea (a) is a cheap S win. Downgraded impact.

Part of Priority 19: Connecting to a Hub

Expected gain

Node event-loop time per MiB sealed drops from ~3.1 ms to ~0.55 ms. Per handshake ~1.3-3 ms down to ~0.1 ms. Screenshot fallback saves ~7.4 ms per frame on the node.

What happens today

Every record the node seals (shell snapshots, thread windows, streaming deltas, terminal output, screenshot frames) goes through suiteRecordAead → noble chacha20poly1305 on the node event loop (Session:402-411). The aeadFactory seam already exists but is wired only to testOnlyAeadFactory (Session:928). Measured on node 24.21: node:crypto chacha20-poly1305 1,859 MiB/s vs noble 327 MiB/s at 256 KiB; one measured 3,053,100 B screenshot record 1.74 ms vs 9.16 ms. Noble is faster only for ~256 B records (3.4 vs 7.8 µs). Handshake primitives: x25519 DH 19 vs 574 µs, Ed25519 verify 42 vs 637 µs, P-256 verify (native-tier client certificates) 51.5 vs 989 µs. The node also borrows the agreement secret from keytar on every handshake (NodeE2eeChannelSession:917).

Proposal

Promote the AEAD seam to a production aeadFactory injected by apps/server and the desktop main process. Use crypto.createCipheriv/createDecipheriv('chacha20-poly1305', key, nonce, {authTagLength:16}) with setAAD for bodies ≥ ~2 KiB and keep noble below that. Add Node KeyObject-based X25519 diffieHellman and crypto.verify for Ed25519/P-256 behind the same choke points (verifyE2eeSignature, Noise DH). Feature-detect via crypto.getCiphers() and a KAT self-test at startup, because the desktop backend may run under Electron's BoringSSL; fall back to noble. Wire format is identical; reuse the existing relay E2EE corpus/interop tests as parity gates.

Verifier (Confirmed)

suiteRecordAead uses noble chacha20poly1305 (relayE2eeSession.ts:402-411), and the aeadFactory seam is only options.testOnlyAeadFactory ?? suiteRecordAead (relayE2eeSession.ts:928). No production factory exists. node-native.txt confirms 1,859 vs 327 MiB/s at 256 KiB, a 3 MB screenshot frame at 1.74 vs 9.16 ms, and handshake primitives 19-51 µs vs 574-989 µs. On the Hub-connect path the saving is about 1 ms to seal a ~363 KiB snapshot plus 1-3 ms per handshake on the node, which is low. The bigger value is sustained screenshot/stream sealing on the node event loop. Electron/BoringSSL support for chacha20-poly1305 in createCipheriv is not verified here, so the proposed KAT and feature detection are required.

Expected gain

(a)+(b): ~60-70% less non-crypto CPU per chunk (≈270 → ≈80 µs per 256 KiB on desktop V8). (c): all decode/decrypt off the main thread, est. 15-70 ms less jank per large message on phones.

What happens today

Inbound path per chunk: ArrayBuffer slice copy (relaySocket.ts:60), hub-session payload copy (hubSessionCodec.ts:93), engine owned copy (relayEngine.ts:758), decodeRelayFrame (cborg decode, then a full canonical re-encode plus a JS byte-by-byte compare, then Effect Schema; relayCodec.ts:111-137, 218), payload copy (relayEngine.ts:1147), delivered copy (relayEngine.ts:1187), assembler copy for multi-chunk messages, then noble open and record decode. Outbound mirrors this: TextEncoder, Uint8Array.from, chunk copy (588/1111), Schema-decode + cborg encode (relayCodec.ts:237-251), hub-session frame copy (70-74), and Uint8Array.from(bytes).buffer before ws.send (relaySocket.ts:85). Each copy is followed by a zero fill. Measured per 256 KiB on desktop V8: decodeRelayFrame 189 µs, each copy 12-14 µs, noble open ~770 µs. A 3 MB screenshot frame is 12 chunks ≈ 9 ms decrypt + 2.3 ms decode + ~1 ms copies on desktop; est. 50-70 ms main-thread jank on a mid phone every ~5.8 s.

Proposal

(a) S: switch to ownership transfer. Pass event.data's ArrayBuffer view without slicing. Have decodeHubSessionFrame return a subarray, with the caller owning and zeroing the buffer. Drop the engine copies at 758/1147/1187 and at 588/1111. Send bytes directly (or bytes.buffer when byteOffset is 0) at relaySocket.ts:85. Keep zeroization by wiping the single owned buffer once at end of life. (b) S/M: add a data-frame fast path in decodeRelayFrame. Parse the fixed CBOR map header and the small keys, verify canonical length prefixes, and run the re-encode/compare only over the envelope bytes rather than the 256 KiB payload. (c) L: move HostedHubSession, HostedRelayEngine and the E2EE record layer into a dedicated Worker that posts decrypted RPC messages as transferables. Lifecycle state and decisions stay with hostedHubController on the main thread; the worker is data plane only and caches nothing.

Verifier (Confirmed)

All the copies are real: relaySocket.ts:60 (slice), 85 (Uint8Array.from(...).buffer), hubSessionCodec.ts:93 (data payload copy), relayEngine.ts:758 (owned), 1147 (payload), 1187 (delivered). decodeCanonicalValue does a full cborg decode → re-encode → JS byte compare (relayCodec.ts:111-137). codec-node.txt confirms 189 µs per 256 KiB decode and 12-14 µs per copy. Browsers copy at WebSocket.send, so dropping the facade copy keeps zeroization safe. For the connect scenario the shell snapshot is about 2 chunks, roughly 0.5 ms decode + 1.5 ms decrypt + copies, about 2 ms on desktop, which is low. The medium-impact case is sustained screenshot streaming (12 chunks per 3 MB frame), which belongs to a different scenario.

Category: CryptoRisk: mediumInvestigator confidence: mediumhub-connection:dpop-native-connect-overhead
Expected gain

Saves one native-bridge hash per Hub request and, on typical launches, one hardware signature plus 1 RTT off the native connect path (est. 50-300 ms on StrongBox devices).

What happens today

On native clients DPoP proofs are signed by the hardware key (Secure Enclave / StrongBox / TEE), not by noble, so the client does no pure-JS P-256 for DPoP. Noble P-256 appears only on the node, verifying native client certificates (covered by node-native-crypto). Each authenticated request awaits context.sha256(token) for ath, which on mobile is an expo-crypto native-bridge round trip with the same token every time (dpop.ts:125-127, dpopSigner.ts:50-56), plus one hardware ECDSA signature before fetch (api.ts:2928-2932). Hardware sign latency is an estimate: tens of ms on Secure Enclave, ~100+ ms on StrongBox. Every app launch also runs a full enrollment upsert (an extra signed request plus RTT) even when identity, prekey certificate and revision are unchanged (nativeE2eeEnrollment.ts:343-391). It runs alongside the directory, but on keystores that serialize signatures it adds to the critical path before the first ticket.

Proposal

Memoize ath per token string inside createDpopProofSigner, cleared on token change. Persist the last Hub-confirmed enrollment summary (revision, prekey certificate digest, expiry) in the existing secure enrollment store. On launch, treat it as provisionally ready when the local material is identical and the certificate is not within its renewal window, and run the upsert in the background. The Hub still validates the enrollment at ticket/grant issuance, and revocation already arrives via e2ee.enrollment-revoked.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

dpop.ts:118-131 does hash the token per proof through context.sha256 (expo-crypto digest, dpopSigner.ts:50-56), but memoizing that saves well under 1 ms per request. The per-request hardware signature is inherent to DPoP (a fresh iat/jti/htu per proof) and cannot be removed. The enrollment part is stronger than claimed: the upsert runs on every coordinator start (nativeE2eeEnrollment.ts:340-391), and issueMobileRelayAttempt refuses account-grant attempts unless the enrollment status is 'ready' (apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/accountE2eeAttempt.ts:236-239). That puts the upsert RTT plus its DPoP signature on the critical path before the first ticket for native account-grant connects. Treating a cached enrollment as provisionally ready touches revision and revocation semantics (expectedEnrollmentRevision), so it needs security review. Mobile-only.

Part of Priority 19: Connecting to a Hub

Expected gain

-1.5 s per connect/reconnect (-3 s per relay drop combined with finding #1) for un-upgraded or degraded nodes; no change for healthy E2EE nodes

What happens today

The web initiator arms advTimer = setTimeout(..., T_ADV) at channel.accept, with T_ADV = 1_500 (relayE2eeConstants.ts:251). On a channel where the node sends no capability carrier, that timer is the only path to the legacy lock (row K13, relayE2eeInitiator.ts:566-586). Until the lock, relayEngine buffers every application send and only then emits onTransportStatus('online') and flushes the subscriptions (#applyModeLock, relayEngine.ts:962-978). The node suppresses the carrier for 'statement-unavailable' or 'undersized-connection' (NodeE2eeChannelAdvertiser.ts:32, 54-60), and un-upgraded nodes never send one. Web attempts run with legacyPermitted: true (e2eeAttempt.ts:162). So against an un-upgraded node, a node whose statement build failed, or an undersized connection, every hosted connect and every reconnect adds a deterministic 1.5 s before the shell subscription is even sent. With the double establishment in finding #1, a relay drop costs 3 s of pure timer wait on such nodes. This is code-derived and was not measured on the wire.

Proposal

Make the 'no carrier' outcome explicit instead of timed, for unlatched selections only. The Hub already knows whether the node has a published and acknowledged statement (the node publishes and renews statements to the Hub, HubConnector.ts ~1147). Let the Hub add an explicit noCarrier marker to channel.accept, or the directory node capabilities. When the selection is unlatched and legacyPermitted, lock legacy immediately on that marker. This gives the Hub no new downgrade power, because withholding the carrier for T_ADV already forces the same legacy outcome for such selections. Latched or require-E2EE selections keep the timer and fail closed exactly as today. It needs a §4.4 K13 spec amendment and crypto review. Until then, surface 'node E2EE advertisement unavailable' prominently, because it now also costs 1.5 s per connect, so operators fix the underlying statement issue.

This finding was added by the adversarial verifier while checking the investigator's report. It has not been verified a second time.

Mobile cold start 18 findings · 3 high · 8 medium · 7 low

8,557 modules are evaluated before the first frame; 6,189 of them are Tabler icons for 91 icons actually used. Direct-only users wait for a Ryco Cloud probe (up to 30 s) before they see their workspace.

How it works today (investigator's summary)

How a cold start runs today (apps/mobile, Expo SDK 57, RN 0.86, Hermes V1, production iOS). Metro runs with Expo's defaults: experimentalImportSupport true, inlineRequires false, and no tree shaking (the EXPO_UNSTABLE_* flags are unset). babel's lazyImports does nothing here because Metro handles ESM itself. So every static import in the app graph is evaluated before the first frame. My static analysis follows the Metro/iOS resolution rules and folds __DEV__, NODE_ENV and Platform.OS branches. It finds 8,557 eagerly evaluated modules (24.7 MiB raw source) and only 507 behind import()/function-level requires.

  • **Tabler icons:** 6,189 of those modules are @tabler/icons-react-native, pulled in by root-barrel imports of 91 icons.
  • **Screens:** every screen is imported statically by Stack.tsx/AppAccessGate.
  • **Shiki:** the core, JS regex engine and 7 grammars (~0.8 MB of JSON.parse) are eager.
  • **Hosted/E2EE code:** noble, cborg and the relay E2EE handshake load eagerly through the client-runtime/authorization barrel. This happens even for direct-only users.

Startup sequence after JS evaluation:

1. The native splash hides as soon as one KV read (preferences) completes.

2. A JS LaunchSurface logo then shows until AppAccessGate resolves.

3. In parallel, the per-environment snapshot cache hydrates from SQLite into the threads store. That is one query per environment, run sequentially. Direct-node connection work is held behind this hydration barrier.

The gate itself is the main problem: it needs both planes to have hydrated.

  • **Hosted users:** ensureMobileHostedSession runs a serial chain: hub profile KV → keychain token → keychain trust doc → device-key/Secure Enclave key → restoreSession (DPoP-signed HTTPS, first one pays TLS) → listNodes (second DPoP-signed HTTPS). Only then does the already-cached thread list become visible. Each request has a 30 s deadline. Offline, the user gets the locked "Hub unavailable" screen, not the cache.
  • **Direct-only users:** hosted mode is configured by default (https://app.ryco.space). With no stored token, bootstrap() falls through to a network /api/auth/bootstrap-status probe (with a Secure Enclave mint proof) before the workspace can mount.

Time to a live list:

  • **Hosted:** enrollment upsert POST (every launch) ∥ directory → selection restore (waits for directory) → relay ticket ∥ keyset → WebSocket TLS + DPoP upgrade → E2EE handshake → shell snapshot. That is ≈ 11–12 RTTs on a cold network path. Every binary frame is then base64-decoded in JS (RN WebSocket) and decrypted with pure-JS noble ChaCha20-Poly1305 on Hermes.
  • **Direct:** hydration barrier → keychain → GET /api/auth/session → (rotation if due) → keychain → POST /api/auth/ws-token → WebSocket → parallel subscriptions → snapshot.

Once live, HomeScreen rebuilds both the inbox and projects models and re-renders every visible row on every store tick. It also does this on every scroll event (~30/s), because the scroll offset is reducer state and useHomeWorkspaceData returns fresh filtered arrays on every render. In addition, every projection change schedules a full-environment snapshot capture 500 ms later: JSON.stringify (≤2 MiB) + 2× UTF-8 encode + a SQLite write + an eviction scan.

Answers to the questions:

  • **Hermes:** yes, V1 (the expo-build-properties default).
  • **inlineRequires:** no.
  • **Lazy screens:** no.
  • **Splash:** it is NOT held for the network, but a second JS logo is held for the network-bound gate.
  • **Cached state:** it is hydrated before the relay connects but hidden behind the hosted revalidation, or behind the Ryco Cloud probe for direct-only users.
  • **Screen registration:** eager.

Part of Priority 20: Mobile app cold start

Expected gain

−6,094 eager modules (−71% of startup module count) and ≈−5.9 MiB raw JS removed from the bundle/bytecode. Estimated −40-150 ms of startup JS on device and −2-8 MiB retained heap (estimate based on the proxy above).

What happens today

Ten source files use import { IconX } from "@tabler/icons-react-native". AppSymbol.tsx alone imports ~70 icons, mostly as Android fallbacks: on iOS it renders SF Symbols at :194-195. The package root (dist/esm/tabler-icons-react-native.mjs) re-exports all 6,185 per-icon modules plus icons/index.mjs (436 KB) and icons-list.mjs (122 KB). Metro has no tree shaking here and inlineRequires is false, so every icon module factory is registered and executed before first render. Each one runs createReactNativeComponent: a forwardRef plus SVG node arrays. Measured: the static graph has 6,189 eager Tabler modules out of 8,557 total (72%), 6,846 KiB raw. Proxy measurement: executing the 6,184 factories takes 56-64 ms (first pass, V8 jitless, M-series) and adds 8.2 MiB of heap. Metro's per-module require overhead and Hermes interpretation are not included.

Proposal

Add apps/mobile/src/components/icons.ts with deep re-exports only, e.g. export { default as IconGitFork } from "@tabler/icons-react-native/IconGitFork";. The package exports "./*" → dist/esm/icons/*.mjs (import) and dist/cjs/icons/*.cjs (require). Point all 10 files at it. Add an oxlint no-restricted-imports rule for the bare "@tabler/icons-react-native" specifier. Add a guard test modelled on apps/web/src/perf/webBundleSplitting.test.ts that fails if apps/mobile/src imports the root.

Verifier (Confirmed)

I checked that all 10 files import from the bare "@tabler/icons-react-native". AppSymbol.tsx:1-80 imports 77 icons, and on non-Android it short-circuits to ExpoSymbolView at :193-195.

The package has no export condition for react-native. The static graph (eager-files.txt) shows Metro resolving the require condition: dist/cjs/tabler-icons-react-native.cjs (734 KB, a chain of top-level require('./icons/X.cjs')) plus dist/cjs/icons/index.cjs (693 KB), not the .mjs the evidence names. That matters for the fix:

  • Expo tree shaking (ESM-only) cannot remove a CJS barrel.
  • inlineRequires cannot remove it either.
  • Deep ./* subpath imports (both cjs and esm targets exist per icon) are the correct fix.

The graph what-if numbers check out: −6,094 modules / −5,940 KiB raw. That is raw source, so the minified/bytecode saving is smaller. The 56-64 ms proxy measurement is in tabler-eval.txt.

metro.config.js:72-75 is just withUniwindConfig and is irrelevant; the defaults come from getDefaultConfig at :6. Extra suggestion: split AppSymbol into AppSymbol.ios.tsx / AppSymbol.android.tsx so the iOS bundle never contains the 77 Android fallback icons.

Category: ReliabilityRisk: lowInvestigator confidence: highmobile-boot:direct-only-gate-waits-for-hub-probe

Part of Priority 20: Mobile app cold start

Expected gain

Direct-only users lose 1 TLS handshake + 1 HTTPS RTT to app.ryco.space + Secure Enclave proof/key generation + 2-3 keychain operations from the time to thread list (≈100-600 ms on cellular, estimate). Removes a worst case of 30 s on stalled or captive networks. Also stops contacting the Hub on every launch for users who never use it.

What happens today

Hosted mode is configured by default: the build config falls back to DEFAULT_HOSTED_APP_ORIGIN https://app.ryco.space. deriveAppAccess returns hydrating until BOTH hostedHydrated and directHydrated are true, even when a direct credential is already readable. For a user who never signed into a Hub, ensureMobileHostedSession still does the following:

1. Reads the hub profile from KV, the hosted token from the keychain, and the E2EE trust document from the keychain.

2. Creates or loads a Secure Enclave key (createMobileDpopSigner → ensureKey).

3. Calls bootstrap(): restoreSession throws missing-token locally, which isSessionFailure treats as a session failure. clearSessionMaterial() then issues a SecureStore delete on every launch, and the code awaits getBootstrapAvailability() — a DPoP-minted GET to app.ryco.space with a 30 s deadline.

Only then does .finally(setHostedHydrated) run. The only consumer of bootstrapAvailable is the sign-in sheet copy (first-run vs signed-out).

Proposal

1) Change deriveAppAccess to unlock as soon as either plane affirmatively grants access: directHydrated && directCredentialReadable → unlocked (via direct-node), later upgraded to both. Keep hydrating only while no plane has decided. Update appAccessModel.test.ts "stays hydrating until both". 2) In ensureMobileHostedSession, when hydration finds no stored hosted token, do not call bootstrap() at launch. Publish signed-out locally and fetch bootstrap availability lazily when the identity/sign-in surface mounts. 3) Defer createMobileDpopSigner/ensureKey until a hosted ceremony or stored session needs it. 4) Skip clearSessionMaterial's SecureStore delete when no token was ever hydrated.

Verifier (Confirmed)

What I verified:

  • app.config.ts:118 defaults hubBaseUrl to DEFAULT_HOSTED_APP_ORIGIN (packages/shared/src/hostedApp.ts:2).
  • deriveAppAccess returns hydrating until both planes are true (appAccessModel.ts:22). The test at appAccessModel.test.ts:13 pins this.
  • AppAccessGate.tsx:64-72 sets hostedHydrated only when ensureMobileHostedSession settles.
  • runtime.ts:321-349 runs this chain serially: profile KV → token keychain → trust keychain → configureMobileHostedRuntime (createMobileDpopSigner → deviceKey.ts:82-86 ensureKey at runtime.ts:123-131) → bootstrap().
  • With no token, api.ts:2912-2926 throws session_invalid/missing-token before any signing. state.ts:638-647 treats that as a session failure, calls clearSessionMaterial, and awaits getBootstrapAvailability (api.ts:866-875, dpop:"mint", so it does a Secure Enclave sign plus a network request). REQUEST_DEADLINE_MS is 30_000 (api.ts:160).
  • bootstrapAvailable's only mobile consumer is hostedAuthModel.ts:432.

Caveats:

  • The SecureStore delete is fire-and-forget (sessionCredentials.ts:70-81, 43-58). It wastes a keychain op but adds no latency.
  • The gate blocks UI only. driver.start() is not behind it, so the gain is time-to-visible-workspace, not the connection itself.

The 30 s stalled or captive-network worst case is real.

Part of Priority 20: Mobile app cold start

Expected gain

Removes ~30 full model rebuilds/s during scroll and one per live store event. At 400+ threads each rebuild is estimated at several ms of Hermes time, so expect visibly smoother scrolling and lower CPU while agents stream.

What happens today

Three things combine:

  • useHomeWorkspaceData(eligibleEnvironmentIds) returns three freshly .filter()ed arrays on every call. The useMemo deps of both inboxSections (buildInboxSections → buildThreadInbox: maps, per-thread settlement classification, 3 toSorted) and projectRows (buildProjectRows) therefore change on every HomeScreen render. projectRows is computed even in inbox mode.
  • InboxScreen's onScroll (scrollEventThrottle 32 → ~30/s) dispatches set-scroll-offset, which creates a new reducer state each time. HomeScreen re-renders ~30×/s while scrolling, and each render also runs the filters, excludeChatProjects, threads.filter, flattenInboxSections and a LegendList render with a new renderItem/data array. Each row also gets a fresh MenuView actions array and resolveSnoozePresets(new Date()).
  • useHomeEnvironments subscribes to the whole environmentStateById, which changes on every shell/orchestration event, so the same rebuild happens on every live event.

Also: rows and InboxThreadRow are not memoized (memo( appears once in apps/mobile/src), and buildThreadInbox builds worktreesByProjectKey with an O(W²) array spread.

Proposal

1) Memoize useHomeWorkspaceData's filtered arrays with useMemo keyed on (projects, worktrees, threads, eligibleEnvironmentIds). Better, derive eligibility inside a selector so references stay stable. 2) Compute projectRows only when mode === "projects", and inboxSections only for inbox. 3) Keep scroll offsets in a useRef map (or dispatch only on onScrollEndDrag/onMomentumScrollEnd); never use per-frame React state. 4) Wrap InboxScreen and InboxThreadRow in memo, use a useCallback renderItem, compute snooze presets once per render/minute, and reuse row objects whose underlying summary is unchanged (keyed cache in buildInboxSections). 5) In useHomeEnvironments, select only a bootstrapComplete per-environment map with useShallow instead of environmentStateById. 6) In threadInbox.ts, push into the worktree arrays instead of spreading.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Verified:

  • homeData.ts:23-28 returns three new .filter() arrays on every call. HomeScreen always passes a Set (:36-40), so the useMemo deps at :62-109 change on every render. Both buildInboxSections and buildProjectRows run regardless of mode.
  • The reducer (homeMode.ts:58-65) returns a new state for each offset. InboxScreen.tsx:209-210 dispatches on every onScroll with scrollEventThrottle=32. The offset is only consumed as initialScrollOffset (:208), so a ref suffices.
  • renderItem is recreated per render; for each row it calls resolveSnoozePresets(new Date()) (:118) and builds a fresh actions array.
  • flattenInboxSections runs per render (:63-68).
  • useHomeEnvironments.ts:32 subscribes to the whole environmentStateById, and its final useMemo depends on it (:64+).
  • threadInbox.ts:406-413 spreads arrays (quadratic per project).
  • The only memo( in apps/mobile/src is CopyTextButton.tsx:9.

This is not covered by the Aug "no longer rebuilds every second" item (2026-08-12 doc:70).

Medium impactEffort S◐ Partially confirmedHosted users see a logo until restoreSession AND listNodes finish; offline launches show sign-in instead of the cached workspace−1 RTT + 1 DPoP proof on every hosted cold start (≈80-400 ms on cellular, estimate). Worst case on stalled networks drops from up to 60 s (two 30 s deadlines) to the chosen launch deadline. With (c), offline launches show content instead of a sign-in wall.
Category: WaterfallRisk: mediumInvestigator confidence: highRating changed by verifier: impact high → medium, effort M → Smobile-boot:hosted-gate-waits-for-directory-and-locks-offline

Part of Priority 20: Mobile app cold start

Expected gain

−1 RTT + 1 DPoP proof on every hosted cold start (≈80-400 ms on cellular, estimate). Worst case on stalled networks drops from up to 60 s (two 30 s deadlines) to the chosen launch deadline. With (c), offline launches show content instead of a sign-in wall.

What happens today

The snapshot cache is hydrated into the threads store at startup, so the last-known thread list exists in memory early. But AppAccessGate only flips hostedHydrated when the whole ensureMobileHostedSession promise settles. That promise awaits #restoreAccess, which publishes authenticated at state.ts:629 and then runs await this.refreshDirectory() (listNodes) at :635. So the cached list stays hidden behind two sequential DPoP-signed HTTPS requests, and each needs a Secure Enclave signature. Each request may take up to REQUEST_DEADLINE_MS = 30 s. If restoreSession fails transiently (offline, timeout, 5xx), accountStatus becomes unavailable. With no direct credential the gate is then locked and shows the "Hub unavailable" identity surface, even though cache policy deliberately keeps content across session expiry for offline use. The native splash hides as soon as preferences hydrate, so the user sees native splash → a different JS logo (128 px tinted SVG) → workspace.

Proposal

(a) Unlock the hosted plane when accountStatus === "authenticated" is published, not when bootstrap() finishes. For example, have AppAccessGate observe a hostedAccessDecided signal resolved inside #restoreAccess before refreshDirectory. The directory keeps loading in the background; mutation authority is unchanged because it already requires a ready directory and a fresh shell snapshot. (b) Use a shorter launch-time access deadline (e.g. 8-10 s); the access-retry backoff already re-checks. (c) Product/security decision: allow a read-only cached access state when a stored hosted token exists and the failure is transient. Render the cached workspace with a "Reconnecting to Hub" banner while recovery runs. This contradicts the current documented rule ("workspace navigator mounts only after a revalidated native Hub session") and needs explicit sign-off. (d) Keep the native splash until the gate leaves hydrating (cap ≈800 ms, then show LaunchSurface) to avoid the double launch visual.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

Confirmed:

  • #restoreAccess (state.ts:621-650) patches authenticated at :630, then awaits refreshDirectory at :635, which reaches listNodes at :2022. bootstrap() (:535-543) only resolves after that, so hostedHydrated waits for both requests.
  • Home renders from the persisted roster plus cache-provenance ids (useHomeEnvironments.ts:27-31), so unlocking early would show cached content.
  • The splash hides on preference hydration (App.tsx:46-54), and LaunchSurface is a second 128 px logo (AppAccessGate.tsx:38-51).

Corrections:

  • (a) is simpler than proposed and is S effort. The gate already subscribes to hostedAuthenticated (AppAccessGate.tsx:58), so it can treat hostedHydrated || hostedAuthenticated as decided.
  • (c) is not a bug. The offline lock is the documented policy (docs/mobile-native-status.md:21-24, "mounts only after a revalidated native Hub session"), so it needs sign-off as the investigator says.
  • "Up to 60 s" needs restoreSession to nearly time out and then succeed before listNodes stalls. The realistic worst case is about 30 s.

The solid gain is about 1 RTT plus 1 DPoP proof on every hosted cold start.

Medium impactEffort S✓ ConfirmedEvery projection change triggers a full-environment JSON.stringify + double UTF-8 encode + SQLite write 500 ms laterAvoids up to ~2 MiB stringify + ~4 MiB of UTF-8 encode work and allocation per capture (estimated tens of ms of JS-thread time per capture for large environments). Category: CPURisk: lowInvestigator confidence: highmobile-boot:snapshot-capture-full-reserialize

Part of Priority 20: Mobile app cold start

Expected gain

Avoids up to ~2 MiB stringify + ~4 MiB of UTF-8 encode work and allocation per capture (estimated tens of ms of JS-thread time per capture for large environments). Most captures during streaming become no-ops, with fewer SQLite writes and eviction scans.

What happens today

applyShellEvent, applyOrchestrationEvents and syncServerShellSnapshot all call markEnvironmentSnapshotDirty, a 500 ms trailing debounce. captureNow then:

  • rebuilds the record over all threads and serializes it (≤400 threads, ≤2 MiB);
  • in boundStoredEnvironmentSnapshot, encodes the whole payload with new TextEncoder().encode(payload) just to read byteLength (repeated per trim round);
  • in saveEnvironmentSnapshot, encodes the full payload again via payloadByteLength;
  • writes to SQLite, then runs listEnvironmentSnapshotStats plus eviction.

This happens after the first live snapshot and after every quiet gap during agent activity, even when only message-detail events arrived and the persisted slices (projects/worktrees/shells/summaries) are unchanged. If Hermes lacks TextEncoder, the pure-JS Utf8TextEncoder polyfill in polyfills.ts does this byte by byte.

Proposal

1) Record the identities of the persisted slices at the last capture (projectIds, projectById, worktreeIds, worktreeById, threadIds, threadShellById, sidebarThreadSummaryById). With immutable zustand updates, skip capture in O(1) when all are unchanged. 2) Compute the UTF-8 length once, without allocation (charCode loop, or the fast path payload.length*3 <= cap → no encode needed), and pass it into saveEnvironmentSnapshot instead of re-encoding. 3) Use a longer debounce with a max-wait, and flush on AppState background. 4) Longer term: store per-thread rows so a capture writes only changed threads.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Verified:

  • environmentStateSink.ts:66-110 calls projectionChanged after applyShellEvent, applyOrchestrationEvents and syncServerShellSnapshot.
  • markDirty is a pure trailing debounce with no max-wait (environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts:151-162, 500 ms at :39).
  • captureNow (:125-146) rebuilds the record, then calls boundStoredEnvironmentSnapshot. That function stringifies and runs new TextEncoder().encode on every loop check, including the first (codec.ts:123-133).
  • saveEnvironmentSnapshot encodes again via payloadByteLength (snapshotDb.ts:68-70, :131).
  • Each capture then runs evictToCapacity, which does another listEnvironmentSnapshotStats query (:97-111).

The evidence is stronger than "if Hermes lacks TextEncoder": the repo's own comment (polyfills.ts:76-78) states Hermes ships no TextEncoder. The active encoder is therefore the pure-JS Utf8TextEncoder (polyfills.ts:210-231), which makes two full JS passes per encode.

Expected gain

−420 eager modules / −3.0 MiB raw source evaluated before first frame (measured on the static graph). Estimated −30-100 ms startup JS; each first visit to a screen pays only that screen's own cost.

What happens today

Stack.tsx statically imports every route screen: Thread, ThreadFile (shiki, @pierre/diffs), Review, NewTask, the Settings screens including Statistics, E2EE verification, HostedAccount, SourceControl, and more. AppAccessGate statically imports NativeIdentityScreen (react-native-webview Turnstile) and ConnectionsNewRouteScreen (expo-camera) for the locked stack, even for unlocked users. Static-graph attribution: cutting these edges removes 420 modules / 3,078 KiB raw from the eager graph. Examples: Statistics 130 KiB/20 files, HostedAccount 127 KiB/9, NewTask 79 KiB/13. React Navigation's static config does not accept per-screen getComponent (it is omitted from static screen props), so laziness has to come from the component itself.

Proposal

Add a lazyScreen(load) helper that returns a stable component which calls require() on first render and caches the result. This is the same function-scoped require pattern index.ts:18-22 already uses. Use it as screen: lazyScreen(() => require("./features/threads/ThreadRouteScreen").ThreadRouteScreen) for every route except Home, and for the LockedStack screens. After Home's first frame, prewarm the Thread route via InteractionManager.runAfterInteractions / requestIdleCallback so the first thread open is not slower. Optionally extend a mobile bundle guard test to assert these modules are not reachable eagerly from index.ts.

Part of Priority 20: Mobile app cold start

Expected gain

−1 HTTP RTT and one JSON decode per direct cold connect and per foreground reconnect (LAN ≈2-10 ms; tailnet/DERP 50-300 ms, estimate); −1-2 keychain reads.

What happens today

connectSavedEnvironment does the following in sequence:

1. catalog.readBearerToken (keychain).

2. checkSavedEnvironmentSession (HTTP GET /api/auth/session).

3. savedSessionRenewal.renew, which adds POST rotate + keychain write/read + GET session when the session is >1 day old.

4. Builds the WsTransport, whose URL resolver reads the bearer from the keychain again and POSTs /api/auth/ws-token.

5. Opens the socket.

The ws-token endpoint already answers expired/revoked bearers with 401, which is wired as a terminal credential rejection (isSavedEnvironmentCredentialRejection → onCredentialRejected). The pre-check is only needed to decide renewal and to refresh role. AppAccessGate also reads the same bearer from the keychain at launch.

Proposal

Persist the last AuthSessionState.expiresAt and role per saved environment (non-secret, in the runtime/registry store). On cold connect, when !shouldRenewSavedSession(cached, now), skip the pre-socket session GET and go straight to ws-token + socket. Refresh session/role in the background once connected. Keep today's sequential path whenever renewal is due, because a superseded bearer must never be presented. Read the bearer once per attempt and hand it to the first URL resolution.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Verified the sequence in environmentDriver.ts:

1. Keychain readBearerToken (:356).

2. checkSavedEnvironmentSession → GET /api/auth/session (:374-380; remoteApi.ts:100-108).

3. renew (:394-399), which rotates only when shouldRenewSavedSession is true (savedSessionRenewal.ts:43-46, 194-197).

4. The WsTransport URL resolver re-reads the bearer via savedSessionRenewal.readBearerToken (:306-313).

5. POST ws-token (remoteApi.ts:138-152).

The ws-token 401 is already terminal: isSavedEnvironmentCredentialRejection (savedEnvironmentSession.ts:52-54) is wired to isTerminalUrlError/onCredentialRejected at environmentDriver.ts:320-321. The in-code rationale at :371-373 ("would retry its ws-token request forever") therefore looks stale, but confirm the server's ws-token 401 behaviour before relying on it.

AppAccessGate.tsx:81-91 reads the bearer from the keychain again at launch. Persisting expiresAt and role is a sound way to skip the pre-check when renewal is not due.

Category: RenderingRisk: mediumInvestigator confidence: mediummobile-boot:no-react-compiler-on-mobile

Part of Priority 20: Mobile app cold start

Expected gain

Fewer re-renders and derived-data rebuilds across all screens during live streaming and scrolling. The size of the win needs profiling (estimate: largest on Home/Inbox and thread detail).

What happens today

apps/web compiles with reactCompilerPreset, and babel-plugin-react-compiler@1.0.0 is already in the repo. The mobile babel config is only babel-preset-expo, and app.config.ts sets no experiments.reactCompiler, so babel-preset-expo's compiler path stays off. Mobile has a single memo( across 353 source files. Many screens subscribe to zustand/atom stores whose ticks re-run expensive derivations (see the Home finding) and re-render whole subtrees.

Proposal

Add babel-plugin-react-compiler to apps/mobile devDependencies and set experiments: { reactCompiler: true } in app.config.ts; babel-preset-expo wires it. Start with a sources filter for features/home, features/inbox, features/threads and components. Verify with the React DevTools profiler and existing tests, then widen. This complements, and does not replace, the explicit HomeScreen fixes.

  • The web uses reactCompilerPreset (vite.config.ts:2,108), and babel-plugin-react-compiler@1.0.0 is installed (apps/web/package.json:70).
  • The only mobile memo is CopyTextButton.tsx:9.

The proposal is valid. The gain is unmeasured.

Medium impactEffort L◐ Partially confirmedHosted live list waits for a per-launch enrollment upsert and a directory-gated selection restore before the relay ticket−1 to 2 sequential RTTs (+1 Secure Enclave proof) on time-to-live for hosted users (≈100-400 ms on cellular, estimate).
Category: WaterfallRisk: highInvestigator confidence: mediumRating changed by verifier: impact medium → medium, effort M → Lmobile-boot:hosted-relay-turnup-waterfall
Expected gain

−1 to 2 sequential RTTs (+1 Secure Enclave proof) on time-to-live for hosted users (≈100-400 ms on cellular, estimate).

What happens today

At process start the enrollment coordinator is idle. So when accountStatus becomes authenticated, watchSelectionForE2ee calls ensure(), which does ensureIdentity → prekey/enrollmentId → POST upsertE2eeDeviceEnrollment (DPoP-signed) on every launch. prepareMobileRelaySocketContext refuses until enrollment is ready. The persisted node selection is restored only once directoryStatus is ready (after listNodes), and the selection persistence is installed only after the SQLite cache hydration finishes. Only then does the relay attempt run: ticket ∥ keyset (already parallel), WebSocket TLS + DPoP upgrade, E2EE handshake, shell snapshot. Approximate count from launch: TLS(2) + session(1) + directory/upsert(1) + ticket(1) + WebSocket TLS/upgrade(2-3) + E2EE(1-2) + snapshot(1) ≈ 9-11 RTTs plus Secure Enclave signs.

Proposal

(a) Persist the last ready enrollment summary (namespace, enrollmentId, revision, certificate digest/expiry — public data) and treat it as ready at launch when the certificate is not near expiry. Revalidate with the upsert in the background after the relay is up. Ticket issuance already fails closed with enrollment-revoked and triggers invalidate. (b) Once accountStatus is authenticated, start the relay ticket for the persisted selection immediately (the Hub authorizes tickets), in parallel with listNodes. Drop or deselect if the directory later disagrees. Mutation authority keeps requiring a revalidated directory + fresh snapshot, per AGENTS.md hosted lifecycle rules. (c) Install selection persistence before snapshot hydration completes (it only needs a KV read).

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

Confirmed:

  • The enrollment coordinator starts idle, so watchSelectionForE2ee calls ensure() on every authenticated launch (runtime.ts:262-271). That runs ensureIdentity → prekey/enrollmentId → upsertE2eeDeviceEnrollment (nativeE2eeEnrollment.ts:341-391).
  • prepareMobileRelaySocketContext refuses until enrollment is ready (accountE2eeAttempt.ts:109-121).
  • Selection restore waits for an authenticated account, directoryStatus ready AND browserStatus current (selectionPersistence.ts:63-81).
  • Selection persistence is installed only after cache hydration (environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts:366-371).

Correction: ensure() starts as soon as accountStatus flips to authenticated, and it calls refreshDirectory itself (:345), which joins the in-flight listNodes. The upsert therefore already runs in parallel with the directory read. Proposal (a) only saves max(0, identity+prekey+upsert − listNodes); the real saving is (b), about 1 RTT.

(b) changes the single hosted lifecycle owner's ordering (AGENTS.md hosted boundaries), so it needs a security/lifecycle review. The effort is larger than M.

Medium impactEffort L◐ Partially confirmedEvery hosted relay frame is base64-decoded in JS (RN WebSocket) and decrypted with pure-JS noble on HermesUnknown. Estimated tens to hundreds of ms of JS-thread time for MB-sized snapshots on Hermes; the measurement decides whether L-effort work is justified.
Category: CPURisk: mediumInvestigator confidence: lowmobile-boot:relay-frames-base64-and-js-crypto
Expected gain

Unknown. Estimated tens to hundreds of ms of JS-thread time for MB-sized snapshots on Hermes; the measurement decides whether L-effort work is justified.

What happens today

RN's WebSocket delivers binary messages across the bridge as base64 strings and decodes them with base64-js (base64.toByteArray(ev.data)); sends go through binaryToBase64. The relay socket uses binaryType arraybuffer for CBOR frames. The E2EE channel (X25519, ChaCha20-Poly1305, HKDF/SHA-256, Ed25519/P-256 verification) is @noble pure JS. Hermes has no JIT, so per-byte work runs in the interpreter: base64 decode → ChaCha20-Poly1305 open → CBOR decode → JSON/Schema decode. This all happens on the JS thread for the first shell snapshot and every subsequent frame. No throughput number exists for this path on a device.

Proposal

First measure: extend the existing dev-only e2eeVectorRunner with throughput benchmarks (ChaCha20-Poly1305 open MB/s, base64 decode MB/s, handshake ms) on a physical iPhone. Also add performance marks around first-snapshot receive → decrypt → applied. If significant, either (a) back the noble primitives with a small native module (iOS CryptoKit provides Curve25519.KeyAgreement, ChaChaPoly and Curve25519.Signing) exposed via JSI/Nitro with ArrayBuffer zero-copy, keeping the same wire format; or (b) adopt a JSI WebSocket that hands ArrayBuffers to JS without base64. Have the node keep shell snapshots minimal and compressed.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

The code path is confirmed:

  • RN WebSocket.js:200-201 sends via sendBinary(binaryToBase64(data)).
  • :241-242 receives via base64.toByteArray(ev.data).buffer.
  • relaySocket.ts:306 sets binaryType arraybuffer.
  • relayE2eeNoise.ts:1-5 uses @noble/ciphers chacha20poly1305, x25519, and noble HKDF/SHA-256.

The impact is entirely unmeasured; there are no device numbers. Measure first, as proposed. Shell snapshots are bounded (≤2 MiB per environment), which caps the per-snapshot cost.

What happens today

After hydrating the hub profile (needed first), the function awaits these one after another: hydrateMobileHostedSessionToken (keychain get) → mobileE2eeTrustStore.hydrate (install-marker KV read + keychain get + parse) → configureMobileHostedRuntime → createMobileDpopSigner (expo-crypto + device-key module, then the native Secure Enclave ensureKey). None depends on another's result. The documented constraints only require that the token and trust store are loaded before configureHostedRuntime/bootstrap.

Proposal

After hydrateMobileHubProfile and the config re-resolve, run Promise.allSettled([hydrateMobileHostedSessionToken(), mobileE2eeTrustStore.hydrate(), createMobileDpopSigner()]). Keep the existing failure mapping (credential-storage / device-security), then configure and bootstrap. This preserves both ordering guarantees.

The documented ordering constraints (runtime.ts:296-317) only need the token before bootstrap and the trust store before configureHostedRuntime. Signer creation is independent and can overlap with the two keychain reads. The gain is small.

Low impactEffort S✓ ConfirmedOpening a thread on another hosted node always waits a fixed 250 ms trailing debounce before retargeting−250 ms on every cross-node thread open in hosted mode (deterministic).
Category: WaterfallRisk: lowInvestigator confidence: highmobile-boot:retarget-trailing-debounce
Expected gain

−250 ms on every cross-node thread open in hosted mode (deterministic).

What happens today

THREAD_CONNECTION_RETARGET_DEBOUNCE_MS = 250 is a trailing debounce, chosen so an A→B tap-through costs one relay ticket. Every thread open whose node differs from the current selection therefore waits 250 ms before the selectNode/relay turn-up even starts, including the common single-open case.

Proposal

Dispatch on the leading edge when the engine is idle (no pending intent and nothing in flight). Apply the trailing debounce only to opens that arrive while an intent is pending or in flight, which keeps the one-ticket guarantee for rapid A→B. Alternatively shrink the window to ~80-100 ms.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Verified:

  • THREAD_CONNECTION_RETARGET_DEBOUNCE_MS = 250 (threadConnectionRetarget.ts:237).
  • open() always calls armDebounce (:415-425).
  • evaluate() bails while the timer is pending (:357-358).
  • The engine is driven by ThreadDetailScreen.tsx:383 through useThreadConnectionRetarget.

The delay is only user-visible when the decision is retarget, i.e. the thread's node is not already the healthy selection with a hosted connection (:101-107). Otherwise the deferred evaluation resolves to none harmlessly. A leading-edge dispatch when idle keeps the one-ticket guarantee for rapid A→B taps.

Low impactEffort S◐ Partially confirmedProject icons are re-fetched over RPC after every (re)connect because the cache generation is keyed on connectedAt−N RPCs per reconnect (N = distinct visible projects) and less decode/remount churn when the app returns to the foreground.

Expected gain

−N RPCs per reconnect (N = distinct visible projects) and less decode/remount churn when the app returns to the foreground.

What happens today

Each InboxThreadRow renders ProjectFavicon. It passes the WebSocket connection status (including connectedAt) as the cache generation to readProjectIconSource, which drops the whole per-API LRU whenever the generation changes. Every cold connect and every foreground reconnect therefore re-issues one projects.readIcon RPC per visible project (over E2EE relay in hosted mode). Each result is a base64 data URI decoded again by expo-image. Rows also build a JSON.stringify request key per render.

Proposal

Key the icon cache by environment and server instance, not by connectedAt. Rely on customAvatarContentHash plus the existing 5-minute TTL for invalidation. The policy stays memory-only, matching the 'node artwork never enters persistence' rule. Drop the per-render JSON.stringify by memoizing the request key.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

ProjectFavicon.tsx:23-57 passes the whole WsConnectionStatus object (connection) as the generation, not just connectedAt. projectIconSource.ts:20-24 drops the per-API LRU whenever the generation changes identity.

The status object (wsConnectionState.ts:18-35) changes on any field write, including online flips that are written to every keyed slot. The cache is therefore dropped even more often than the investigator claims. InboxThreadRow.tsx:106 renders it per row.

However, connection-scoped, memory-only caching is an explicit design decision (projectIconSource.ts:4). The identical pattern is in apps/web/src/components/ProjectFavicon.tsx:56, so the fix should be made in the shared helper or for both callers. Keying on connectedAt only (or on environment plus server instance) would keep the design intent.

Expected gain

Removes 3 + (1+N) sequential native SQLite round trips and full cache decoding from the direct connect path. Estimated 20-100 ms typically and several hundred ms with large caches; also shortens JS-thread blocking during launch.

What happens today

driver.start() runs only after mobileRuntimeStartupBarrier hydration completes. That hydration covers:

  • the catalog KV read;
  • opening ryco-client-cache.db (openDatabaseAsync + PRAGMA WAL + DDL = 3 native round trips);
  • loadHubNodeRoster, then listEnvironmentSnapshotStats;
  • for each environment, sequentially: loadEnvironmentSnapshot (one SELECT each), JSON.parse + validation, and a separate zustand set.

Caps allow up to 32 environments / 16 MiB, so worst case all of that JSON is parsed on the JS thread before the first direct network request. The store already guarantees "Live data always wins the connection-startup race": hydrateEnvironmentStateFromCache is a no-op when state already exists.

Proposal

1) Load all rows with one query (SELECT environment_id, schema_version, payload FROM environment_snapshots ORDER BY updated_at DESC). Decode the most recent environment(s) first, yielding a macrotask between environments, and apply small ones in one batched store update. 2) Let the direct supervisor's network pre-flight (keychain read, session check, ws-token, socket open) start right after catalog hydration. Gate only the application of the first shell snapshot on the barrier, or rely on the live-wins guard after confirming that connection registration does not create empty environment state that would block cache hydration.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

The code is as described:

  • driver.start() is behind runAfterHydration (bootstrap.ts:167-174), and hydration runs at :105-119.
  • The DB open does openDatabaseAsync, then WAL, then DDL (snapshotDb.ts:94-105).
  • Hydration loads the roster, then the stats, then runs one SELECT and one store set per environment, sequentially (environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts:246-302).
  • The caps are 32 environments / 16 MiB (metadataSnapshot.ts:13-14).
  • hydrateEnvironmentStateFromCache is a no-op when state exists (store.ts:3404-3418).

Why the impact is lower than claimed:

  • For typical users (1-3 environments) this is a few async SQLite round trips (single-digit ms each) plus JSON decode of at most about 2 MiB per environment.
  • For direct-only users it is not on today's visible critical path: the UI gate waits much longer on the Hub probe (see direct-only-gate-waits-for-hub-probe). It becomes relevant once that is fixed.
  • Proposal (1) is cheap. Proposal (2) is risky, because catalog.runtimeStore.ensure and connection registration may create environment state before the cache lands, which would make cached content disappear. The investigator flagged this.

Expected gain

Unknown until measured. Typically defers a large share of module initialization off the first-frame path (RN's own template enables it); on top of the targeted fixes, the remaining ~2,000 eager modules would mostly become use-time evaluation.

What happens today

Expo's default getTransformOptions returns {experimentalImportSupport: true, inlineRequires: false}, and apps/mobile/metro.config.js does not override it. Because supportsStaticESM is true, babel-preset-expo disables its CJS transform, so its lazyImports option has no effect either. Result: any module reachable by a static import executes during startup, whether or not the first screen uses it (8,557 eager modules vs 507 lazy). The repo already relies on manual laziness in a few places (index.ts:18-22, bootstrap.ts:107-109, hostedHub/state.ts:41-43). It also has import-time registrations that would need care: setHostedRuntimeConfigurator, configureAuthoritativeNodeTrustSource, setThreadsRuntimeConfigurator, and the polyfills side-effect import.

Proposal

Run a measured experiment: set config.transformer.getTransformOptions = async () => ({ transform: { experimentalImportSupport: true, inlineRequires: true } }) in metro.config.js. Add the explicit side-effect modules and polyfills to nonInlinedRequires, or convert their registrations to explicit init calls from App. Compare startup with performance marks (bundle start → first Home frame) on a release build. Treat this as complementary to the targeted fixes (Tabler, lazy screens, shiki), which are deterministic.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

The config is as stated:

  • ExpoMetroConfig.js:343-348 sets experimentalImportSupport:true, inlineRequires:false.
  • apps/mobile/metro.config.js does not override getTransformOptions.
  • uniwind's withUniwindConfig does not touch it (grep found no getTransformOptions in dist/metro).
  • babel-transformer.js:81 sets supportsStaticESM, so babel-preset-expo skips its CJS/lazy transform (module-transforms.js:24-33).

The payoff is overstated. Re-exports (export * from in client-runtime/authorization/index.ts and contracts/src/index.ts, effect's index, and the tabler CJS barrel) assign into exports and cannot be inlined, so barrels stay eager. The proven big wins are the targeted fixes. Run this as a measured experiment only after those land.

App.tsx eagerly imports useHostedAppLifecycle.ts:1 and hostedHub/state.ts:1-12, which import @ryco/client-runtime/authorization. That barrel does export * of api.ts (index.ts:2) and nativeE2eeEnrollment.ts (index.ts:9). Two edges then drag in the E2EE stack:

  • api.ts:57 imports assertE2eeAccountId from relayE2eeTranscripts. That function (relayE2eeTranscripts.ts:374-379) is only a UTF-8 length check, but the module imports @noble/hashes sha256, cborg and effect at top level (:6-8).
  • nativeE2eeEnrollment.ts:7-10 imports relayE2eeKeys, relayE2eeHandshake (→ relayE2eeNoise → @noble/ciphers chacha, @noble/curves x25519) and relayE2eeTranscripts.

Measured on the static graph, these are eager before the first frame:

  • @noble/curves 351 KiB / 13 files
  • @noble/ciphers 79 KiB
  • @noble/hashes 66 KiB
  • cborg 97 KiB / 18 files
  • relayE2eeHandshake 115 KiB, Transcripts 76 KiB, Close 64 KiB, Session 61 KiB

That is about 0.9 MiB raw / about 40 modules. It is evaluated for every user, including direct-only users who never open a relay channel. Hosted runtime wiring itself is already deferred (hostedHub/state.ts:41-43 dynamic import), so the barrel is what defeats that laziness. The web boot graph in EVIDENCE.md has the same problem.

Proposal

1) Move assertE2eeAccountId and any other pure input validators api.ts needs into a dependency-free shared module (e.g. packages/shared/src/relayE2eeIds.ts with E2EE_ACCOUNT_ID_MAX_BYTES). relayE2eeTranscripts re-exports it, and api.ts imports the light module.

2) Stop re-exporting nativeE2eeEnrollment.ts (and the trust resolver / handshake consumers) from the root @ryco/client-runtime/authorization barrel. Expose them via a subpath such as @ryco/client-runtime/authorization/e2ee, imported only by apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/runtime.ts, which is already loaded through await import("./runtime"). Alternatively, have nativeE2eeEnrollment await import("@ryco/shared/relayE2eeHandshake") inside its certificate validation.

3) Add a boot-graph guard test (for mobile, plus the existing web webBundleSplitting.test.ts) asserting that @noble/* and cborg are not reachable from index.ts / main through static edges.

This finding was added by the adversarial verifier while checking the investigator's report. It has not been verified a second time.

Prior work

EVIDENCE.md notes the web counterpart (hosted/relay/E2EE/noble in every standard-build boot graph). The mobile investigator mentioned it in the scenario summary without a finding. No fix exists yet.

E. Background I/O

Logs and traces 13 findings · 1 high · 4 medium · 8 low

Provider event logs are always on: 4.1 GB on disk, ~486 MB written per day, with the canonical stream duplicating native payloads. Nothing in the app reads them, and Diagnostics tails two files that are never written.

How it works today (investigator's summary)

Every provider event is written twice, and both logs are always on. When the Claude, Codex, ACP or OpenCode adapter receives an SDK or app-server message, it writes a "native" log line (ClaudeAdapter.ts:2104-2140 and CodexAdapter.ts:2748-2753). The Claude adapter first deep-clones the message through redactAgentControlSecrets. The adapter then maps the message to one or more ProviderRuntimeEvents. Each of those events is deep-cloned again (ClaudeAdapter.ts:1986), carries the full native message in raw.payload, and is written a second time as a "canonical" line from ProviderService.publishRuntimeEvent (ProviderService.ts:611-636). That write happens before the event reaches the PubSub. Both writes go through EventNdjsonLogger: Effect.fn spans and a SynchronizedRef lock per write, JSON.stringify, a template line, and a 200 ms batch. AsyncRotatingFileSink then does one fs.promises.appendFile (open, write, close) per record into per-thread files, 10 MiB x 3 files per stream. Nothing turns this off. There is no total-size budget. Nothing in the app reads these files: Diagnostics looks for provider/events.log, which is never created. The shared loggers are also never closed.

On the user's real install (read-only analysis) the provider log directory holds 4,185 MiB in 689 files across 209 threads. Zero files are older than 30 days, so the boot-time sweep reclaims nothing. In the last 24 h, 486 MiB is still on disk, and more than that was written, because rotation discards the oldest files. While three Claude workflow-coordinator threads were running, the canonical stream wrote 11x more than native for the same window (111.9 vs 10.1 KiB/s on the busiest thread). 87-95% of canonical bytes are the duplicated raw.payload. Each native task_progress message fans out into 2.4-2.6 canonical lines on average and up to 16, and each copy carries a growing workflow_progress array of up to 78 KB. The result is 40 MiB of canonical log per 5 minutes on one thread, so the 3-file rotation keeps only about 5 minutes of history. SQLite persisted 3.7 MB of activity payload for that same window. Codex threads log 1.5 MB attachment items four times, about 3 MB per canonical line. Native delta lines are 709 B each but carry about 9 B of real delta (1.2%).

CPU cost is real but modest: about 2 ms of main thread per second per busy workflow thread. A single large workflow tick can cost an estimated 10-17 ms. The bigger costs are disk volume and SSD wear, rotation that makes the logs useless for debugging, memory held by deep clones and a queue bounded by record count, lost records at shutdown, and retry loops that dominate server-child.log and desktop-main.log. In those two files, expected failures are logged as full stack traces: 26k "history recovery failed" warnings, 1.7k source-control stack traces, and up to 815 per minute rejected desktop:workspace-activate-transport IPC errors. On desktop, the Electron main thread writes all of these with synchronous appendFileSync calls.

Part of Priority 21: Background I/O: logs and traces

Expected gain

Default off removes 100% of provider-log disk I/O and its serialization (about 165 KiB/s / 580 MiB/h while 3 workflow threads run; 486 MiB/day observed on disk) and frees about 4 GB. A 512 MiB budget bounds worst-case disk use regardless of thread count (today about 12 GiB possible). gzip on rotated files: about 6-10x less on disk when enabled.

What happens today

ProviderEventLoggersLive always builds both the native and canonical loggers. NoOpProviderEventLoggers exists (64-67) but only tests use it. There is no setting or env flag (cli.ts only has RYCO_LOG_LEVEL and RYCO_TRACE_MIN_LEVEL). Retention is age-only (30 days, line 25), and the sweep runs once, at boot (ProviderEventLoggers.ts:81). The per-thread cap is 10 MiB x 3 files x 2 streams = 60 MiB per thread with no global cap, so the theoretical ceiling is threads-active-in-30-days x 60 MiB (209 x 60 MiB = 12.2 GiB here). Measured: 4,185 MiB in 689 files, 0 files older than 30 days (the sweep reclaims nothing), 486 MiB still on disk from the last 24 h, and about 165 KiB/s (about 580 MiB/h) combined write rate while 3 workflow threads ran. Nothing in the app reads these files: Diagnostics tails config.providerEventLogPath = provider/events.log (Diagnostics.ts:746-750, config.ts:343), but the logger only creates <threadId>[.native].log. That diagnostic source is therefore always empty, which is also a bug. logs/terminals has no retention at all (files from May 17-20). Reliability risk: disk exhaustion on long-running hosts or Hub nodes, plus SSD wear.

Proposal

Add providerEventLogs: 'off' | 'lifecycle' | 'full' to ServerSettings (diagnostics section) and an env override RYCO_PROVIDER_EVENT_LOGS. Default to 'off' (or 'lifecycle': turn/session/error events only, no deltas or progress) in packaged builds and 'full' in dev. When off, ProviderEventLoggersLive returns NoOpProviderEventLoggers, so the zero-cost path already exists. Hot-toggle through the existing settings stream. Extend sweepStaleEventLogs into a budget sweep: collect (mtime, size), delete oldest-first until the directory is under a byte budget (e.g. 512 MiB), run it on boot and every hour with Effect.repeat(Schedule.spaced), and apply the same policy to logs/terminals. Optionally gzip rotated .N files in the threadpool (measured 5.8-10x smaller, 30-50 ms per 10 MiB). Fix Diagnostics to tail the newest per-thread files, or remove that source.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Code checked. ProviderEventLoggersLive (ProviderEventLoggers.ts:74-93) always builds both loggers and is wired unconditionally at server.ts:443. NoOpProviderEventLoggers is referenced only in tests. No setting or env flag exists (cli.ts:307-330). The sweep is age-only (EventNdjsonLogger.ts:25) and is forked once at boot (ProviderEventLoggers.ts:81). Disk state confirmed: logs/provider holds 4,180 MiB in 689 files across 209 thread ids, 0 files older than 30 days, and 477 MiB modified in the last 24 h. events.log does not exist. Diagnostics.ts:746-750 tails config.providerEventLogPath, and readFailureLogTail (Diagnostics.ts:615-633) silently returns [] on ENOENT, so this source is always empty. The investigator missed that the same is true of the other failure source: Diagnostics.ts:740-744 tails config.serverLogPath (logs/server.log, config.ts:340), which nothing writes (grep finds only config.ts and Diagnostics.ts; desktop writes server-child.log). The Diagnostics failure list is therefore always empty. logs/terminals: 109 files / 52 MB, oldest May 17, with no retention code (only Manager.ts:914-918 uses the dir). The 580 MiB/h figure is a workflow-burst rate. On default 'off': 'lifecycle' is the safer packaged default for supportability.

Prior work

Partial. Commit 6e23b8afc (#508) added the 30-day age sweep and per-thread rotation depth 3. The Aug report says 'Provider event logs ... use asynchronous rotating writers with byte limits', but the limits are per file and per thread, not a total budget. New here: no opt-out, no size budget, sweep only at boot, terminals dir unbounded, and the Diagnostics path mismatch.

Part of Priority 21: Background I/O: logs and traces

Expected gain

Canonical bytes -94% to -96% (measured: stripped size is 4.0-5.8% of current); on the busiest thread about 112 KiB/s becomes about 6 KiB/s, roughly 380 MiB/h less disk writing across the 3 observed workflow threads; canonical format CPU 127-203 us becomes 6-7 us per event (about 0.9 ms/s less main thread per busy workflow thread); canonical retention grows from about 5 min to about 1.5 h at the same 30 MiB cap

What happens today

Every Claude runtime event built from an SDK message gets raw: { source, method, messageType, payload: message }. This is the shared base at ClaudeAdapter.ts:3921-3933, used for every member event in emitWorkflowMemberProgress (3851-3856) and for subagent.updated (2055-2060). A single task_progress therefore becomes 1 coordinator task.progress, plus one task.progress per changed workflow member, plus one subagent.updated (4363-4384). Each carries the same full message, including the cumulative workflow_progress array of up to about 64-78 KB. ProviderService.publishRuntimeEvent then stringifies every one into the canonical log (629-633) before publishing. Measured on the user's live threads in overlapping windows: canonical 111.9 KiB/s vs native 10.1 KiB/s (40.3 MB vs 3.6 MB in 352 s); raw.payload = 92.5% / 87.2% / 94.7% of canonical bytes; 2.42-2.56 canonical lines per native message, worst 16 lines / 1.26 MB for one message. Each such raw message is also present in the native log. The only runtime consumer of raw.payload is ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:324 (raw.payload.threadId, a Codex-shape field). SQLite stored 3.70 MB of activity payload for the same thread and window, so the non-raw part of canonical (the payload) also duplicates the event store. Because of this volume, the 10 MiB x 3 rotation keeps only about 5 minutes of canonical history on that thread, so the log no longer serves its debugging purpose. CPU: 127-203 us/event to format, vs 6-7 us with raw stripped.

Proposal

(1) In EventNdjsonLogger, add a stream-specific serializer for 'canonical'. Use a JSON.stringify replacer, or build the record explicitly, that writes raw as {source, method, messageType, nativeId: raw.payload?.uuid ?? raw.payload?.id} and drops raw.payload. The native log already has the full message, so it can still be found by id. (2) Better, fix it at the source: stop attaching raw.payload to derived fan-out events (emitWorkflowMemberProgress, emitClaudeSubagentUpdated/Started, the coordinator task.progress), or attach it only to the first event per SDK message. Move the single consumer (ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:324) to a typed field. (3) Consider making raw a non-enumerable or WeakMap side-channel so it never reaches serializers or PubSub consumers by accident. Add a guard test asserting the canonical line size stays under a few KB for task.progress.

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

Code checked. ClaudeAdapter.ts:3921-3933 builds base with raw.payload = the full SDK message. The same raw is attached at 3853 (each changed workflow member), 2055 (subagent.updated), and through ...base on the coordinator task.progress and thread.token-usage.updated (4321-4390). ProviderService.ts:629-633 writes the canonical log before PubSub.publish. The only runtime reader of raw.payload is ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:323-325 (grep across server, web, client-runtime and shared found no other). I verified the duplication directly: on the live 58db canonical .log, all 2,044 raw.payload uuids match a native record with a byte-identical payload (.perf-research/verifier-logging-io/pair2.mjs). The headline numbers are burst numbers, though. The 11x canonical/native ratio and the 87-95% raw share come from workflow-progress windows. The current 58db .log is 79.5% raw at 1.19 lines per native message, and canonical now covers 14 min instead of 5. Across all 767 MiB of current canonical files (209 threads), raw.payload is 42.7% of bytes (Claude 54.3%, Codex 37.1%; rawshare.mjs). On disk overall, native and canonical are close: 1,992 vs 2,194 MiB. So the realistic saving is about -43% of canonical bytes on a typical thread and -90% or more in workflow bursts, not a flat -95%. The 127 us 'format' figure includes the 36 us redact step, which runs in the adapter, not the logger. CPU savings are well under 1 ms/s. The real benefits are disk volume and longer log retention. The fix is still correct, S effort and low risk.

Prior work

none. The Sep 3 commit 6e23b8afc (#508) split native and canonical files and reduced rotation depth from 10 to 3, but did not touch payload duplication. workflowMemberFingerprints (ClaudeAdapter.ts:437-444) reduced member fan-out, but each emitted member event still copies the full raw message.

In an earlier rotation, input_json_delta alone was 7,352 events = 49.5% of native bytes (thinking_delta another 9.8%, thinking_tokens 7.4%). Codex thread 421bac44: agentMessage/delta 4,965 events = 29.1% and reasoning/summaryTextDelta 12.0% of native bytes. The complete content is logged again by the final Claude assistant message and by Codex item/completed.

Proposal

In the native logger path, coalesce deltas per (turnId, content index or itemId). Accumulate them in memory and emit one record when the block closes (content_block_stop, message_stop, item/completed) or at the 200 ms flush, with {kind: 'delta-run', count, firstAt, lastAt, bytes}. Include the concatenated text only in 'full' mode. Also drop redundant envelope fields (createdAt == observedAt, id == payload.uuid, providerThreadId == session_id) and do not log thinking_tokens or ping.

Verifier (Confirmed)

Every SDK message, stream_event deltas included, is logged by handleSdkMessage, which calls logNativeSdkMessage at ClaudeAdapter.ts:4862 (function at 2104-2140). Codex logs every event through writeNativeEvent (CodexAdapter.ts:2061, 2748-2753). Verified on the live 58db native.log: 4,125 of 6,028 lines (68%) are content_block_delta. A sampled input_json_delta line is about 650 B with partial_json "", carrying the duplicated id/uuid, createdAt/observedAt and providerThreadId/session_id. The investigator's analysis shows deltas at 40-60% of native bytes (Claude input_json 49.5% plus thinking 9.8%; Codex 29.1% + 12.0%). Not covered by the proposal: the canonical stream also writes one content.delta per delta, each carrying raw (Codex canonical: 1,046 agentMessage deltas = 12.2% of the file). The coalescer should apply to both streams. This becomes moot if logging defaults to off or 'lifecycle'.

Part of Priority 21: Background I/O: logs and traces

Expected gain

About 85-90% less server-child.log volume (measured composition: 46% + 37% + 10%); removes up to about 13 IPC error stacks/s, each costing 3 sync writes (about 96 us) on Electron main during relay-activation failure storms

What happens today

server-child.log.1 (10.48 MB, Sep 27 to Oct 10): 1,735 INFO SourceControlProviderError 'detectProvider' stack traces = 4.84 MB (46%, about 2.8 KB each), from Effect.ignoreCause({ log: true }) around refreshWorktreeSourceControlState (ws/context.ts:363, 369, 388, 392) for worktrees with no known remote provider, an expected condition. 26,049 'Provider history recovery failed' WARNs = 3.88 MB (37%; see history-recovery-poll-storm). 516 'VCS remote status refresh failed' = 1.06 MB. desktop-main.log: rejected desktop:workspace-activate-transport IPC invocations (main.ts:3254-3256, invoked by desktopWorkspaceSocket.ts:77) were logged by Electron as 'Error occurred in handler' with 4-line stacks: 22,075 on Sep 5 at up to 815/min, plus 5,823 more through Oct 10. The renderer re-creates the socket on each failure without visible backoff. The server logs with Logger.consolePretty at Info (serverLogger.ts:8; RYCO_LOG_LEVEL default Info, cli.ts:308). Each such line is formatted with pretty-print, piped to Electron, and written there with synchronous appendFileSync.

Proposal

Add a shared logOnceEvery(key, window) / dedupe helper to the server and desktop logging (first occurrence with full cause, then a periodic '(repeated N times in 5m)' summary). Classify 'unknown source control provider' as an expected outcome: return Option.none and log at Debug instead of ignoreCause({log:true}). Make the activate-transport IPC return a typed {ok:false, reason} instead of throwing (Electron prints every rejected invoke to stderr). Add exponential backoff in the desktop workspace socket reconnect path. Consider Logger.consoleLogFmt or JSON in packaged mode (cheaper than pretty-print and greppable).

Verifier (Partially confirmed)

Counts verified: server-child.log.1 has 26,049 history-recovery WARNs (27,476 in .2), 2,199 SourceControlProviderError mentions and 516 'VCS remote status refresh failed'. desktop-main.log.1 and .2 each have 22,075 activate-transport lines (peak about 830/min on Sep 5); the current file has 5,823. ignoreCause({log:true}) is at ws/context.ts:363, 369, 388 and 392. main.ts:3254-3256 and desktopWorkspaceSocket.ts:74-80 match. The cause is mischaracterized. All 1,735 SourceControlProviderError stacks have the cause chain VcsProcessSpawnError, then PlatformError NotFound from FileSystem.access, then ENOENT on deleted worktree directories (e.g. 257× ryco-87dc6d1c__cihaw). They are not 'no known remote provider'. Just lowering the log level would hide a stale-state bug (see additional finding stale-missing-checkouts-reprobed). The claim that the renderer has no backoff was not verified (the reconnect path in client-runtime was not traced). Average server-child.log volume is low (about 0.8 MB/day), so the CPU benefit is limited to failure storms. This is mainly log hygiene and reliability.
